top_reviews.content:
The matcha latte had a delicate, smooth flavor — creamy, gentle, and perfectly balanced.
The ichigo daifuku was simply delightful: soft, chewy mochi wrapped around a juicy fresh strawberry, with a subtle sweetness that complemented the fruit beautifully.
A lovely combination!

Stopped by to grab a drink and was pleasantly surprised. The milk tea was really good, and the drinks came out fairly quickly. I ordered a matcha milk tea with boba, and the flavors were nicely balanced. The matcha wasn’t too bitter, and the boba had a great chewy texture.
I also picked up a croissant, and it was surprisingly good. Light, flaky, and a nice little treat to go with the drink. It was an easy and enjoyable stop, and I’d definitely come back to try more items on the menu next time.

This tea house is supported by the sale of bubble tea and other tea-family sweet drinks served in plastic disposable cups and straws. The space is cool, but the vibe is ruined by poorly amp'd junk music that is more sound graffiti than music. They would be better off with ambient sounds or no music at all. But invest is speakers first.

I know a thing or two about tea, so I wanted to enjoy some properly brewed Chinese tea while in Downtown Berkeley.  I opted for Da Hong Pao (Great Red Robe), a generally wonderful tea from Fujian. I watched the staff brew it in a small pot; after steeping,  they served it to me in 8 oz ceramic cup. Serving chinese tea to westerners in a way that works in  can be hard. I prefer gongfu places where I can brew myself and get multiple steeps.  Or places devoted only to tea and not tea infused drinks. That said, it wasn't a bad brew. But one doesn't get to linger over the tea, or enjoy the other aspects associated with traditional tea culture here.

I won't come back unless it's empty, the music is off, or something else changes.

If you want a fruit, milk or bubble tea, I would recommend. Head to Blue Willow, Far Leaves, or Teance if you want to drink actual tea.  They could certainly do it here, but they can't do both starbucks-style tea and fine tea at the same time. It's a shame.

Great teas!
Yummy matcha soft serve!
Compostable cups and straws!
Oh my.
And the boba was perfectly cooked (not heavily sugared like most boba places).
We also got daifaiku which they sell from another vendor.
I love that the tea quality wasn’t secondary like many shops.
Staff were friendly too.

I highly recommend this place.

Nice tea house at Berkeley.  They have another location at SF. We stopped by after lunch. Looks like it is a good place to study or work as I see many customers working on the laptop.
I heard this tea house is pretty famous. it has nice interior and high ceiling. They also have one popup store inside when we visit.
There are plenty of teas  and match varieties. They also sell the match powder, tea leaf and Hojicha powder . They also have imperial Matcha powder.  We ordered just cold matcha and it was good.  it was not that strong.  We will stop by next time to try other tea.

It’s a super cute matcha cafe. They sell matcha here and other teas. Service was fast and they were all very helpful.

We stopped here after a recommendation. I love a creamy, umami, nutty, and minimally bitter or astringent matcha. My friend and I both got the plain matcha latte, and we were floored. It was so delicious!! Both one of our favorite matchas ever! I live in Seattle but will come back on my next trip!

Used to be good, the quality is worse and more expensive now. I work nearby and so I have come here often over a long period of time. I used to feel it was worth it paying more than other shops to have quality. But then they started to upcharge everything, even for getting no ice 😂 and they put less matcha every time. This last time it was almost pure milk, so I asked for an extra shot. This is how the color is with a double shot of matcha. So I will sadly drink my last cup of milk from Asha , hopefully they’ll change.
One of the baristas has yet to make my drink to my specifications, so it’s super inconsistent. This is a photo of when I asked for a double shot (after the double shot was poured in). Basically milk
One of the best matcha spots in the city! The matcha is always smooth and high quality, and the boba is delicious with the perfect texture. Definitely one of my favorite places to grab a drink.

I really thought this place was cute, and their menu was amazing with so many delicious options. But when I got my drink, the matcha wasn't very strong, there was a lot of ice (I got light ice), and the Asian pear I got in it was chunky and not very flavorful. The size was also pretty small, and this whole drink cost $8.15!! I also asked for it 'for here,' but it came in the same cup as the 'to-go' cups. Overall, it wasn't that good and I would likely not come again. Maybe their other drinks are better though!

The milk tea was really delicious! The flavor was rich and creamy, but not too sweet, which I really liked. Stopped by ChaHalo and was genuinely impressed. The shop is beautifully designed, and the attention to detail shows from the decor to the packaging. The staff were friendly and worked quickly despite a steady flow of customers. It’s great to see a new tea spot.

top_reviews.content:
BW is the friendliest, loveliest place to sit and enjoy a tasty drink in Berkeley. Their tea is so consistently delicious and the staff is so knowledgeable and welcoming. Everyone who works here has been so warm and generous in creating a space that truly feels like a community hub that brings the best of all the colorful sides of life that the bay has to offer. I’ve spent hours talking with strangers at the bar about art and poetry and life, and I’ve spent hours reading and writing in peaceful solitude. Blue willow is truly an escape from the stress of daily life.

Their wide range of teas is a testament to the very intentional curation and selection of really special cakes and leaves from around the world. Their in house blends and herbal options are also a treat. But nothing beats their hojicha latte on a cloudy day.

The acupressure + tea tasting I did there in the fall was one of the sweetest little moments of last year. Pairing a grounding puerh with a lesson on acupressure points related to the lungs and grief, giving me a chance to tune into my body and mind in a safe, educating space.

I’m so grateful that such a beautiful place like this exists and is thriving so well, community spaces like this are what allow us to share our lives and selves, and spaces like this are what makes Berkeley and the east bay feel like home.

Thanks BW for offering a sense of place, and a beautiful space to inspire creativity and community.

Superb Japanese tea house experience in the heart of Berkeley with caring people and clean, artfully decorated premises. Just learned about this establishment today due to recommendation from Artis Coffee (top notch roastery) and hit the mother lode. Aly, the exceptionally kind and engaged owner took care of us personally while Niko served the beverages with authentic courtesy and care. The establishment is bright and airy, with several intimate spaces creatively designed for Zen like relaxation which encourages one to linger. I’ve never observed a broader selection of quality teas, however, Aly and Niko helped us efficiently navigate choices to match our taste profile. You can even order a flight to sample several teas and from there decide what to purchase for taking home (Blood Orange super tasty). In addition to tea, Blue Willow offers high quality pastries and Japanese cookies as well as tea preparation and serving ware. Happened to hit their 9 year anniversary which elevated the experience. This establishment which exudes pride of ownership throughout fit us to a ‘tea’ and we can’t wait to return. Bravo Aly!

This was such a fun find in Berkeley! We came after wanting to try something different that didn't involve alcohol and tea sounded perfect.

Good:
- The private room was really good! We got out own private spot for about an hour and thirty minutes
- The service was great - we had our own tea steeper and had enough tea for the entire time
- Loved the duck s*** tea and the dragon tea and puerh tea, super tasty and we even tried mixing it a lot
- The place is so cute! Very relaxing

Bad:
- Gets super busy, so make a reservation ahead of time!

Overall, really enjoyed having the time to sit and relax and be present with me and my boyfriend!

This is my new favorite teahouse. You know it's legit when there's a bookshelf, awesome music, friendly staff and great lighting. The Sakura mochi was amazing and we shared a pot of shou that tealuminated us in all the right ways. Great prices, great packaging, a one of a kind vibe. I'll most definitely be coming back to explore more varieties of tea. Black Phoenix on Ice this Summer sounds like just the thing!

The tea and atmosphere were great, and the place is beautiful. However, we didn’t feel welcomed. We were taking a few photos because we loved the decor, but one staff member kept following us and asking what we were photographing, which made us uncomfortable. Later, my brother accidentally closed the communal room door, and she immediately came in to tell us to keep it open. She also warned us not to touch the decorations, even though we hadn’t touched anything. Unfortunately, the experience was disappointing because we felt like we were being watched instead of welcomed.

Stopped by after touring UC Berkeley. A little pricey. 4 drinks and 2 orders of the egg pancake was $44. There are 2 self order kiosks. We were the only ones there so everything was done in 5-7 minutes.  The menu states the egg pancakes can be 10-15 minutes.  Drinks were good. Boba was still warm. It is nice and chewy. There is no seating but you can go across the street and find a place outside to sit on campus.

This is the best boba place ive even been to. They are well known for the fruit teas but personally i love their brown sugar milk tea. The boba is also very chewy. If you love sugarcane, they have sugarcane milk for u to try. Also try their wintermelon drink

I definitely need to go back and give it another go.

5/11/2026*
When I ordered online, the estimated wait time was 10 min, but I ended up waiting another 40 min in the store, and my drink still wasn't ready. I finally checked in with the staff, and that's when they realized they had never started making my drinks. This is actually my second time experiencing this issue. On a separate occasion, I also asked a staff member for a bag, and she just placed it on the counter and threw the straws onto the counter as well.

4/27/2026
I went there to get my usual order, the Triple Supreme Matcha, and everything tasted perfect with great matcha flavors!

9/24/25
I feel that Heytea's quality is really consistent, even though its price are a bit higher than other boba shops.

This time I tried their Coconut Matcha Bbo, which has cloud, macha, coconut milk and boba. It tasted great, the flavor was on point. I ordered on their app, which makes it easy to customize your drink. Highly recommended!

The triple supreme matcha is a disaster, taste like a smell fish. 2 people shared it and we only could finish half of it.

Service is also very slow, no one respond to my question while they talking loudly.

A friend recommended this place, & I came to try many times.  I think these 4 are the ok drinks here: the supreme bobo milk tea (for 1st time, after that it becomes boring, too creamy & to sweet), the cold  jasmine milk tea (very strong), coconut mango boom ( which my son likes), & recently the pistachio cloud king jasmine (light/less sugar adjustment).
I like the way they provide the paper bag, it looks fancy. The shop is small & clean.

Downside: take really long time to get the drink, all their milk teas taste the same flavour as the supreme bobo milk tea. Nothing different when adding bobo into the drink.  I guess they using too much brown sugar, that’s why it becomes too sweet when adding bobo into the drink.
I don’t recommend to add bobo into the black milk tea with less sugar. It tastes sooo sweet.  I bought my drink at 13:25 & just drink 2 sips to taste, & the drink still full at 10:41pm.  This is the first time I’ve ever been able to drink a milk teas.
Second one is the triple supreme matcha latte, it tastes bitter & blind, we had to throw it away.

I have had Heytea before, trying the Triple Matcha and the Mulberry Boom.

🍵 Triple Matcha: I think my favorite was the triple matcha with the combination of Jasmine and matcha giving a very strong green tea flavor along with the matcha heavy cream.

☕ Yingde Mochi Milk Tea: This time I tried their Yingde mochi milktea which was very unique. I had tried mochi milk tea before but the last time I had it, it was a choking hazard. This time however, it was a perfect consistency where it wasn't too tough to cause clumps in the bottom, but still soft enough to be sucked up through the straw. The tea also had a really nice toasty black tea flavor and I really enjoyed the complexity of this drink. It was also fun to open up the drink and scoop up the “mochi” off the bottom. I just wished I could see the pretty layers of this drink in a clear cup. I hope I can order this again next time!

name: TP TEA – Berkeley
address: 2383 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley, CA 94704, United States

top_reviews.content:
Cute little boba shop tucked away in Berkeley, in the Telegraph district, close to several popular food joints. Parking is super convenient with several reasonably priced garages and plenty of cheap street parking. This place has a small seating area with a few tables and pickup options available. Ordering is efficient through a kiosk and fulfilled quickly.

We ordered a matcha yuzu tea, a strawberry pudding with boba, a taro tea and a signature black tea with boba. All were excellent. They allowed for customizing the ice and sugar levels for all drinks. My favorites were the matcha yuzu and the signature black tea. The matcha yuzu was light, extremely fresh and citrusy. The black tea was strong and very high quality. The strawberry one was on the sweeter side so opting for a lower sugar level is a good idea. The taro one had an overpowering taro flavor.

All in all, highly recommend this for a post meal dessert if you're in the area!

I’m a huge fan of this place because their drinks especially the milk tea are spot on. But beyond the flavors, the service here is truly top-notch. There’s a young guy (who looks Chinese) who is always smiling and even remembers my usual order. Also, the woman who can speak Thai is absolutely wonderful. Both of them go above and beyond, and whenever there’s a hiccup with an order, they handle it so helpfully and with a great attitude. Even the manager is amazing. I once had an issue with an order and called the store, and the manager handled it personally. He didn't let the problem slide and was super enthusiastic about making things right. The customer service here is truly next-level. The owner is honestly so lucky to have such an amazing team!!

This was one of the BEST Boba drinks I have ever had. I tried the lychee rose ice slushy with boba added and no extra sugar. The flavour was delicate, the blended ice made it refreshing and subtle sweetness from lychee fruit balanced it out! I am definitely coming back and sharing with friends.

Haven’t been to this TP Tea location in years! Used to come here weekly while I was in school. I’m glad to see that they are still doing well and in the same spot.

When you enter, there are 3-4 different self order stations which is great because there was no wait/line! If you prefer ordering from a real person, it’s a bit hard to get their attention but if you’re lucky and can waive someone over they’re happy to help.

I ordered the Boba Fresh Milk Tornado with 50% sweetness for $6.25. I was really craving a matcha tornado but they only had the fresh milk and Thai tea tornados.

Considering that it was only boba pearls, tornado (custard/cream), milk, and ice it was actually very good. Super refreshing, the custard went very well with the milk and perfectly cooked boba pearls. The pearls were bouncy and didn’t stick to your teeth, they were also not over saturated in sugar either.

I do have to say that the store itself was uncomfortably hot and humid. I’m not sure what was going on with the ventilation. They even had one of the front doors propped open and it felt like a completely different climate inside the store. Hopefully that gets fixed soon.

Ordered two boba milk teas from TPT and they were both great.

The tea had strong flavor, not overly sweet (0% and 30% sweet) and the boba was fresh with the right chew. Drinks were made quickly and the staff was friendly. Clean shop with a simple vibe—no frills, just solid milk tea.

Definitely a spot I’d come back to when I’m craving boba. No rest room here so that needs to change soon. Don’t
Worry about parking near the store as it’s impossible to find parking. You are better off parking at the nearby parking garage.

top_reviews.content: Make your reservations TODAY! I absolutely LOVE LOVE LOVE Malaya Tea Room! I have been countless times and have recommended it to so many different people and everyone has LOVED it and raved about it once they go or once I’ve taken them! The whole experience is amazing, delicious variety of teas to choose from: black teas, green teas, Asian teas, no caffeine herbal teas. There is also a large variety of traditional European sandwiches to choose from as well as delicious Malaysian/asian flavored sandwiches! During December they have a special fixed holiday menu that’s also different than usual. They also change the desserts selections frequently so it’s always a different experience every time you go. The service is always impeccable and kind. Atmosphere and decor is beautiful and comfortable, like a favorite auntie’s warm and inviting home who loves to feed you! Visit this place to treat yourself (I’ve gone solo and they have tea for one!), or book for a special event or your besties birthday. They have 3 seatings a day on their open days which are Thursday - Sunday. The times are 11 am, 1 pm, and 3 pm. They very often get booked out and full, so plan ahead and make your reservations!
Low key location. Menu items on par with Nieman Marcus' tea service. Distinct Malaysian flavors in both beverage and food offerings. Good but not excellent service.

**credentials: Teahead with a good amount of tea experience in the US, BC, and UK; recently relocated to the Bay and on the hunt for the best tea service locally.**

Kicking off the series here with Malaya, a tribute to British Malayan culture; an unconventional but intriguing pick.

Ambiance: Tea for two on a rainy Saturday afternoon. 1:15 p.m. time slot; full house, too packed for an audible conversation. I’d recommend booking the proper 3 p.m. slot.

Our table was directly in front of the open entrance, so expect some wind and chills.

Tea: Refillable water, non-refillable tea. The Apple Cider lacked apple flavor. The Genmaicha with Coconut was pleasant but weak; I had to ask for a double bag.

Eats: The Southeast Asian–style sardine sandwich was well-seasoned and balanced with cucumbers, absolutely phenomenal!

The Chicken Apple came on brown bread with generous apple chunks.

The Turkey and Smoked Salmon sandwiches were mediocre.

The scone was on the dry side, but the clotted cream was proper. Unsure if the jam was homemade or commercial. Fruits were fresh and sweet. The pandan cake was a nice twist, subtle enough for those unfamiliar with the flavor.

Service: The servers were very polite and kind, with some training in tea knowledge. They kept interactions minimal to avoid disruption. Ring the bell for service.

Amenities: The room was clean and well kept, with a spacious restroom in the back. Non-formal china. Low coffee table. Chairs and tiered stands can be wobbly.

Accessibility: The entrance is ADA-compliant, though the packed seating can pose challenges for wheelchair access. I’d recommend noting your needs during booking to ensure the best seating.

Overall: A cozy neighborhood spot for those seeking a casual outing. A lot of thought and emphasis have been put into showcasing the owner’s Southeast Asian heritage, and I’d highly recommend exploring that when ordering.

Very cute Malaysian tea room. Food was ok but not really high tea quality. You'll fill up on white bread and hot water. Unfortunately the tiered platter was too big and prevented my friend and I from being able to see each other very well. We had to peek through the gap in the plates. Apart from that, it was a pleasant experience overall.

This was a nice experience! I loved the selection of  food and tea available, and the service was top-notch. It's a great place to go if you've never experienced a tea hour before and it's not too expensive like other places. Very kid friendly, but I do recommend 7 and up as it is a very small and quiet shop. Each person gets their own individual tea pot! (PICTURED: Sandwich flavors- Curry Chicken, Cucumber, Turkey and Fig, Smoked Salmon. Tea- Butterfly Pea Flower)

reviews_snippets.content: "Also, I expected a lot more sandwiches and quality food for a 125$ check."

top_reviews.content: Good place for tea purists. Everything is minimally sweetened which I appreciate. Matcha strawberry latte was well done. My oolong macadamia latte was a Greta idea but perhaps not ideally executed - tasted a bit astringent.

A beautiful and tranquil tea house, perfect for slowing down and enjoying a cup of tea. The atmosphere feels calm and refreshing, with plenty of space that makes it easy to relax and unwind. The environment is both spacious and inviting, filled with a quiet charm that makes you want to linger longer. A lovely spot for conversation, reflection, or simply enjoying the moment with a warm cup in hand.

Not sure if I came at a bad time but their matcha was not the best. I have lots of matcha in my hometown and I worked at boba tea shops before so I had my fair share of matcha. We got three different matcha drinks and their texture and flavor profiles all were different. Either watery, grainy, or too milky. The boba was okay as well. It had that harder center texture. Be sure to ask about the size too because we didn't know they would come in a different size. The staff is really sweet and was helpful. I just wish the drinks were better, especially for the higher price point!

top_reviews.content:
What a fantastic experience! Dartealing’s High Tea was truly the best I’ve ever had. The seasonal menu was beautifully curated, with every item fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. The house special Baja fish sandwich was outstanding and absolutely worth the additional $9.

The service was equally impressive. My server, Keith, was attentive, friendly, and helped make the afternoon even more enjoyable. I highly recommend Dartealing to anyone looking for an exceptional tea experience, and I’m already looking forward to my next visit!

Darteeling has absolutely ruined me--I don't think I'll be able to enjoy another tea lounge for a good while. I've been to Rundle Bar in Banff, Courtyard in Boston, Majorelle in NY, and a few other places in DC and as wonderful as those locations were, I always left feeling the savory sandwiches were underwhelming or not really savory/bland and sweets were too sweet with flavor profiles that seemed too unique for my taste.

Dartealing's savory bites this season were balanced, familiar but elevated, had great contrasting textures and genuinely delicious. The sweets were also not too sweet, which I appreciated because I finished my entire portion before my husband finished his (this never happens). I also felt the preset menu was very intentional in how it was composed and loved how there was no silverware (don't know if this was intentional) because that typically takes up so much space on the table.

It was also super cozy inside and felt homey which is my preference. I felt like I could just  sit and enjoy my tea time without worrying about anything else.

I don't live in SF, but would be willing to fly from the opposite coast to come here again!

I spotted Dartealing Lounge several times when riding by on a SF Muni bus going from Caltrain towards downtown. A lover of tea, I was happy to finally try it with a friend this past weekend.
The experience was good. 😊
Ambiance: the lounge is in an old (historic) building on 3rd Street in SOMA. The long room has a cozy feel with the cutest décor (decorative lamps, chintz curtains, a variety of seats and photos). It is spacious compared to another SF (Noe Valley) tea room I’d visited years ago - giving you some privacy.
Food: the Proper Tea service was what the two of us ordered. It is two pots of tea (separate flavors) in gorgeous heavy china teapots and a 3-tiered plated tower with a mix of savory and sweet creations. We happened to be at the lounge while the June menu was « Latin flavor ». My absolute favorite things were the tea sandwiches. The shop makes their own sauces and recipes for these. There were two corn (elote), two chicken salad and two cucumber sandwich triangles per person - basically we each ended up with 1.5 entire full-sized sandwiches on soft white and brown bread.
The acclaimed scone was just okay.
I found having my scone sliced already and a spot of clotted cream and a spot of lemon curd on it (rather than keeping it whole and the toppings in side cups) to be less pleasurable. The scones were small and slightly toasted - they ended up being dry :(
Cutting one small scone in half with a result of two pieces was dainty-looking but not substantial. The puréed black bean (with chunks of bean) empanada was yummy but underbaked and the chorizo roll in puff pastry was nice but there was very little chorizo.
Teas: I chose a black tea (Her Majesty’s Secret Service) and my friend chose a white, fruity tea (Cabana Boy). Both teas had light aromas and tastes. They went well with the food.
Service: Very pleasant. We were asked to wait in the entry lounge for 5 minutes until our official start time of 11:30am commenced. Then right on time, we were escorted to our table - a cute round set up in a corner. The wingback chair I sat in was plush and I sank in. The tea service was clearly explained to us and we placed our orders. We were asked how things were once and had the water in the teapot’s replenished.
Interesting fact: the lounge has been in business for 17 years. That’s some longevity!!!
Overall, Dartealing Lounge provides a nice tea service at a reasonable price. The other patrons (Moms with daughters, Grandmothers with grandkids or just groups of friends) were enjoying the experience. The 90 minutes for this reservation went by so quickly that we had to box some of the food to takeaway. I’m sure others were like me wishing we were given more time to relax.

OMG so much fun. The food was excellent, tea was delicious, and environment was beyond charming. I highly recommend trying this at least once. The flavors were an inventive, global version of high tea. DO make a reservation, they only offer the afternoon tea on weekends. Unless there is a game happening (though it explicitly says no game parking), the side street is good for parking.

P.s. If they have baja fish sandwich, say yes.

Me and my husband enjoyed the challenge, it was fun trying to escape together. But it just offended us how they don’t give a warning about what could be in the themes. The employee that helped us the whole time was great, she was nice and even gave us extra time.

Julian was our game master and they were really good.

Some things to keep in mind:
- the rules or guidelines should be spoken at a speed that everyone can comprehend. First timers or anyone who may not have English be their first language may have difficulty following.
- Asking us afterwards repeatedly if we had any questions was a bit much. It’s a closed-ended question. Instead maybe ask an open-ended like what we enjoyed or found difficult?

Great exhibits on 1/2/26...we really enjoyed the Oakland Museum of California. It was much more expansive and engaging than we expected and very well organized overall. Some sections are fuller than others, but nothing felt confusing or disjointed.

🏛️ Layout & Exhibits
The museum is divided into three main sections on three different levels: (1) California & Oakland history, (2) Science, and (3) Art.

The history exhibits were a highlight—walking through the decades made California and Oakland’s story feel much clearer and more connected. What stood out most is that everyone was genuinely engaged: the kids explored on their own (not just tagging along), and the adults were just as absorbed. It worked well for all of us at the same time.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Ages
Good for all ages, but younger kids will enjoy the science section the most. The history and art sections felt best suited for older kids (8+), which matched our experience. Walking through the decades of California/Oakland history helped everything click in a clear, connected way—great for homeschoolers or families who value contextual learning.

🎒 Bags, Food & Lockers
- No purses allowed, but jackets with pockets were fine
- No food or water bottles allowed inside
- Lockers available for belongings

♿ Accessibility
There are many stairs, but also ramps and elevators connecting all levels of the three museum sections. Wheelchairs are available. Security is present at entrances and throughout.

🚗 Parking (Important Notes)
There is an on-site parking garage, and you can pay inside or outside. Once you pay, you have about 15 minutes to exit.
⚠️ When the museum starts closing, everyone is pushed out at once, which caused a line to exit the garage—plan extra time.

⏰ Closing Time — Plan Ahead
Although it says they close at 5:00 PM, they begin closing everything around 4:45 PM. Bathrooms close, doors lock, and visitors are directed out. We didn’t even make it to the gift shop because we didn’t realize how firm this was.
‼️If anyone in your group needs the bathroom, go earlier—otherwise expect a long wait or to miss it entirely.

Overall: A really engaging, well-designed museum that works for meaningful family learning: kids and adults at the same time. Just plan your timing carefully near closing. Absolutely worth the visit.

Oakland Museum of California, Oakland

I’ve been here many times especially when my daughter was small, now I come here with my nieces and nephews. The museum displays changes often, so there’s always something new to see.

I usually love visiting the garden area especially on a beautiful sunny day! The garden area has been renovated so there’s many places to sit, relax and have a quick lunch when in the area.

The museum has three floors, so there’s plenty to see, so make sure you wear comfortable shoes! 👟

The bottom floor is the Nature Area, most kids love that area, to see and explore all the wild animals that roams in California. The “Welcome to Oakland” sign and “Oak tree” display is located on this floor. Awesome exhibit!

The second floor is where you pay for your admission, the gift shop is here, one of the main rooms changes to new event or exhibition. It’s also next to the entrance of Town Fare restaurant! Great food and great vibes! The other room is based on history of technology and revolutions. Old school car and television, the history of the Black Panther Party, the Chinese Excursion Act,  Angel Island, Paper brother and paper sister, the history of the great San Francisco fire and earthquake, the history of technology and so on. There’s even a small theater room too.

The top floor is mainly art and statues, many hidden rooms to explore.

We came on a weekday so that’s usually field trip days for kids, it wasn’t crowded either so we still got to see plenty of stuff.

I will always come back and visit! 💕

Our group from the NAACP Merced County Branch recently visited the Oakland Museum of California, and the experience was outstanding from start to finish.
We traveled in through the Amtrak Gold Runner partnership from Merced, and the museum staff were welcoming and accommodating to our intergenerational group, from elementary age students to seasoned community leaders. The exhibits were thoughtfully curated, engaging, and deeply reflective of California’s diverse history and cultural contributions. The storytelling throughout the galleries was powerful, interactive, and relevant.
We especially appreciated how the museum creates space for meaningful conversations around culture, identity, and community. It was not just a visit. It was an experience that sparked dialogue and connection long after we left.

Overall, an exceptional experience. We will absolutely be back, and we are already talking about the next trip.

With as populated as the Bay Area is, it can be more challenging than some might think to get a taste of nature without leaving the city. This takes me the Emeryville/Berkeley area where I had the opportunity in visiting "McLaughlin Eastshore State Park". There is no actual street address here but it is where University Ave. & W. Frontage Rd. meet. It is also about 1/2 mile from I-80 so it is quite easy to get to when traveling my car.

I had come here during the evening of Saturday 6/23/2022 at around 7:45pm. The weather was a comfortable 64°F while being crystal clear with no clouds in sight as well as no Bay Area fog for that matter. What makes this state park convenient is that they offer a sizable parking lot (which is free of charge) as well as several trash bins and a few porta potties within a mere 50 yards from the bay water and trails.

The hours of operation are from 5am to 10pm seven days a week. Since this is a protected open space preserve area, the park actually extends 8.5 miles along the East Bay shoreline from the Bay Bridge to Richmond, This includes tidelands along the waterfronts of Oakland, Emeryville, Berkeley, Albany, and Richmond. Since I-80 is a very heavily traveled highway, you can witness joggers, cyclists, and walkers exercising from a distance if you look close enough.

Since I arrive right before dusk to check out the sunset, I luckily parked a stones throw from the water, rocks, and sandy beach area. Since this area stretches a very long distance, it never seems super crowded as opposed to a way more densely popular park or bike trail. And if you arrive during the time I did, you can witness some of the most awesome sunsets in all of the Bay Area.

With the good things about this park, you also need to consider the not-so good things as well. On any given day, you will spot quite a few homeless people (in tents, sitting in cars, and even just sleeping on the streets). It is the grim reality of many that hit hard times. But for the most part, many people here are courteous and keep to themselves. I felt safe during my visit and was able to soak in some of that fresh bay air while enjoying a perfect sunset. With that said and done, I am going to give "McLaughlin Eastshore State Park" an above average four-star rating.

top_reviews.content: Indian rock is a quick little hike but a great place to sit, eat lunch and realize we live on the best side of the bay cause of our views and culture compared to other places in the bay. We are just so blessed and this rock gives you that feeling. So come check it out.

What a gem! Super cool area tucked into a residential area. We visited close to sunset on a Sunday and the top of the rock was speckled with small groups enjoying the view. And what a view! Perfect view of the SF skyline and the Bay and Golden Gate Bridges. There are steps carved most of the way up and down and lots of folks climbing and scrambling everywhere else. Great for all ages!

The view from the top is beautiful. You can see the bay and San Francisco city and also Golden Gate Bridge. However, I would like to call out a few things that might help folks make their decision as to whether to visit or not - especially if they’re driving from far.

1) This place is basically a large rock that one needs to climb. Once at the top, you get access to this beautiful view. The climb itself is barely 5-10 minutes. There are stairs to do so. If you truly want to “rock climb”, you can take the non-stairs route and climb from one of the other sides. But if you’re not a trained climber and you are going to take the stairs anyway, this is barely a 5-10 minute climb.

2) While the view is beautiful, getting to this place is basically driving for several miles on hilly roads with lots of stops/traffic lights through narrow streets. The distance from wherever you live might not be much but it’ll be a slow drive due to how much you’d have to stop just to get here.

3) There’s no designated parking here as such. This is a residential area and you will have to park on the street. Finding a parking spot itself took us 10-15 mins. It might take more if you come during busy hours. The lanes are VERY narrow and a pain to navigate in a car.

4) The view itself is nice but maybe something that you can sit and enjoy for no more than 15-20 mins perhaps.

Overall, if you live in the area and don’t have to drive a long way to visit this spot or deal with parking, I’d totally recommend this spot. However, if you’re driving from a distance and if you will need a parking spot, it may not be that productive a use of your time and energy.

Cafe Strada in Berkeley: Hot Chocolate That Didn't Live Up to the Hype

If you're searching for the cozy cafe to spend a weekend afternoon in Berkeley, Cafe Strada may come up on your radar — but don't get too excited about the hot chocolate. Despite all the hype, it didn’t quite deliver the rich, indulgent experience you might expect from a café with such a strong reputation. The chocolate was decent, but nothing extraordinary.

The café, though, is a bustling hub of activity, especially on weekends. Expect to find it packed with students and those just chilling with friends. A friend introduced me to this spot, and while the crowd may be overwhelming at times, the environment has a certain charm. It’s a lively place where you can soak in the energy of the city, but if you're looking for solitude, you might want to come during the quieter hours.

Hey friends! This review is about sustainability only.

I so appreciate your attention to detail when it comes to how folks here can use reusable mugs, and also limit their impact on the environment via plastic pollution.

The real silverware, the real glassware, the real mugs, the real spoon for the bowl of sugar, and the recycled napkins are an excellent touch!

That said, I was a bit disheartened to see how many people were enjoying their coffee to stay, but in to go cups. I understand that these to go cups might be compostable. But a quick glance into the recycling and trash bins shows that there is no delineation between the two. I wonder if there are ways that the barista can work clearly articulate the for-here option, by asking if people are staying to work or meet a friend.

I was also a bit disheartened to see the sale of plastic bottled water here. By 2050, there will be more plastic in the ocean than fish. And over 95% of the plastic that we try to recycle does not actually get recycled. But rather ends up in landfills, oceans, or burned in incinerators.

By now, there are tons of options for at least better water. Maybe aluminum canned?

Thank you for considering my feedback. All in all, I was impressed by your Sustainable offerings. Just would love to see some better communication to folks dining in, who would be able to skip the trash made entirely. Thanks again! Lovely courtyard too.

I received an email from Punch Line SF offering two free tickets and confirmed our attendance for Red Richardson on September 19. We hadn’t been to Punch Line in about a month and were looking forward to seeing the show.

I have a disability that requires strict dietary restrictions, and because of medication I had just taken, I could only drink basic tap water. After we were seated, I explained this to a staff member, who said he would notify our server.

When our server, Kat, came to the table, I again explained my situation and asked for tap water. She said she would bring it but that I would still be charged $7 for the Liquid Death water they provide. I explained that I specifically needed basic tap water and was dehydrated. She then told me that I was still required to purchase two drinks for myself and that my boyfriend had to purchase two drinks as well.

I explained that paying was not the issue. My boyfriend was happy to meet the two-drink minimum, but I was not going to pay for tap water that I medically needed. Kat laughed, told me I had to comply, and then said, “Let me get my manager so he can talk with you. I’m sure he will make you leave.”

This entire exchange happened while the MC was on stage, and it was loud enough that people around us were looking over.

The manager, Kim, asked me to step outside the venue so we could discuss the situation. I explained what happened and asked for Kat’s name, which Kim provided. Kim explained the two-drink policy and offered a reasonable accommodation: my boyfriend could purchase two food items and two drinks to satisfy the minimum, while I would not be charged for tap water. I accepted that solution. She also asked whether I was comfortable having Kat continue as our server. I said no, so she arranged for another server.

Unfortunately, when Kim returned inside and told Kat that she had lost our table, I could hear Kat laughing loudly and making racist comments about me. My boyfriend heard them as well. At that point, we decided we could no longer stay.

The replacement server came to take our order. I thanked her and explained why we were leaving. I also told Kim on our way out that we were leaving because of Kat’s behavior. There was no apology or apparent concern. Security also watched my movements as we left, which added to an already uncomfortable experience.

The issue was never about paying. It was about how I was treated when I disclosed a legitimate disability-related need. I understand that businesses have policies, and Kim did ultimately offer a workable accommodation. But the way Kat handled the situation—including laughing at me, refusing to identify herself, threatening that I might be removed, and the racist comments we heard afterward—completely ruined our evening.

The two-drink minimum is also a recurring complaint in the reviews, and I understand why. The prices are extremely high for food and beverages at a comedy club. Whether tickets are complimentary or purchased, requiring customers to spend substantial additional money to satisfy a drink minimum can make an already expensive evening even more costly.

I am an event manager and promoter and operate my own event business. I work with a large professional network, and many of my clients rent entire venues for their events. Because of this experience, I will not recommend Punch Line SF to my clients, use it for my own events, or choose it for my own entertainment.

Punch Line SF: do better.

I went to see the Lunchbox which is a set in Bombay India. The music was awesome and the acting was beautiful.  The talented voices rang out. I loved it. Not allowed to take pictures with my phone but I took one picture of the set which was also very creative with a moving stage. The underlying theme was about women and their role in the family.

Attended the All My Sons play at the Berkeley Rep. I'm so glad I did.
This was our first time the theater has great staff.
Took BART from the city a quick trip. Exited at Downtown Berkeley and walked to the Addison Street access.  It was a quick left and only steps to the Berkeley Rep.
Picked my tickets at will-call no problems.
The play was fantastic.

Berkeley Repertory Theater is a jewel in the East Bay and in America.   Berkeley Rep is recognized as one of the finest regional theaters in the country.  It puts on quality productions with the best creative teams and actors in the world.  You can see new productions of older and recent plays as well as brand new productions of plays that have never been presented before.  In some of these cases, the theater acts as an incubator for shows that will go on to Broadway and London and other venues.  It deserves your attendance and financial support.

Berkeley rep is an asset to the community. It’s such a wonderful experience. Both theaters are fairly small and yet they managed to get superb talent.

They have fostered new shows that end up going to Broadway.

They are minutes from the downtown Berkeley BART station.

They offer a wide variety of baked goods: bread, cookies, donuts, bagels, pies, cinnamon rolls, empanadas, sandwiches, cupcakes, cookies, cakes. They also offer frozen doughs and breads. I’d recommend asking the staff which items are vegan, as it can be a little confusing. Must try for anyone visiting Oakland. Hopefully they add more vegan options soon.

My GO-TO bakery.
For like EVERYTHING.
For 7 years straight.

My faves: the fruit/cheese danish, the cheese scone, the buttermilk biscuits, the cheesecake, I mean, my bday cake was from here.

Kinda pricey, ngl. But very worth it. If you are gluten-free & want tasty baked goods.

They also now have a stuffed bacon, egg and cheese bagel that’s amazing.

Follow me on IG: @freshdotdaily

3.5⭐️ Selection: insane, prices kinda high even for gf but not atypical..but doesn’t match the taste, which was only ok.

There must be over 60 different gf items in this bakery! Some are other packeged brands, most are theirs.

We tried a few things and they were ok good but nothing I need to return for. I’m a decent cook/baker so I know how good gf bakes can taste. I will say the vibe and setting is GREAT. Lovely spot with some seating indoors and out and an airy design.

The white bread🍞was pretty good but again, a pretty straight forward gf bread. The best selling cinnamon bun🥮wasn’t as moist as I’d expected given moist is one thing gf CAN do well. It was a bit cakey and the icing was too sweet. I realized it was just a sugar icing vs the classic and expected, WAY tastier cream cheese style icing. That was a big miss for me which could’ve made this scrummy, as Mary Barry would say😉

Of course prices as elevated for the gf part and most seem pretty on par with the market. Bigger things like full cakes and cobbler trays were overpriced I thought.

Check it out once. And if you’re easy to please (like most here giving a 5⭐️review) or celiacs and don’t bake or have kids, you’ll love this place!
I love this place where everything is gluten free! I buy fresh, hot food & get a bag of goodies to go home with! This location is so much easier to find & get to than their ferry building location!

I was craving a sweet treat and couldn’t resist the gluten-free cinnamon roll! It was so good—generously sized and perfect for sharing. The bakery offers a variety of gluten- and dairy-free options, which is rare in the East Bay. I’m happy that Mariposa Baking Company exists and has a great selection of dairy-free and gluten-free treats.
.

top_reviews.content:
Absolutely loved The Game Parlour — genuinely one of my favorite places we visited while in San Francisco.

As someone with celiac disease, finding places that are not only safe but also fun and genuinely exciting to eat at can be difficult, and this place absolutely delivered. Everything being gluten-free immediately made it feel more relaxing, but what really surprised me was just how many options they had. It was honestly hard to choose because so much of the menu sounded good.

There were two of us, and we ended up ordering three items to split because we wanted to try multiple things, but the portions were way more filling than we expected. The waffle sandwiches especially were substantial, and combined with fries and drinks, we were struggling to finish everything by the end — definitely not a complaint!

Beyond the food, the whole concept and atmosphere were just great. It’s part board game café, part restaurant, and it created such a fun, welcoming environment. They had board games, cards, games for purchase, and what appeared to be rentable/playable games as well. Even in the middle of the week around lunchtime, there was a nice mix of people there — some working remotely, some grabbing lunch, some hanging out and playing games. It really felt like a community space.

The owners/staff were also incredibly kind and patient while I asked a million questions trying to decide what to order because there were so many things I wanted to try. They were genuinely helpful and welcoming throughout the whole experience.

The space itself was comfortable too, with nice bathrooms and what appeared to be outdoor seating for warmer weather.

Overall, this is exactly the kind of business I love supporting: inclusive, social, community-oriented, and safe for people with dietary restrictions without making the experience feel limited or boring. I truly hope they continue to thrive because I would 1000% go back and already want to return next time I’m in San Francisco.

Spent a few hours here on our last day visiting San Fransisco. Was very busy and we felt lucky to get a table. Big selection of boardgames with welcoming staff keen to help with our decision making. Great coffee, chicken waffle sandwich was delicious, served quickly and came with the best fries we experienced in San Francisco. TGP was fairly noisy when we visited but that's to be expected as there were gaming events happinging at the same time. Great place that I dont hesitate to recommend.

This place is super awesome! It’s really a great combination of a lot of different things that I love. They have a lot of magic product to browse from and other TCG games. Also, they have a great catalog of games to play with your friends if you want to make this into an outing. The food there is also delicious and to the best of my knowledge It’s all gluten-free, which is great for me and I’m always gonna shout that out in a review so other gluten-free people can find it. Definitely recommend checking this place out.

Food was SO good! All gluten free- waffle sandwiches and crispy chicken dishes. It’s also a place to go play board games, so we happen to visit when there was a competition. We had an hour to eat, I wish we had longer but it was nice to see all these people gather together.

Perfect hangout place to chill and enjoy the company of your favorite people.

I only tried their build your own mochi waffle and it was pretty good. It was the original waffle with bananas, chocolate sauce, and chocolate scoop on top. It was pretty good combination.

The service is great too. The people there at the time were very friendly. It was a Thursday evening.

And the atmosphere is the best part. I really like it, plus the many board & card games you can play. It’s better to go in groups but two people can also have fun.

If you ask for the manager’s name to follow up, they tell you they “do not have the authority to disclose that information.” This is university bureaucracy at its finest - petty tyrants making terrible policies and then hiding from the public rather than actually making good decisions and being accountable. Dogs are allowed on leashes, and all the owners we encountered were friendly, with their dogs on their best behavior. There were also many cyclists along the road, and also along the trail.

Note to the wise: If you are going to walk in the tall grass, there -are- ticks. I have been on many walks and hikes that say there are ticks....and there aren't many. This. Trail. Has. Ticks. In the long grass. I had two for a short 5 minute off the pavement walk.

On Saturday, June 20, 2026, I ate at U :Dessert Story for my birthday.

We went there a little bit after 5 pm. The place wasn't busy at all. There were a few people eating there.

Here's what we ordered. The Salted Egg Yolk Brick Toast, Chocolate Volcano Bingsu 🌋 and Mango Stick Rice Bingsu. The Salted Egg Yolk Brick Toast was hands down one of the best desserts I've ever eaten. The orange Egg custard sauce was delicious and the Brick Toast was warm and soft. The vanilla bean ice cream on top was the perfect addition to this dessert. Hands down the best dessert out of the 3 we ordered and definitely a 5 out of a 5! The Chocolate Volcano Bingsu was good. It wasn't knock your socks off good like the Salted Egg Yolk Brick Toast but good overall. The chocolate flavor was lacking in my opinion. I wanted it to taste more like chocolate and have more of a chocolate pronounced flavor but it didn't. The chocolate flavor was mild at best. There were bananas, cocoa krispies, corn flakes and brownie chunks throughout the chocolate volvcano. I can see why a lot of people order this dessert because the presentation is cool. It's pretty big and it comes out with a dry ice cube on top that makes it look smoky and foggy to simulate a volcano that just erupted. Cool concept. The mango sticky rice Bingsu was my least favorite. The mango chunks weren't ripe and were hard. They didn't taste good or have good flavor. The sticky rice which was green tasted okay but not so great. The condensed milk on the side was super sweet and made the dessert taste somewhat better. But overall the mango sticky rice Bingsu was a failure. I don't recommend ordering this dessert.

Even though the mango sticky rice Bingsu wasn't good, I would still come back and try more desserts. I would try another Brick Toast and some other chocolate desserts that sounded good on the menu.

I came with friends for dessert one evening, but it was a bit disappointing overall.
When we arrived (a little late), all the toast items were already sold out. The staff didn’t inform us beforehand and just let us sit down, which felt quite unprofessional.

The regular cakes were average — nothing special. The shaved ice (bingsu)was less sweet than I expected, which was actually a good thing for me, but it was served in very basic, low-quality dishes that didn’t match the café’s supposed aesthetic or price level.

The biggest disappointment was the Thai Tea Mille Crepe. The sauce was not smooth at all — it had clumps and felt very sweet(looks like curry?). I still finished it, but the next day I suffered from severe diarrhea. I strongly suspect the sauce and cream in the Thai Tea mille crepe were not fresh.

Lesson learned: it’s probably best to avoid dairy-based desserts here in the evening.
Will think twice before returning.

Live Oak Park is a nice city park with a mix of amenities and spaces for meeting up with friends. There are several distinct areas for different activity types, and this park is especially popular with families.

Between Shattuck and Walnut Streets, there is a green space for groups and families to hang out. There are some nice trees and an idyllic stream where you can catch nature vibes.

Directly south of the lawn and separated by the stream, there is the Live Oak Community Center and Live Oak Theater for community events and performing arts. This side of the park contains playgrounds, basketball courts, and tennis courts. The playground amenities are much better for older children than toddlers. The varuous ball courts are in decent-but-not-amazing condition.

Across the street (between Walnut and Oxford), there is a smaller park "Area 2" with some picnic tables and a grill. There isn't much green space on this side, but you can visit the Berkeley Art Center while here. I recommend stopping by if you are visiting when the Art Center is open (12pm-5pm, Fri-Sun, free admission).

That’s not just shady, that’s credit card FRAUD. This bartender was unprofessional, dishonest, and clearly had no interest in doing his job. First time at this bar and definitely the last. If you go here, watch your drinks, your tab, and your receipt. He clearly thought he could get away with it and probably has. I'm sure this isn't the first time either and management must not care since he still has a job.

this place used to be THE spot for midweek karaoke, and now karaoke is every night, meaning it might be the spot for weekend karaoke too! i don't think it has thus transformed into A Karaoke Bar though, even if it is one per se. (note: this is legally correct use of "per se", whether you like it or not.) it's kind of an offbeat-but-earnest divey vibe, which hasn't changed over the years — i find this comforting. usually i just go to hang out with my own group of friends, but it is very common that i will end up chatting a bit with someone new, and everyone is always very kind and very cool. it's an eclectic crowd made up of nonetheless normal and genuine people. years ago, i thought the bartenders didn't really like me because they were making me weak drinks (i always tipped well, in case that's what you were thinking). i kept going anyway. now i feel like that problem has been fully corrected, although that might just be because my tolerance is dropping now that middle age is approaching on the horizon. i do see some reviews mentioning bartenders being rude, and for what it's worth, i've never personally had that experience. management also seems to be handling these situations appropriately. but the thing is: i kind of don't want to go to a bar where someone hasn't complained about a rude bartender? that's how i know a spot has character. a metaphor: this bar shares the name for a soldier in a core unit of the ancient roman army, but when you arrive, you will be greeted by a sign reading "cead míle fáilte", which feels like an ironic juxtaposition, especially for someone like me whose family came from ireland through scotland to the united states. rome never openly attempted to conquer hibernia (their name for ireland), but they did exert a proto-colonial type of influence over the region, primarily through christianity. however, catholicism came to be a defining aspect of irish identity, especially during the troubles. small aspects of gaelic paganism survived even into my own family's traditions by being fully wrapped in a christian coat. now these things are inextricable; culture is messy like that. and in that respect, the name kind of works. that's this bar — it's a lot of things, and they weirdly fit together into being a special little community. the reason i have to withhold a star, even though (in case you haven't figured it out by now) this is my favorite bar is that the drinks... are fine? this is mostly a review of the experience, but drinks are a part of that experience, and they're honestly whatever. they're good enough! it's the memories and fun times that keep me coming back. objectively, it's a four out of five. but subjectively... well, everybody knows it has a perfect score in my heart.

The bakery is one of the best all-around bakeries in the area -- other places in the East Bay may specialize in a certain type of baked good, but the Cheese Board can make everything well (especially if it has cheese!)

If stopping by for the bakery, you must try the signature cheese roll. Otherwise, there is a rotating selection of breads and pastries, some of which were "invented" in house and have special names (wolverines, zampanos, chocolate things, etc.). The bakery items are continually made throughout the day.

While waiting in line for the bakery, you can also get a selection of cheese and prepared sauces. The $25 Adventure Bag contains a good choice of random cheeses, and the green hot sauce is also tasty as a condiment/dip.

You can buy par-baked pizzas to finish baking at home. The pizzas are always vegetarian and change every day. If you're just visiting, you can get a baked pizza at the pizzeria next door instead. The pizza is the best pizza in Berkeley.

Everything you can buy here is delicious. You can't go wrong with any of the food choices.

---

For first time visitors or a casual stop, I recommend buying a cheese roll, seeded baguette, and any pastry that tickles your fancy.

For a more substantial amount of food to bring home, I recommend a pizza, a 6-pack of English muffins, the green sauce, and a cheese Adventure Bag. The green sauce usually goes well on the pizza.

Staff here are very friendly, knowledgeable and helpful.

A great variety of cheeses are available here, with 3 flavors available to try each week. They offer plentiful amounts of sheep and goat cheeses as well more common cheeses as well.

Service is quick but doesn't feel rushed. Store is very clean and well presented.

Great stuff.
This is the best cheese store and bakery around. Just the smell of everything when you walk in is amazing. Everything here is excellent, but especially the cheese rolls and sticky buns.
If you come to Berkeley this is a must visit bakery! The best bread, cheese, olives, scones, muffins, and sweet rolls (outside of Nabolom). Get half bakes or go next store to get some hot pizza!

This park offers two playgrounds, a grass area, picnic benches with bbq, basketball, tennis and volleyball court, a small amphitheater, and sidewalks for biking and walking. The grassy area is really sunny as most trees are on the outer rim.
The larger play area has a structure, standard swings, and a tire swing. The structure has two slides (a double and a spiral), steps, ladders, a bridge, and activities.

top_reviews.content:
Typical East Bay regional park, complete with classic EBRPD trail layout which go directly up the steepest parts of a hill. I don't know who or if anyone plans these trails, but it sure seems like their motto is "The shortest way from Point A to Point B". We started at the Stonewall-Panoramic trailhead off of Claremont Ave, which has almost no parking, you're fighting with residents and other hikers to find a spot. We got there around 8AM and still had trouble parking. Narrow winding road, parallel parking on steep inclines, cars park 2 inches from your bumper, fun stuff!

The trails we took were nice, again the start was extraordinarily steep, right off the jump you go from resting HR to max effort. The trail network is bracketed by Claremont Ave and Grizzly Peak Blvd. There are nice spots for panoramic vistas of the Bay, and some flatter trails as well. The views are the best reason to visit this park, it's just a bit of a headache to park and the steepness of the trails is annoying. Good wildflower displays in spring.
No parking? Two lane winding road.  Beautiful drive.  Overlooking the San Francisco Bay Area.  Court tower and the bay and Golden Gate Bridge’s can be seen.  No cell service in areas.   Hiking trails

I love watching the sunset from here, it's amazing. During the day it's excellent to hike for the views alone. I highly recommend visiting at least once and taking a good camera. Lots of incredible views and trails. The trails have numerous steep parts, so bring water and good trail shoes.

Great park with challenging hikes and fantastic views. There are trails here that ascend ~1,500 feet - all the way to the base of Tilden Regional Park. It’s a park I frequent when weather permits (which fairly often) for the hikes.

I’ve seen all manner of wildlife on trails in this park: Coyotes, deer, prairie dogs (or at least that is what I think they are), rabbits, rattle snakes, lizards, etc… but haven’t had any issues.

Gorgeous view of the city and the bay from the preserve! The best view points are close to different trail heads around  Berkeley, the Berkeley Overlook Vista Point and a place marked as Pano. However, those segments of the trail are also the steepest so definitely be prepared for some strenuous climb.
The trail east of Panoramic Way is significantly quieter with much less foot traffic but also you are getting away from the best views and getting into the woods.

top_reviews.content:
The best escape room I have ever been to!

Our group of 8 did “The Attraction” room and it was so immersive! The challenges were diverse, and not repetitive in any way so each piece of the puzzle suited different skills. You really have to work as a group to get out in the 2 hr limit.

Located quite literally in the Palace of Fine Arts building this is a must do group activity!

10/10 recommend!

This was hands down one of the most memorable experiences of our entire California trip.

We came as a family of five with three kids (ages 3, 7 and 10) to celebrate our oldest daughter’s 10th birthday, and choosing the Edison Room turned out to be the perfect birthday gift.

What impressed us most was that every single family member could participate. Even our 3-year-old had little “missions” and felt like an important part of the team. Our 7- and 10-year-olds solved plenty of puzzles, while the adults had enough challenging moments to stay fully engaged. I’d definitely recommend having at least one puzzle-loving adult in the group, but that’s exactly what makes it such a rewarding family experience.

The puzzles are incredibly creative, varied and satisfying. Nothing felt repetitive or cliché. Every new discovery made us smile and made us want to keep exploring.

What made this room truly special, though, was its educational value. It’s much more than an escape room—it’s an immersive journey into the world of Thomas Edison, inventions, electricity, innovation and the spirit of discovery. On our way home we spent another hour talking with our daughters about Edison, his laboratory, the history of electricity and how great inventions changed the world. That’s something we definitely didn’t expect from an escape room!

A huge thank you to the entire Palace Games team for creating such a thoughtful experience. Especially to Andrew for his thoughtful advice which room to choose, and AJ who was incredible hands-on game manager at the place. It was worth every penny and became a birthday our daughter—and all of us—will remember for many years.

We have done 3 rooms here, all of the rooms are the best of the best. "The Attraction," is truly amazing. I doubt I'll ever find an escape room that well designed and elaborate ever again. The staff is always great. Important note, drive through the pay parking lot to the parking right in front of the entrance. :)

Can't wait to come back and try the others, kudos to the designers and the very friendly staff.

top_reviews.content:
A must-visit place for anyone living in the area (4/5 Green Stars)
Bring cash! That’s the first rule of Schmidt’s Pub. Maybe it’s the only rule! I’ve been coming here a bit more regularly, lately – more visits in the last year compared to the previous decade, in fact. Now I wonder what I was waiting for.

According to the East Bay Express, Schmidt’s Pub is “basically your living room, but better” – that does sum it up, except that very few of us have living rooms anything like this, with a cozy fireplace surrounded by comfy armchairs and rustic tables beside sunny windows. Not many of us have living rooms with Old Speckled Hen on tap, or populated with an entertaining parade of quirky folk and friendly dogs. If the people and dogs are not entertaining enough then pick up a copy of Calvin and Hobbes or A History of Clay Pipes (okay, I made that one up) and have a little retreat with a pint.

4/5 Green Stars for social and environmental impact, based on these factors:
•	Beer on tap (transported in reusable kegs) has a much lower footprint compared to bottles or cans.
•	Allows you to bring your own food, which is good for folk like vegans who are often more comfortable with BYO.
•	The snacks available at the counter could be a bit more Berkeley (or Albany)! They were mostly from big corps – Lays chips (PepsiCo) and chocolate bars from Mars. Would be nice to see a more imaginative/ethical selection.
•	A great community space with an inclusive atmosphere. Schmidt’s is home to many groups (e.g., knitting) and provides a second family for many, some who send postcards from their trips!
•	Finally, we shouldn’t underestimate the importance of having a place to slow down, reflect and connect with each other a little. In that respect, Schmidt’s Pub is worth its weight in gold.

Schmidt's is a rare anomaly. A cross between an English pub, a bed and breakfast and the living room of cultured intellectual. Where else in the East Bay can you enter a 100+ year old house, choose from a selection of ales, lagers and stouts on draft and in bottles and cans and an assortment of fine tobacco, cigars and smoking accessories, sit down in a chair with a wooden table and read something, including the books on the shelves? Truly a wonder. And if you do purchase a cigar, you can smoke it outside. I wouldn't be surprised if people discuss Proust here. Cheers!

We highly recommend this escape room to anyone looking for a fun and challenging adventure. We can’t wait to come back and try another room!

A great escape room! We were a group of 7 with a mix of people who had never done an escape room and people who had escaped many times. Great vibe, great sweets and chai, but sub-par customer service.  Stopped a little before 8 pm for a chai and a treat. The chai itself was deliciously creamy and mild with a lovely undertone of sweet spiciness.  The almond cornmeal pound cake was ridiculously good. It made me want to raid more of the sweet display case to see what other secrets the treats there were hiding.  The vibe was fun and upbeat, but the seating was a little hard to navigate.  My only real gripe is the staff.  The staff member who helped was barely engaged with us, and did the bare minimum at the register before preparing my order.

The hint of salt, almost an aftertaste, and the mild caramel played so well with the espresso shot.  No notes.  It was incredible.  Also had to try another slice of the almond corn meal pound cake, so rich and delicious.  Loved it, and I promise it will be devoured again.

The place has the fare one expects at a good coffee shop, a selection of coffee brews and espresso drinks along with pastries and other goodies.  However their mocha is quite the delight, with a real dark chocolate taste to it - something that I love.

On top of the normal coffee drink menu, there are a number of more exotic chocolate drinks, a tasty thicker chocolate espresso drink or even thicker European style hot chocolate.  For chocolate lovers these are a must.

The ambience is rather eclectic with fun decorations and even little dragon figurine sets, it definitely gives the feel of fun place to visit.

There is a huge variety of chocolates to choose from, some just shelves with a collection of chocolate bars from different providers, but also their own selection of chocolate as well.

The owner is a fascinating woman, and very interesting to talk to with a lot of background in the local chocolate industry.

The service of course was very good and the verse that was very friendly.

I was thoroughly impressed by the selection of both drinking chocolates and chocolate bars for purchase. I was disappointed, but mostly delighted, by their ban on working in the cafe during holiday hours in favor of reserving the tables for socializing. The barista who took my order was very helpful with explaining their drinking chocolate options and informing my selection. If I lived in the area, I would be here constantly (which might be a problem!)

I ordered their iced pistachio latte, and genuinely my jaw dropped when I took the first sip, because I wasn’t expecting it to taste that good. They use a very high quality spread that tastes like the nut itself, and adds a sweetness to the drink that does not overpower the coffee at all. It’s perfect. I noticed a lot of coffee use pistachio syrup for a pistachio flavoured drink, which I personally despise. But Heyma use a spread that really enhances the coffee. Going here is an experience, transporting you to a different place and culture. As a Middle Eastern girl myself, it is officially one of my favourite coffee shops in the world.

We wanted the Kirby but after we won they gave us this blue girl which we were so confused about. Like why have three prizes and then not have any indication of which prize it was. We honestly wouldn’t have even tried this game 3-4 times if we knew this was the prize :/ like hello why?! And their manager still wouldn’t let us switch it to the Kirby … plz be aware the bottom prize will always be the one you get

An hour of bowling is $66 which is pretty expensive compared to more mom and pop bowling alleys, the bowling alley uses strings attached to the pins

Been going to Round 1 for years but never been so disrespected by the staff as I have here. I was visiting last weekend and went to the Stonestown Round 1 to see if they had any good prizes at the exchange since I had ~16,000 tickets saved up over the years and my local Round 1 doesn't have many good prizes.

I chose a locked up prize worth 10,000 tickets and had to fill out some paperwork for the exchange. They swiped my card and the screen showed the purchase. I filled out the paperwork, handed it to the staff and asked if there was anything else I needed to do. The woman behind the counter told me "No, my manager just needs to sign it" and walked away to help someone at a different counter. I stood around for around 30 seconds, not sure if I needed to be present any longer but couldn't get her attention while she was busy. I figured the transaction was complete so I took the prize and walked out to my car— I had an appointment to get to soon, a gift from the family member hosting me while visiting SF.

Just after I got back to my car and started navigating, I got a phone call. It was the manager at Round 1, demanding I return immediately. He said he needed me back to "verify my tickets are legitimate". I explained I was visiting and had an appointment to get to, etc, that they had my member card information if they needed to verify anything like that. That I could email them any more info if they needed something since I really didn't have time to spare. He said that his staff said I swiped the item and took off after she told me I needed to wait for the manager, and he told me that he'd report me for stealing the item if I didn't return.

I reluctantly hurried back and got the counter. I handed my card over to the staff (again) and she swiped it, looking to her screen and pressing something on there to pull up my transaction history. She swore up and down that they'd "tried refreshing it like 6 times" but that it didn't work before. She went to get her manager who did me the kindness of showing up after 4 minutes before proceeding to stare at the screen and scroll through year after year of every time I earned tickets at round 1. He did this for a few more minutes, saying nothing to me, not looking at me, before signing his part of the paperwork and saying "Thank you" to me before walking off.

After all the hassle he'd put me through, the stress of knowing I'd be late to my appointment, that I couldn't do my family the decency of showing up to an appointment on time, after threatening to report me as stealing his merchandise, he can't even look at me and give me a simple apology for the difficulty. For making me trudge back to fix his mistake since he clearly hasn't trained his staff to communicate clearly, all so he could swipe my card again since I guess there must have been something wrong with it on his end the first time. So he could idly look through my years upon years of visits to Round 1 after having insulted me and called me a thief.

I peeked at the screen while he was going through my history. Seems over the years I've spent more than $1200 at Round 1, but no more. Absolutely baffling that someone in his position could lack the most basic semblance of customer service skills, it's no wonder his staff are incompetent.

Around six months before we got married in Berkeley in August, we started reaching out to possible welcome party venues for the night before the big day. We wanted to find a place that would allow for outside food at a reasonable cost, provide quality drinks for a fair price, and has a nice access-controlled event space on premises. As someone who has run a number of large events previously, I know well that this task can be somewhere between tough and impossible. The minute one uses the term “wedding” to any vendor, costs can go way up. Or venues can charge exorbitant fees for space reservations, or have minimum spends that are crazy. And, honestly, it is really hard to simply find venues that allow for outside food.

So we started the search, and emailed venues throughout the East Bay area (Oakland, Berkeley, Emeryville, Albany, Alameda), At first, the only possible venues I could find were craft brewing establishments. The one with the best location for us charged a lot for space reservation, and for a space that was not access controlled, and without our own dedicated bar. So, in effect, we would be paying thousands for a craft beer spot to a few “reserved” signs on some random tables for us. Suffice to say, we were starting to get discouraged.

Then, after another internet search, I found a listing for Acme Bar in west Berkeley. Having never been there before (it has been a few years since I have lived in the East Bay), I asked around and realized that it’s a pretty cool bar with good service and great drinks. We checked in out in person, and was pretty impressed with the available event space. But our greatest surprise was when we actually emailed Acme, and got to know the owner of the bar. She must have had a previous life as an event planner or something, cause she was amazing. The prices she quoted were quite fair, and she helped identify possible outside food vendors that met our needs. She helped arrange special drinks for our event, which ended up being really tasty. The beer selection we ended up having was top notch as well, as was the wine selection. We arranged for our own dedicated space on a Friday evening, with our own bar. She helped identify our needs for us, and went out of her way – along with her great staff – to ensure we had a great event.

Some of my friends are quite experienced with events, and others are pretty hard to please, and everyone had a great time. The price quoted was on target, and there were absolutely no surprises, price-wise. I have never been more satisfied with a venue, or had a better event for the price. Working with Acme was, in two words, both fair and fun. We highly recommend working with them – you will not be disappointed.
