top_reviews.content:
I went to 924 Gilman Street last night for a hardcore show, and it was honestly one of the most beautiful, heartwarming experiences I’ve had in a long time. My partner used to go to Gilman 20 years ago and really wanted me to see it.
All of the bands were indígena, and the energy was just through-the-roof positive. Before the second band started, they played norteño and were like, “We’re proud of who we are and where we’re from. ICE can’t take that from us.” It was so powerful. One moment people were dancing bachata, and the next it turned into hardstyle two-step.
It made me so proud to be Chicano,and so proud of our young ones. You could really feel how important hardcore is. Arms flailing, incredible twirls, cartwheels, roundhouse kicks, playful punching. There’s a kind of radical freedom in hardcore that’s so rare to witness.
When the show ended and we were driving home, I looked at my partner and said, “Wow… that venue has probably saved so many lives.” An all-ages space, no drugs, no booze, shows happening constantly,it’s no wonder it’s such an institution. It creates room for people to safely be themselves.
Definitely my favorite place in the bay. So worth visiting.

Prices do seem a little higher than before, but honestly with the way everything is right now, it’s understandable considering the portion sizes and quality.

top_reviews.content: Beautiful simple and delightful cafe in Albany. Stopped for a Boba and Banh Mi and have fully made this one of my regular neighborhood spots. The sandwiches are killer. ❤️ And the owners are amazing. Definitely worth a stop!

When searching for a quick, easy, and filling lunch during my break, I ended up here at this cute little Viet Bagel & Banh Mi shop called Tay Tah Cafe!

When you first enter, you’re guided by arrows that lead you to the ordering tablet, or you can order at the main counter. The shop is small, but has plenty of counter seating and some small tables available as well! In between the front door and ordering, there’s a selection of chips and snacks for you to browse as well.

I was initially looking to order Banh Mi but was a bit intimidated by the $17/banh mi price tag. I opted in for an open face Asiago Bagel with Lox for $13 and placed my order. Breakfast orders that are $10+ get a free house coffee as well, so of course I opted in for it!

There’s a bathroom just around the corner from the ordering kiosk, but while I was making my way over there, the kind staff let me know that they are actually sold out of lox. They offered me a refund or to change what I ordered. I decided to switch to the Asiago Bagel with Ham, Bacon, Egg, and Cheese since it was the same price as the Lox!

My coffee came out first, and the person who gave me my coffee also filled up my cup with ice when I asked! The coffee itself had a nice deep & bitter flavor which I look for in a house coffee.

The sandwich was STUFFED full. I’ve never had a bagel breakfast sandwhich where I’ve quite had to unhinge my jaw like this. My photos did not do the sandwich justice, but I promise it’s so much bigger than you’d expect!

The eggs were perfectly fluffy and smothered in cheese. The ham and bacon were cooked to my personal liking. If you like crispy bacon, maybe mention that to them, because it was perfectly chewy for me. The bagel, was soft, fluffy, yet so bouncy, and I LOVE that there are poppy seeds mixed into their Asiago bagel.

The cost to quantity ratio for the breakfast sandwich was 100% worth it. I’ll definitely be back when I need a hearty sandwich.

Stopped by Tay Tah Café on Solano Ave in Albany for lunch and had the Avocado Tofu Banh Mi—fresh, flavorful, and such a generous portion that I had to take half home. They also serve coffee, tea, boba, and smoothies. A really nice spot, I’d definitely come back.

Such a cute little bakery shop!! The morning buns, pastry, and coffees were amazing. Staff was super friendly.

After I put the beans in the hopper, I began to grind the machine made a loud crunch noise mid grind. I looked inside and found rocks (pictured) lodged in the grinder and completely ruining my Breville machine. I called Cole’s, emailed them, and went back to show them the rocks they sold me in the bag. The associate said she was going to speak to her manager and they would call me after she confirmed these were rocks and from the bag. Few days went by, no call. I went back, the associate wanted a picture of the machine. I showed them a picture and they again said the manager would call. A few days later, no call. I went back again, the associate said I could leave a message for the manager. Still…no…call. I’m out a $700 Breville machine and was looking for Cole’s to help with the repair cost or replace my machine but I’ve gotten radio silence over their severe lapse of quality control. Avoid this shop at all costs.

top_reviews.content: I really wanted to like this place but it didn't meet expectations. The staff were friendly when we first walked in and politely sat us down. top_reviews.content:
Wow, the hojicha latte was so good here. We also got a matcha latte which tasted a little too milky so I wonder what's up with that. They have both a lot of workers and customers, so you can tell the food and drinks are good.

Just checked out Binge Coffee House and I’m impressed ☕✨

This Vietnamese-inspired spot is a whole vibe, super cozy, study-friendly, and definitely a go-to if you’re in the Berkeley area. They’ve got everything from authentic Vietnamese iced coffee to unique matcha creations and tasty bites like bánh mì and pandan waffles.

I tried the banana matcha and wow… sweet, creamy, and perfectly balanced with salted cashews on top 🤤🔥 that sweet + salty combo really hit.

They’ve got a wide variety of matcha flavors too (banana, pistachio, and more), so there’s plenty to explore.

Highly recommend if you’re looking for a chill spot with good energy and even better drinks 💚

I got the white peach matcha, less sweet with oat milk! It only cost about $7, which I feel isn't bad, especially considering the inflation of everything right now. It was perfect! The matcha tasted authentic and wasn't overly powered by the milk. The white peach added a nice sweet kick, but not overly so. Very clean inside and they have kiosks to order at. It seems to be a popular spot for studying as all tables were occupied with laptops :D 10/10 would recommend and come again!

Black sesame foam latte is very sweet but still good, would give it 8/10. I like the foam to coffee ratio too.

Parking is also terrible around this area

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

This indoor playground is fantastic! It’s the perfect spot for my child to burn off energy and have an amazing time. The climbing wall is a highlight—safe, well-maintained, and so much fun. My child couldn’t get enough of it!

The arcade is another great feature, with a nice variety of classic and modern games. The entire space is clean, organized, and offers something for everyone. The staff is incredibly friendly and attentive, which made me feel confident about my child’s safety.

The playground is spacious, colorful, and designed to keep kids entertained for hours. Whether it’s for a casual day out or a special occasion, I highly recommend this place for families looking for a fun and active experience!

Bay Play was a great place to hold my daughter's 8th birthday party. My daughter loved bouncing, climbing and running around with her friends on the various structures. Mirinda, who helped check my family and our guests in, was a godsend. Her graciousness and kindness throughout the whole event (prepping the room and making sure she kept our cake cold while kids were playing before food time, etc.) made the event flow smoothly and relieved a load from me (as the mama planner). Thank you Mirinda and Bay Play for making my daughter's birthday a memorable one!

All around awesome indoor spot to come for just a play date or a birthday party!

Plus they carry some millinery (hatmaking) supplies like wool felt hoods (cone shaped) and millinery petersham ribbon. Check out what I blocked! Oh and they have a hat block lending library and classes in all kinds of crafts.

This place is one-of-a-kind. I was a crocheter and had picked up embroidery, so I stopped by on a whim for thread. But I got totally sidetracked by their incredible lace collection. I walked away with so much more than thread that day. That collection was what inspired me to pick up shuttle tatting, which has become such a delight to me. It's also been my main hobby since my hands/wrist don't agree with crochet anymore. And tatting is good for your hands!  I've moved away from the area, but still order supplies from here and will sometimes travel in for classes. I am so grateful that Lacis exists because it enables us to keep the art of lace alive. The staff and class instructors are kind, helpful, and patient.

My friend and I went to visit the place out of curiosity. We were amazed by the variety of things that were displayed and sold. This place truly is a wonderland for the people who love sawing, knitting, crocheting,  and all other textile arts and crats.

Call in advance for tours.

top_reviews.content: Tucked in cute Westbrae neighborhood for Berkeley, surrounded by wholesome establishments like the Berkeley Natural Grocery, Coffee Conscious just to name a few. It is hard to find parking, best by the North  Berkeley Bart Station, 12 bus line, cycling and walking along the Ohlone trail. However, because it is an outdoors brewery, restaurant you have to take whatever weather you get, heavy rain or strong winds can ruin your night. The food is what you'd find at the bar, I really like their sandwiches, the burger is fine. There's a long beverage selection, even non-alcoholic, and the staff bring the food to you; they also clear your table.  The kids menu is small. There's a play structure in the back for kids. Restroom, they have two, one with a changing table for babies and toddlers. For sporting events they have two big flat screen TVs, outside and in the tent, where I prefer against the element. Great for sporting events, or with a group of Friends, and very Family Friendly. I recommend this place.

I go here often couple times a month. The people are absolutely wonderful. The food is outstanding. The atmosphere is priceless. Calming enjoyable dog friendly family friendly solitude friendly. Just a great place to go and have a good time. And a beer is wonderful. My favorite the party wave.
Love this brewery! Not only do they make delicious beer and food but also help the environment, animals, LGBT, and people in need. The service was excellent and atmosphere comfortable.

This beer garden is great, especially if you have kids. The kids corner is really cool and their kids menu is good. The beer selection is great and there are cider/non-beer options available too. I really enjoyed their lemon shandy. The atmosphere and service is good. There are gluten free options available; I recommend the loaded fries + pork and the gluten free burgers.

This was a fun little brewery. I especially liked being able to order at the table from your phone and then bringing your drinks and food straight to you. The beer was great. I tried the GOAT Maibock, Earth to Beer Kolsch, and Hawk Hill Hefeweizen. The maibock was my fave of the 3.

There are bench tables plus lawn chair table seating arrangements. Staff was awesome and very family and pet friendly.

top_reviews.content: Love this place! The membership is absolutely worth it if you live in the Bay Area and can visit regularly. The staff are amazing, friendly, welcoming, and great at what they do. The sake quality never disappoints. We always leave with a smile, and every friend I’ve brought here has loved it too. Don’t miss their occasional events, they’re set in such a great atmosphere and make for a truly unique experience! One recommendation would be to open the parking lot for customers on tasting days.

For sake and wine lovers alike this place is a must! Learn about Sake while enjoying a guided tasting to help you deepen your knowledge about the difference between each type of Sake available.  The next step is to watch a short video of how Sake it’s actually brewed followed by a visit to their museum where they have gathered many of the old and original equipments to brew Sake, I haven’t seen anything like this anywhere in the US. I hope you too enjoy it as much as we did!

When we visited 2–3 years ago, we enjoyed our experience so much that we decided to bring our family back with us today. The sake we tasted was delicious, especially the Nigori.

Unfortunately, the experience this time didn’t quite live up to our previous visit. The mandatory gratuity added for our group of five felt a little disappointing, especially since we were seated at a shared communal table rather than a private table. We also remembered receiving several complimentary tastings during our last visit, which encouraged us to purchase a few bottles on our way out. This time, we didn’t have that same experience, and the overall visit felt more focused on gratuity and upselling the additional shots than on creating the warm, welcoming experience we remembered.

We still enjoyed the sake, but we left feeling that the hospitality and generosity that made our previous visit so memorable were missing this time.

Do make sure make a reservation before you go and credit card only if you like to purchase anything after your testing!

We have Eugene as our guide/host. He is wonderful, very knowledgeable about the products and the making of the sake.

We sampled more than ten different Daijinjo, Junmai and Kinpaku. But my favorite is still the Daijinjo!

Everyone here is very nice and friendly. Miss Hope Cooc is very nice and helpful with our order. We love to continue to coming back here to fix our Sake withdrawal.
Kampai! Yuji was so knowledgeable about sake and its production. I would highly recommend this as a fun activity in the Bay.

top_reviews.content: Lovely hole in the wall place! Great flavors executed very well. The Shiro latte is definitely where it’s at. Slightly sweet, slightly salty, perfectly umami. The space is serene. Everything is beautifully put together. Full disclosure parking is horrendous, but the area is really nice. So even if you have to park far and walk, it’s not so bad.

Best specialty coffee shop in the bay area, hands down. For pourover enthusiasts, it doesn't get any better.

Whether you're deep into pourover or need an alt-milk latte, these guys deliver in an uncompromising, intimate setting with a super focused menu. I think you gotta enjoy this now before they blow up and scale up.

They're rotating globally top-tier coffee brands like Tim Wendelboe and Big Sur, while also being a micro-roaster themselves with a specialization in Chinese origin coffee. The curation is second to none, everything is superb.

Pourover and espresso are all faultless. The gear on the bar is all unmatched and cutting-edge, think Dragonfly and Orea drippers and I've actually seen them brew with (not cheap at all) Sibarist Fast filters.

The cups are absolutely dialed in with hyper clarity. These are real-deal pourover gods. The milk drinks are so elegant that you can pick anything and be sure it'll be good.

I could go on and on... but will just say this is the finest specialty coffee experience in the bay right now. Oh, and they're super nice guys.

Finally got to try Yunan coffee again! They are rare to come by in the US (last time I had them was in Kurasu Kyoto), I’m grateful that Masterpiece offers them right here in the Bay Area :)
My barista gracefully shared their recipe with me too. I enjoyed my visit!

I recently got a chance to visit Masterpiece Coffee in Berkeley. They focus on specialty coffee produced in Yunnan, China, with Asian-inspired drinks served at a kiosk. Their specialty is Chinese coffee, slow bar pour over, a minimal menu, and uniquely crafted drinks. Young Sun takes incredible pride in every cup, and my experience was truly heavenly!

Pricewise yhe coffee and tea are reasonable. Will visit next time to try the pour over coffee.

Came here for lunch and it was such a good find! The baristas were super friendly and thorough — they asked me like 5 variables for my matcha including sweetness, milk, toppings, iced/hot — and it was exactly how I like it!
I got a tomato panini which was hot and delicious!

Polaris Cafe is like a big oasis in the middle of a city. This is my new favorite spot to decompress and study. It is very inviting and relaxing. The staff are very nice and accommodating. The prices are reasonable. The vegetarian, breakfast, lunch, pastry and dessert options are a lot. The specials for today are butter chicken and tandoori chicken over basmati rice. I got my drink for $6. I am very glad to see that it is not packed. I can literally just sleep here. It look so peaceful with all the plants and granite tables + the beautiful fountain and scenery out the floor to ceiling windows. I’ll go the extra 20 miles to study here. I really love the concept and would love to have my own like this in the future.

I stayed at a nearby hotel for a little over a week and visited Polaris pretty often. The hotel WiFi was trash so I (embarrassingly) camped here for large chunks of the day. The beverages are great—I had Vietnamese iced coffee, a thai tea situation with pandan foam (so good!!), iced matcha, hojicha, a passion fruit iced tea. They have rotating cold foam flavors which is pretty cool. All of the drinks I had were great. The pastries are also fantastic. The staff are SO NICE! During one of my visits, I had to rush and use the bathroom and a staff member kindly watched my things while I ran to one (it’s the buildings’ bathroom, so they don’t have their own for public use). It was just so thoughtful and kind of them. Oh! I also had a corn chowder soup that was delicious here. I was disappointed at first that they don’t make breakfast burritos anymore but the food is great still, pastries are fantastic, and the beverages are lovely.
There is limited seating inside the cafe itself,  but the atrium has plenty of tables (two in a corner that have outlets), and the plants are so lush! The stone tables are pretty but hurt to sit in for too long (which is entirely my fault bc I was a camper lol)

top_reviews.content: Came here for the first time and the waiters, staff, owner was kind. Lots of Hong Kong style snacks, food items on the menu along with selection of drinks. l Plenty of seating and easily accessible location being at the front of the plaza. Right off I80, check this place out!

Came in on a Friday afternoon and restaurant was about half full. Appreciate the food was not too salty as we had two elderly's in my party.

Corn and Chicken Soup: Standard Chicken Corn Soup. It was more corn starchy than I liked
Walnut Prawns: No complaints on the prawns or the candied walnuts but I have never seen this dish served as two separate components and without broccoli.
Sautéed Pea Shoots: Always a favorite of mine but this dish was on the tough side. They definitely did not peel the older pieces.
Seafood Noodles: Appreciate the amount of seafood in this noodle dish however too much corn starch was used in the sauce.
Bell Pepper Squid Stir Fry: Good amount of squid and pepper. Flavor was good. Probably best thing we ordered.

Overall this restaurant was okay, the staff was just the right amount of attentiveness however will likely not revisit.

Came here for dinner, first time visiting this place even though I've passed by many times since it opened.  The place was busy, but there were still a good amount of tables to sit in.  I think we only waited a minute, and the waitress sat us down and got us tea all within a couple of minutes.  The decoration and atmosphere is casual with a sense that you are in a Hong Kong style restaurant with a large mural of a Hong Kong street with lots of store front signs and neon lights.  The decoration is eclectic with an Asian theme with lots of little Asian themed toys and knickknacks.

The food menu is extensive with lots of common foods found in street cafes such as toasts, baked rice, and noodles dishes to the more common dishes like fried rice, Chow mien, porridge, etc. Then there is the more oddball and exotic dishes made with intestines, blood, and frogs.

As I wasn't into experimenting into the exotic dishes we decided to order BBQ pork fried rice,  salt & pepper deep fried fish, salt & pepper deep fried tofu, wonton soup, western style overeasy egg in minced beef sauce over rice, and stir-fry beef rib-eye Japan style.

All the dishes came in within the next 10 to 15 minutes.  They looked delicious to my eyes and smelled even better.   The bbq pork unfortunately did not meet my satisfaction.  Yeah, it looked great and smelled good, but the taste was just bland.  There wasn't even a taste of the bbq pork. The pork itself was dry, like the remnants of old bbq pork cuttings that have been sitting for a while.  Fortunately the other dishes were arriving and we had a better experience.

The next dish to come was the wonton soup. The bowl had enough soup and wonton dumplings to serve at least all four of us with a couple extras.  There were also fresh baby bok Choi vegetables in the soup, which was nice to balance all the meat.  The soup was okay,  nothing exciting.  The meat filling in the wonton was okay too... I've had better.

The next dish up was the salt & pepper tofu cubes. These deep-fried morsels were piping hot with a nice outer crunch and very soft interior.  The outside had a really nice seasoning that was savory with a hint of spices. There were also sprinkling of fried jalapeño peppers and garlic.  It was delicious.

The next dish was the salt & pepper deep fried fish.  Just like the tofu,  these fish were battered and deep fried and seasoned with salt, spices,  and that mixture of jalapeños pepper and fried garlic. The fish was delicious with a semi crunchy outer shell and a very nice soft, smooth, almost melty interior. I'm not sure what type of fish they used, but it was really nice and soft.

A minute later, the waitress brought out the rest of our order.  It was the overeasy egg in minced beef and sauce over rice and the stir-fry beef rib-eye Japan style.

The western style egg in minced beef sauce over rice was truly delicious.  It was a mound of rice with a brown gravy sauce with minced beef and shavings of I think it was broccoli stems. In the middle of all that mess was a raw egg cooking in the heat of the dish.  The beef and sauce mixed in with the rice was just great.  I really can't explain the taste, it was like putting gravy into your rice but the gravy is not over powering. It balanced the right amount of saltiness, beef flavor, and umami to go right with the plain white rice.

My favorite dish above all the stir-fry beef ribeye Japan style dish.  The pieces of beef are stir fried in a sweet, savory sauce with a very distinctive flavor I couldn't identify.  Under the beef are pan fried soft tofu rounds that have the sauce dripping on it.  Surrounding the beef and tofu is a bed of fresh broccoli with drippings of sauce on top.  This dish was really exceptionally good.  The beef was so tender and juicy with the addition of the sauce that it was an explosion of flavor and texture in your mouth.

We truly ate really well and had lots of leftover for the next day.  I'll probably visit again and try their other dishes.  Some of the dishes you can't find in regular Chinese restaurants.

top_reviews.content:
Both hands up for this wonderful coffee place I happened to stumble upon, right outside the skirts of Downtown Berkeley. They're located right on the intersection of MLK and University, right behind the Indian restaurant.

This coffee place is honestly a little bit small, so please proceed with caution at all costs. But it really makes you feel cozy at home. They do have upstairs seating, but rather really limited. It will be full at times, and at times, not at all. It depends on the time that you go.

They have a wide assortment of sweet and savory pastries available as well. I got their ham & cheese scone, as well as their speciality drink, their banana cream iced coffee. I love how balanced their iced coffee is with the banana cream, which surprisingly, is made with ACTUAL banana puree made from actual bananas.

The barista who made my drink was very nice and very chill, and served it rather quick. That's what's up!

If you're looking for a locally-owned coffee shop right here in Berkeley, look no further than Bench Coffee! Trust me, it will be a trip worth it :)

Bench is an outstanding cafe!! I just got a lavender cappuccino and oh my goodness it was delicious!! Look at this coffee art!! Carson was my barista and he was so kind and welcoming! The chocolate chip cookie is a perfect combination of soft   with that perfect crisp edge! So delicious and really made my day! Thank you Bench!

Lovely place- would come back and recommend! Good spot to read or work  with plenty of outlets, free wifi, open bathroom, and table space upstairs and downstairs. I got the cheese/green onion scone and a warm date latte and enjoyed both. Service was great and atmosphere was calm & relaxing. Came in on a Tuesday from 12:45-2:45pm and was very quiet and not very busy. I essentially had the whole upstairs table to myself for a couple hours.
Note: it seems like oatmilk substitute costs an extra 75 cents.

I just love this local Berkeley gem. Friendly, warm vibe where everyone is welcome. You can tell a lot of thought and care went into the place. The coffee is THE BEST, the pastries are amazing.  From the coffee made with care and the super nice baristas to the comfy/welcoming/inclusive atmosphere, Bench Café has it all. My go to breakfast items are the Spinach Feta Empanadas and the Date Latte. P.S. the music adds a nice touch to the place.

Bench holds such a special place in our hearts and in our community! It is our favorite spot to enjoy a delectable, freshly baked pastry, cake, cookie, or scone along with a coffee drink or matcha latte prepared just perfectly. The aesthetic is perfect — welcoming, light, bright, airy, with touches of greenery and color. The music always sets a lovely backdrop too. And most importantly, the owner Sanaz and her husband, along with all of the incredible baristas including Norah, create an utterly wonderful vibe for the café. The space promotes productive work both downstairs and above the spiral staircase, but also conversations and connections in a welcoming community setting. From the Persian cookies to the unbelievably soft fall-apart blueberry scones, the food is only matched by the cheerful and warm atmosphere that permeates Bench. It is always so fun to see what the baked goods will be — it’s like a delicious little surprise (unless one takes a peak on IG where they are sometimes revealed ahead of time, hehe)!

Thank you Sanaz and team for an incredible community space. We absolutely love coming to Bench and leave this review in order to share with others the cozy little gem on MLK Way that has a cozy little spot in our hearts! ❤️

top_reviews.content: I could not love Signal more. The coffee is excellent and the independent vibe is a very nice addition to this stretch of Solano, where the espresso options used to be limited to big corporate chains. For really rich coffee flavor, I love the cortado. When I want to sit and nurse a drink longer (i.e. most of the time), I love Signal’s mocha, which is made with Tcho chocolate from right here in Berkeley. If I stop by on a hot day, I go for an iced matcha or ube latte. Indoor seating is limited to a few barstools, but there are four tables outside as well. It’s a great spot to watch the constant parade of dogs walking down Solano and to catch up with friends and neighbors. It gets crowded in waves, but I don’t think I’ve ever waited more than ten minutes for a drink.

I am only docking off a point because Signal could definitely hire more people. The one barista on shift at the moment, was truly knocking out the long lines forming.

Did not skimp on the quality of the coffee either. They were kind to all customers and kept their area clean and organized even with the mountain of people ordering.

Huge shout out to the barista! They deserve a raise after what they have to endure.

Kylie (hope I spelled their name right!) makes the best Ube Lattes!

We’ve been going to this location pretty regularly for around a year now and we’re always glad to see Kylie working. We can always count on them to make a great coffee.

Overall, the place has been very consistent. Out of the many, many times we’ve gone, the coffee has only missed the mark a couple times. However, the staff is always friendly and the prices are fair.

The only improvement I could recommend is on the baked goods. We’ve tried several items and they are never bad by any means, but they’ve never really hit the spot either. There’s a good selection of items, but none of them have stood out as great. BUT it’s a coffee shop, not a bakery so can’t complain much!

Thanks to all who work here and make it a great place! It’s one of the few spot I’d call myself a regular at.

theatre elevated!

Everything you want non-musical  live theatre to be (btw Mother Road had a smattering of non memorable music)

But the contrast of the experience made it clear why I left Mother Road at intermission…. And was (in contrast) on the edge of my seat the entire “Lifespan of a Fact” performance

Despite the fact that often the audience is 3 feet from the actors on “stage” at the Aurora …the performances felt real …like you were a fly on the wall …and this was really happening

And like real life…the conflicts don’t get all buttoned up…there is no formula. There are life-like dilemmas with no clear answer… even from the final lines in the final scene

Will I go to a Berkeley rep show again? … prob…
to see a musical…
because there’s a time and place for a feel-good, predictable, formulaic show that teaches a clear inspirational lesson.

But if you want theatre that perks you up and offers a reframing of a society you THINK you understood… stick to the Aurora theatre…and by all means see The Lifespan of a Fact.
Directing, lighting, acting, overall cleverness, realism of script
…and humor under stress!

Great Notion Brewery: Berkeley's Explosion of Flavor and Innovation

Our insatiable thirst for exciting breweries and unique beers led us to Great Notion Brewery in Berkeley, and let me tell you, it was a revelation. Great Notion truly lives up to its name. Their beers are unlike anything you've ever experienced – bursting with flavor, pushing boundaries, and offering something truly special for every taste bud.

Convenience and Comfort: A Smooth Start to Your Adventure

Finding parking in Berkeley can sometimes be a hassle, but Great Notion makes things easy. They offer decent street parking options, and for those who prefer a contactless experience, pay-by-phone parking is readily available. Once you've secured your spot, head inside for a comfortable and relaxing atmosphere. The seating is described as "decent," suggesting a good mix of tables and chairs to accommodate groups of all sizes.

The MVP Hall of Fame: Electric Headband, Over Ripe Fruit, and More!

Now, let's dive into the main event – the incredible beers!  Great Notion boasts a wide range of styles, but your review highlights a few true champions:

Electric Headband (MVP): I can  describe this beer as "to die for" with its vibrant blue color and surprising blue raspberry flavor. A beer this unique deserves a visit on its own!

Over Ripe Fruit in the Can (MVP): This "mango heaven" sounds like a smoothie lover's dream come true. It's a testament to Great Notion's innovative spirit and their ability to create truly delicious and unexpected flavor combinations.

Munchies: This imperial stout takes the cake for intriguing ingredients. Combining pretzels, potato chips, and peanut butter might seem strange on paper, but a "complex" and "soulful" taste hints at a truly unique and satisfying experience.

GR 75: This red tart ale sounds like a delightful burst of tropical fruit flavors. I can mention notes of guava and raspberry, making it a perfect choice for those who enjoy a refreshing and slightly sour brew.

RIPE: As an IPA lover, my declaration that this is "one of the best IPAs I've ever tasted" is high praise indeed. It suggests a perfectly balanced and flavorful IPA that will leave any hop-head happy.

A Must-Visit for Beer Adventurers and Traditionalists Alike

Great Notion Brewery caters to all palates. Whether you're a seasoned craft beer enthusiast seeking the next boundary-pushing brew, or a casual drinker looking for something unique and delicious, Great Notion has something for you. They even offer non-alcoholic options, like the "Black Cherry Cream Soda" – creamy, different, and perfect for those who want to enjoy the experience without the alcohol.

If you're in Oakland or the San Francisco area, you absolutely must visit this incredible gem! The experience is genuinely authentic and refreshingly unfiltered. She has preserved original newspapers from the Black Panther era, creating a rich educational atmosphere. Jill is friendly, knowledgeable, and deeply passionate about sharing the positive impact of the Black Panthers on both local and global communities.

The Black Panther Party Museum, Oakland

As someone who went to Merritt College, I had learned about the history of the Black Panther Party from there. Merritt College has many photos and historical documents there that I wanted to learn more about it.

The Black Panther Party was founded in 1966 by Huey P. Newton and Bobby Seale. They met at Merritt College in Oakland. The movement started out small in Oakland’s Black communities, starting with feeding young children to opening up clinics for people of all ages.

Huey also went to China and met with many politicians and famous people there, the black and yellow community united together and not a lot of history mentions that.

This museum is located in Downtown Oakland, it is pretty small and has another room dedicated to Oscar Grant as well. The museum is free but accepts donations. The staffs were friendly and greets you when you walk in.

Would go again if I’m in the area.

I visited the Black Panther Museum in Oakland today and left with a much deeper understanding of this pivotal movement in American history. Located in the heart of the city where the Black Panthers were founded, the museum does an excellent job of presenting the Party’s full story, not just the imagery most people know, but their community programs, like a complimentary breakfast for children, health clinics, and education initiatives. The exhibits are thoughtfully curated, featuring original photographs, newspaper clippings, and personal artifacts that bring the 1960s and 70s to life. What struck me most was how the museum humanizes the Panthers’ members, showing them as organizers and activists working to address real problems in their communities: poverty, police brutality, and lack of access to basic services. The staff are knowledgeable and passionate, happy to answer questions and provide context. Whether you’re familiar with this history or just learning about it, the museum offers a valuable perspective on a movement that shaped Oakland and influenced social justice efforts nationwide. It’s a small space but packed with powerful stories that deserve to be told. Highly recommend for anyone interested in civil rights history or in better understanding Oakland’s legacy of activism.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

After seeing pictures online of these over-the-top fantasy-esque milkshakes and realized there was a new location in Berkeley, I was very intrigued and finally made my way down. This was a very sweet dessert (almost needed to wash down with water at some point) and we were incredibly full by the end of it, even when we shared it. The flavors were very fun at first, but as we continued, it did get a bit overwhelming and the tastes merged together a bit. The milkshake part ended up being a bit more refreshing than the rest of it. And unfortunately but understandably the price is quite a bit steep for the milkshake, but this was a very complex treat with lots of different components that made it a bit more worth it. The staff was also lovely and helpful in getting utensils and choosing a milkshake.

top_reviews.content:
Our order: kaya toast, breakfast sandwich, salmon eggs benedict, avocado coffee, pandan iced coffee with boba, pandan coconut pastry.

Cute atmo but this was probably the most over hyped food outing we've had in the bay area. I don't like leaving bad reviews but I really don't like getting faked out by misleading reviews, either. Especially when it costs almost $100 with tip.

We love brunch and recently got hooked on kaya toast so we were excited to give this place a go after seeing some hype on social media and the solid reviews.

However, the food... The kaya toast was so dry it was difficult to eat and the flavors were completely indiscernible. The egg on the benedict was not cooked well (the egg white was essentially not cooked) and the hollandaise sauce was flavorless. The breakfast sandwich could have been purchased at your local truck stop--the egg was an unseasoned patty between dry biscuits. The pastry was decent but I think only because our bar was so low by the time we tried it. The drinks were okay but forgettable. This was the type of food I'd expect from a coffee shop that also happened to have a few food offerings, not from a supposed brunch cafe. But neither the food nor coffee was noteworthy.

Such a hidden gem I wish I found sooner. As soon as you enter you’re at awe with the vibrancy of the space.

The service was phenomenal, created and led by a kind and gentle mastermind. The food and pastries were SO delicious.

Don’t even get me started on the coffee. The coconut cappuccino and the Kopi avocado have a grip on me. So yummy I had to get some to go and share with family.

I move out of Berkeley this week and I now look forward to returning and indulging in the exceptional flavors of everything and the colorful space. Wouldn’t be surprised to come back to finding a line down the block to try it.

The barista was so kind to customize the avocado kopi for me bc i am vegan and allergic to coffee (I know lol). She added hot chocolate to the vegan avocado base and it was so delicious! A truly sweet treat. She really didn’t have to do this but went out of her way for me💞🙏

The cafe is very nice and service is excellent but the kopi was disappointing, I am not sure if the milk is stale but the coffee taste old. Our coffee was served on disposable cup instead or glass or maybe they are closing and don’t want more dishes . Not something I will come back again.

I’ve always loved the avocado coffee (Kopi Avocado) at the Walnut Creek location — it was one of my favorites! However, when I recently visited the Berkeley spot (at BAMPFA, since Walnut Creek one closed), I was surprised to receive about half the usual coffee portion for the same price ( I paid $19 for 2 of them with taxes and tips which is extremely high for the amount of coffee I got). I’ve attached photos comparing it to what I’m used to getting.

La Loma Park has two playground areas for older childreand toddlers, baseball field, and half-court basketball court. There is a grill, picnic area, and separate gender bathrooms. There's a pretty good view of the bay.

The two parks are quite nice but are not as well maintained as other parks in the Berkeley Hills/North Berkeley. The public restroom is older but clean.

top_reviews.content: Very cute out of the the way park. Play structures for older and younger kids. Bathrooms are super clean and there’s a nice water fountain. There’s two picnic table and trash, compost, and recycling receptacles.
What a cute little neighborhood park with a beautiful view. I really like the play structure, and there's a bathroom here. The freeway is loud, but if you look around, there's a lot of nature around.

This park is new. It officially opened on March 2, 2018. It has turned an awkwardly shaped and sloped piece of land into a nice neighborhood amenity.

At the time I write this review (March 3, 2018), a fair amount of the park is still fenced off to allow the initial groundcover to take hold.

The biggest attraction will, I think, be the playground structures. There are two sets, 1 fenced and designed for kids under 5, the other unfenced and designed for ages 5-12 (per the signs posted).

I doubt Peggy Thompson Pierce Street Park will become a significant destination for people who don't live within walking distance for the following reasons:
1) It's just too close to the freeway. The freeway dominates all views and contributes significant noise. There is no way that anyone might call this park "peaceful" unless a major accident has stopped all freeway traffic!
2) Unless you have a handicapped placard, parking is on-street in an area that had nearly full on-street parking before the park was built. In other words, I don't recommend driving here!

With that said, I think there are three groups of people who will see this park as a great addition:
1) Families with young kids who live within walking distance
2) Bicyclists using Pierce Street (for whatever reason) as it provides a place to stop and rest a bit
3) Anyone who is nearby and needs to find a public restroom!

top_reviews.content:
The Pardee Home Museum (Italianate architecture) was built by the Pardee family.  Three generations lived lived there from 1868 to 1981.  The last survivor put the home in a trust that is run by a Board of Trustees.  It's self-supporting and run by volunteers.  The father (made money in the mines, was an eye doctor and a California State Senator) and his son was Governor of California who made the poppy flower CA's state flower; reformed prisons;  and established the EBMUD.  All furnishings and collections are original and left intact.  The tour is about 1.5 hours. Tour was educational and interesting - it covers the entire residence of 3 floors.  The tour guide was nice and knowledgeable.  She kept the tour intense so you wanted to know more.  She gave insights and tibits of the family.  All questions were answered.

The afternoon tea is delightful.  The food is prepared from scratch with lots of love from the volunteers.  They were friendly, personable and thoughtful.  Since it was the day before Easter, they put some Easter bunny theme to the tea.  Just lovely people who made a delcious three course of food assortment.

I definitely recommend the tour to learn about Oakland history and to visit one of the last standing historical mansions.  Tea was authentic - no crust on the bread :)

Parse Family Museum was like a time capsule with incredible detailing and collections inside. Our work group was able to secure a private garden afternoon tea with 3 courses of goodies and all the english breakfast tea you could ask for. The women there were lovely and patient with us and even gave us each a thank you gift to take home. Following the tea and treats we took the tour which lasted a little over an hour sharing the homes history across 3 floors of unique treasures and facts. There is plenty parking both free and paid on both ends of the street just not directly out front. The ease of access as you come across the overpass made it all the better to get too! Definitely a place I will return to with family.

TL; DR: Great place to experience a tea party (by group reservation only). Interesting Victorian home museum in which to learn about local history, including that it was home to the first fulltime CA governor. House is chilly in cold months so wear layers, but the dinning room has a space heater during tea. Don't forget to bring cash for the donation box, it'd be appreciated :)
---
I visited here with a group for tea service. The entire thing from the set up, baking, and serving was beautifully orchestrated by friendly museum volunteers who delighted us with a lovely spread of tasty tea and baked goods in the historic home's dinning room.

Tea parties are the home museum's main source of income and a great place to celebrate special occasions or just have an outing with a group of friends. The service is hosted by reservation for groups only. There's a minimum number of attendees required. In the winter the max number of tea guests per party is limited to 12 (the size of the dinning room table). In warm weather, the max is closer to 40 people and its hosted in the patio. Check their website for info.

Our visit was concluded with a docent led tour of the house covering the story of the 3 generations of Pardees who lived there. The family was influential in politics, and was also active in medicine. The house is filled with thousands of family artifacts and collections, including some artwork by the talented Mrs. Pardee. There's definitely plenty to see and learn here.

For the sake of time, our tour didn't include a view of the room with old toys and human specimens (remember that least one Pardee was a physician). If you're curious, you could request a view from the docent. I actually was not aware of this room at all until a fellow tour goer asked about it.

This place hit something very personal for me — a childhood dream of an arcade where you don’t constantly pay per game. It’s a flat fee: you walk in and just play. No tokens, no timers, no pressure.

It works really well for adults and for kids. My wife and I had a lot of fun, and our kids were just as happy. There’s self-serve craft beer for the grown-ups, which somehow fits the arcade atmosphere perfectly.

The design is well done: neon signs, video displays, and a layout that feels intentional rather than chaotic. A few machines were broken, but there was still more than enough to play, and most of the games were in good condition.

The best part was how uncrowded it was. We had the place almost entirely to ourselves for nearly 2 hours as a family, which made the experience feel relaxed and special.

There’s some street parking and there are parking garages all around the area. You pay for a fee for an hour to play all of the machines but the pinball machines are $1 for each game.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

We recently hosted an 8th-grade graduation party at Pixels, and it could not have been more perfect. We had seven families and 53 guests, and the venue was ideal for a group of that size. Even with everyone there, the space never felt crowded, and the fun, energetic atmosphere made it the perfect place for our boys to celebrate this milestone together.

A huge part of our positive experience was working with Rob. From the very beginning, he was incredibly responsive, flexible, and easy to work with. Planning an event with multiple families can be complicated, but Rob made the entire process feel effortless. He accommodated special requests, communicated clearly, and genuinely wanted the event to be successful.

The food was great, the games kept everyone entertained, and everything ran smoothly from start to finish. The value was outstanding, especially considering we hosted such a large group.

Most importantly, the kids had an absolute blast. It was one of those rare events where both the kids and parents left happy.

Thank you, Rob and the Pixels team, for helping create such a memorable celebration. We would absolutely host another event here and highly recommend Pixels to anyone looking for a fun, stress-free party venue.

Prior to the development of the 'Claremont Court' subdivision, a spring at the top of the Garber St. hill flowed down and created a pond here.  It is said that in the summer, local farmers would bring their cattle to wallow in the cool waters.  The famed painter William Keith is said to have painted the pastoral scene.

With the initial mapping of the subdivision in 1906, a water company took over the spring, and a culvert was built, allowing the creation of the park.   It is reputed to be one of the first suburban residential subdivisions in the US.  The subdivision's development took place during the rapid transition from horses to automobiles.The subdivision initially featured a watering station for horses right in the middle of the gates on Claremont Blvd. The subdivision plan called for (coal) gas street lanterns,  but after the earthquake and fire in San Francisco the idea was discarded.  In some places, the abandoned gas lines can be seen in the parking strips.   The developer was also concerned that automobile parking would detract from sales so prohibitions on the number and location on the lot where cars could be parked were instituted.  A frustrated wealthy car collector built a 'spite house' on Forest Ave. just outside of the subdivision gates that features a large round-table on the first floor with chauffeur lodging above.

Sometime in the 1920's a Monkey tree was planted on the park.  Over the decades it grew to be very large.  During the 1960's, neighborhood children would meet at the tree in the evening to play tag and hide & seek.  The tree was 'base' for the games and eventually a large smooth spot developed on the tree from so many small hands clinging to it's safety.     Eventually, the Monkey tree grew so large that the City decided it was a potential hazard and removed it, but the name remained.

Although many believe it to be a 'dog park', it is not.  The park is reserved for cats on Tuesday and Thursday.

top_reviews.content:
Tried the Afternoon Tea at Nudi Blue.
Beautiful presentation served in a glass case, everything felt like a little piece of art.
Great balance of sweet and savory. The blueberry peach scone was soft and fragrant and the tea sandwiches were light and well done. Desserts were refreshing and not too sweet.
Loved the rose and peach teas very aromatic, smooth and delicate.
Overall, a lovely afternoon tea experience. Perfect for relaxing or a cute photo moment.

Currently, afternoon tea is the primary offering at Nudi Blue. It includes a sweet course, a salad palate cleanser, a savory course, and two tea selections. You can purchase their impressive selection of teas and pastries à la carte, too.

The first course was a delightful selection of five pastries. The majority were croissant dough-based, but in different shapes and portion sizes. The guava croissant burst with tropical flavor, and its laminated layers had a good bounce. Pink guava cream decorated the top and filled the pastry.

I quite liked the Earl Grey NY Roll, which was a slice of croissant topped with earl grey cream. I do wish the candied tea leaves had a stronger flavor, but they looked lovely.

My favorite item was the half-moon croissant. The whipped dill cream cheese held its piped shape well. Artful bits of onion flakes and caviar were sprinkled and dolloped on top. That lovely cucumber ribbon and the dill fronds added nice flavor to each bite. I love all those flavors together, but I should note that I may also have loved the half-moon most because it was the most sizable item.

Both of the tartlets—pear and apple with lychee cream and a seasonal combination of citruses—were quite enjoyable, though messy to eat in a couple bites.

After I ate all my crumbs, I was happy to have a small, palate-cleansing salad served next. The vinaigrette was light and satisfying, and the simple mixed greens were boosted by thin shavings of strawberry, rhubarb, and leek.

And then it was time for the savory course, served on a fun glass case containing an artificial terrarium that evoked a creekside walk. I was less enchanted with this course overall. Honestly, I think that’s mostly because the milk bread used for the two sandwiches tasted stale and dry. The bread was toasted for the vibrantly arrayed smoked duck breast and blueberry sandwich, so that dryness was likely intentional. But as the duck itself was also on the dry side, it didn’t work for me. Also, I’m not a fan of blueberry and that is completely not Nudi Blue’s fault. I wanted to try that sandwich regardless, because it looked so inventive.

The cucumber sandwich included herbal cream cheese, a cucumber gelée, and a rauram leaf on top. Its milk bread was untoasted but still tasted dry and stale to me. It was also bigger than it needed to be? That’s odd to say for a tea sandwich, I know. Following my dining companion’s example, I found it more approachable to eat one layer at a time. It felt like too much cream cheese when taking a full bite. I couldn’t help but compare it with the half-moon croissant from the first course, and it didn’t wow like that one did.

The ham and quinta cheese bite, served on puff pastry, was a pleasant option. It went down fast, and I especially enjoyed the pomegranate seeds that added a burst of acidity to contrast with the richness of ham and cheese.

Much like the tartlets, I enjoyed both scones. The orange and jelly-topped scone had bold flavors but did not linger in my memory like the wagyu scone did. The latter wasn’t visually pleasing with just a slice of quinta cheese melted on top. And I was surprised by how few bits of ground wagyu were in the dough. But the richness of that scone was incredible! The texture was perfect, and I could taste the butter in the dough. I wonder if wagyu fat was also incorporated into it to make it taste that good. I would have easily eaten another, with or without the provided butter and honey.

Before the first course, we were given a tray of teas to sniff and decide on for our sweet and savory courses. Many of them are varieties of Thai tea leaves, which were new to me, though some English standards are also offered. Do note that some of the teas on offer are considered premium teas and cost a few dollars more, if you prefer them. As neither my friend nor I are tea connoisseurs, we did not opt for those and were satisfied with what we chose.

So did I enjoy the afternoon tea? Yes! The savory course has room for improvement, but the sweet course was pretty darn delicious the whole way through.

Absolutely fabulous afternoon tea! Friendly service, a cute backyard, delicious food (sweet and savory) and fresh tea. I love the concept and will be back. An extra plus — we are GF and they accommodated!

Super interesting teas with the giant tea being my favorite. First course was phenomenal. We went for the full tea service the third day it opened, and you can tell it’s only going to get better. Ambiance was great with a live piano player and handmade ceramic tea cups per person.

Loved it! Had to try Nudi Blue during its opening weekend, as I love, love, love their sister restaurant, Tanzies. Unlike any other high tea in the Bay Area. Attention to detail in every way, from stoneware to tea selections, to architecture and taste of every sandwich and pastry. Beautiful live piano music serenaded throughout. As with Tanzies, I was made to feel like I was a guest in their house, the service was so warm and welcoming. Will be back soon...

top_reviews.content:
A Diorama Museum for the Commons: Public Art on Derby Street
Tucked along Derby Street in Berkeley, you'll find an extraordinary example of art as civic gift—a collection of handcrafted diorama boxes, each a self-contained world visible through small windows. The "Diorama Museum," as one box announces, presents an astonishing range of tableaux: healthy and bleached coral reefs (complete with didactic labels), prehistoric scenes with dinosaurs browsing among ferns, protest vignettes proclaiming "RESIST NOW!", a glittering proclamation of "THEIA'S FATE," folk art compositions with intricate patterns, and even a rendering of Monterey's Cannery Row viewed through a vintage television frame.
What elevates this beyond mere decoration is the deliberate philosophical stance it embodies. These works aren't gated behind museum admission or gallery exclusivity—they exist in the liminal space between private property and public street, offered freely to anyone who walks by. The artist-family (whom I had the privilege of meeting) maintains these pieces for strangers, for neighbors, for the occasional photographer, asking nothing in return. This is art as democratic practice, as radical generosity.
The craftsmanship reveals hours of labor: layered paper constructions, carefully positioned miniatures, painted backdrops, natural materials, found objects transformed. Each diorama invites sustained looking, rewards attention with detail. They speak to environmental concern, political engagement, local history, natural wonder, and pure aesthetic play.
In an era of increasing privatization and digital atomization, these small wooden boxes mounted on posts represent something increasingly rare: art made deliberately, joyfully, for the commons. They remind us that public space can still be a site of encounter, beauty, and shared humanity—if we choose to make it so.
A delightful little public installation, well worth a stop to add some brightness to your day!

top_reviews.content:
Had a solid experience at Viks Chaat. The food definitely leans very spicy, so be prepared if you’re sensitive to heat, but there’s still good flavor throughout the menu. The setup is more cafeteria-style than a traditional sit-down restaurant, which gives it a casual, bustling atmosphere that fits the place well.

The portions are generous and overall it’s good value for the money, especially considering Bay Area prices. The lamb biriyani stood out as a particularly good deal — hearty, flavorful, and filling. Pairing it with one of their draught lagers worked really well and balanced the spice nicely.

Not the place for a quiet upscale dining experience, but if you want satisfying Indian comfort food with solid portions and a lively atmosphere, it’s worth checking out.

Viks is a great one stop for groceries and Indian home style food.

The lunch thali is great at the price point with tandoori chicken or lamb, a daal, rice and a roti.

The chole bature is great. The chole has some tamarind chutney for that nice sour tangyness and some raw red onions and mango pickle. The bhatura is always piping hot and fried to order.

The tandoori chicken was nice and juicy but you don't get the smoky taste from a tandoor. Daal was nice and home style with not too much butter/ghee.

The dahi puri was cool and refreshing.

The lamb was nice but I prefer goat.

Not much ambience and service is self service.

I love to get mango lassi from the supermarket.

All in all will be back again and again.

Viks in Berkeley is a cool hybrid cafeteria and market. No tipping, super fast service, and the whole place—from the restrooms to the dining area—is spotless. The food leans mostly sweet and sour. The Mango Lassi is basically the Indian version of Mango Pomelo Sago—mind-blowingly good!
The only downside was the first cashier, who looked completely over life. Turns out they forgot my Mango Lassi, which you're supposed to get right after ordering. I only figured it out while waiting for my food when I saw the next cashier hand a drink to another customer immediately.
Overall verdict: Definitely worth coming back.

Overall okay kind of restaurant. Not bad but not good that one can miss. Self service mess type atmosphere, clean your own table, can be huge lines when peak time, food quality is bringing street side flavor but prices are mid scale restaurant.

The Samosad were top notch, followed by Dahi Batata Puri, Bhatura was amazing but Chole could have been little more flavorful. Pav Bhajj and Kathi roll were decent but not very amazing. top_reviews.content: A well-oiled machine for distribution of delicious baked goods.  As a newbie to the bakery, I ended up going in the wrong door and found myself at the coffee station, but what I should have done is follow the line of people waiting for their go at the counter to order.  The morning is peak time for buying baked goodies, and the vibe of the bakery is that the crowd were either locals or (many time) repeat customers.  After the quick progression to the counter from entering, I was greeted by a wall of delicious looking bread of all varieties.  The Asiago olive loaf was my first sampling, and I toasted it to add a little crispiness once I got it home.  The mix of slightly baked onions and olives in the sinewy loaf was amazing, the cheese being a lovely accent.  It made me wish I had bought at least one more.  The scones were the real bread all-stars for me.  The corn-cherry scones were so damned hearty.  The corn meal added an even richer texture to the scone, so I loved it even more, but the crown jewel of the scones was the oat-cranberry scone.  The crust was this and crispy, and the inside was perfectly crumbly and soft.  Definitely buying that again on my next visit.   So many things still on the menu that I want to try.  The cost performance of this bakery is incredible.  The only hassle is parking in the area, which being in Berkeley means it’s going to be awful just about all of the time.  The staff was effective as hell and got me through quickly, but the staff seemed willing to step me through examining some of the offerings, but customer speed did seem to be valued as part of the bread buying experience.
Hands down, the best pizza I had in my life. Every day, they prepare only one kind of veggie pizza. There is always line, but moves fast. Don’t miss it, if you are around.

Finally made it to the Cheese Board Pizza Collective in Berkeley — a spot I’ve wanted to try for years.

They serve one style of pizza a day, and when it’s gone, it’s gone. Today’s slice with baby chard and kale, leek, mozzarella, ricotta salata, garlic olive oil, and citrus zest was fresh, unique, and seriously good.

I’m usually a simple pizza guy, but this one delivered. Absolutely worth the wait. A true Berkeley staple.

Popped in on April 30 and tried the mushroom pizza + salad. They do a different vegan pizza every day. As a huge meat lover, I was surprised by how much I liked the mushroom one. The staff were super sweet and even gave me an extra slice! Also, the salad was so fresh, and that green sauce is so good that I bought a small tub to take home.

Love that it’s a worker-owned co-op with a classic Berkeley feel. Their website is actually super helpful too. You can check the daily pizza/bakery menu and live music schedule before you go.
MUST Visit this place especially if you are a strict vegetarian. You CANNOT go wrong with their quality and hygiene. Be ready to wait for 15-20 mins in line to enjoy the pizza

top_reviews.content: Everything was delicious,  just as our server warned.  I had the fried catfish,  which was served with potato salad on a bed of hush puppies.  The fish was delicate and flaky without being over cooked.  The breading was seasoned but not over-powering. Others in our group enjoyed the buttermilk fried chicken.  Impressed by our mains,  we decided dessert was in order,  so we had the chocolate cake,  which does have a satisfying amount of cayenne- just enough to feel the warmth,  not so much as to be spicy. The rum infused whipped cream was a decadent touch.  The bread pudding was also a hit. Only issue was our server was stretched a bit thin,(surprise post- lunch rush) but he was still friendly and helpful.

I just moved to California recently and I had my first dine in experience at Angeline’s Louisiana Kitchen. I had such a lovely time! Our server, Melody, was very kind and attentive! She checked on us from time to time and made sure we were okay. The food was just as amazing and I can’t wait to go back!! It was my first time trying southern food and I loved it!

Thank you Melody and Angeline’s Louisiana Kitchen! 🩷

I've been here a couple of times now. The first time I had high expectations from having enjoyed great food while in Louisiana.  Angeline's didn't quiet feel the same. It's definitely a great spot in the Bay when craving Louisiana food, but it still doesn't come close to the bold flavors I've had during my visit.

Apart from that, they have very good service and ambiance is cozy as well.

These are just my two cents so take it for what you will. Go check them and see what you think.

Total rip off they super skimped out on the catfish nuggets, I paid $18 for fish batter. It's friggin catfish not like it's a super pricey fish especially nugget form. Never coming back here no wonder it wasn't busy.

This was some of the best food I have ever had!!! I used to work at a New Orleans spot in ATL, and this was top tier! Best hush puppies I have ever had, great sweet tea (for not being in the south) and great service despite it being empty! Shoutout to our server Mel, she was great!!

Delicious pizza! My husband went 6 years ago and now that we are both visiting the area he brought me and I can confirm it's absolutely exquisite! We ordered a Zachary's special. Staff was super nice even on a Monday at 8.30. Will definitely come back soon

Must try the stuffed mushroom and spinach. The crust and sauce are too good to be true!

2 mediums was too much for 2 people but having this pizza for 3 days sounds lovely!
Lovely place and staff!

Overall, we had a positive experience and would definitely return for the delicious pizza. Just a small note on the customer service, which could be improved.
OMG can I say yummy yum yum...wow this place has been in business and keeping their customers coming by the service and food... beautiful

top_reviews.content:
the salads, entrees, and dessert were very well balanced. i love how their ingredients were.

i did prefer the egg for the salad to be a little more runny.

loved the sweet and savory balance of the fig toast and prosciutto

the pasta with veggies did not really do it for me. i felt it was an overabundance of corn and veggie accoutrements, which was distracting.

pork loin was nice and tender. the seasoning for the loin was nicely done.

the olive oil cake was something special. i could taste the olive oil from the cake. nice and fluffy as well

although not in the pictures, the apricot galette was not my favorites. i think the apricot filling was too tart and sweet. it is a tricky dessert to get right, as cooking the apricot will make it even more sweet. I would suggest adding a tad bit of salt to balance the tartness, and sweetness.

The last five years I came here, they used to scrape the bread crumbs off the table for me. this time they did not do it even after we finished the bread and going into the entree round. they finally did it before the desserts.

overall, i applaud the use of fresh ingredients.

Delicious food and great service.  Definitely price and a special occasion kind of place.  We were pleasantly surprised with the small appetizer, dessert tea, and small candies (orange peel and chocolate covered almonds) included with the prix fixe menu!

Had lunch at the cafe -- 3.5 stars, rounded down. It was frustratingly almost great. But IMO for an $80 lunch it needs to be solidly fantastic.

My waiter took long to take my order for main and for dessert. Food wait times were very long as well. Took many minutes for my dessert to come, and it was a slice of galette with a scoop of ice cream.

Baked salmon - Almost incredible. The cook on the salmon was gorgeous. But the flavours and seasoning were just far too subtle for my taste. My first bite was exciting and I was hoping for more, but I felt like the amount of flavours diminished with each subsequent bite. Sadly underwhelming for $47.

Apricot galette - Almost incredible. Overall it was just too tart, even with the ice cream trying to balance things out. The crust was great though.

top_reviews.content: Fantastic authentic jewish and Israeli cuisine in Berkeley! Definitely recommend checking out Saul’s if you are missing your Bubbe in Brooklyn. Of course you are paying for the authenticity ($26 for a sandwich w/ side), but that feels like a given in Berkeley. It is what it is. Don’t let it stop you from coming to try Saul’s. I recommend the corned beef reuben. You can skip the deserts and the latkes (too oily for my taste).
For the real ones, this place is the closest thing to Au Coquelet (shut down years ago). Cozy seating, yummy food, immaculate vibes. A little pricey, though! Also try their flourless chocolate cake.

Large open space, clean, tidy and well-attended. Thursdays there may be a Farmer's Market out front at noon, or one (weather permitting). We happen to be here on one of those less amenable weather days.
One visit only, so no in-depth review here.
Great Bagels and Smoked Salmon.
Well worth visiting and getting to know this place.
Staff are friendly, helpful, and try to keep my modifications from costing too much. The pastry cases are hard to pass up. Rugelach and Hamentashen come in 4 flavors, maracoons 2.
I am not eating everything to report, but the one chocolate Rugelach was dreamy.

I have loved coming to Saul’s for lunch/brunch with friends and family for 10 years. And even with the ownership change, the experience and food remain top notch! The pastrami is the best I’ve had. Get the knish, French fries and pickles. Do not sleep on their Bloody Mary as it is one of the best in the East Bay. Honestly can’t wait to go back

I really wanted to love this place, but the food was sub-par, though I did have a nice and attentive waiter, and the atmosphere was fine.

At least 1/3 of my pastrami sandwich was inedible fat & gristle (see posted pic).  While I never love picking that much fat off a sandwich, I especially didn't love it when the sandwich costs $26.95.  While, I wouldn't call the meat portion skimpy, I also wouldn't call it generous and thickly stacked like, you often get in a traditional Jewish deli, so to have a third of it be inedible was really a waste of money. The flavor was fine, but I didn't pay for a "fat" sandwich.

Also I got a latke for my side (an extra $2.95), and it was very greasy + rubbery and burned (see posted pic of inedible burned portions). It also had a slight fish flavor.  Made me wonder when the last time was they changed their frying oil?

I won't be going back - too disappointing.

top_reviews.content:
La Note is *the* brunch spot in Berkeley for a reason. The patio is lovely, the service was great, and I’ll absolutely be back to try other menu items.

That said, I ordered the Lemon Gingerbread Pancakes with Poached Pears, and my expectations and reality had a brief disagreement.

When someone says “pancakes,” I imagine soft, tender, fluffy clouds that happily absorb maple syrup. These were more like:

* Dense
* Cakey
* Crumbly
* Heavy

The texture reminded me less of a pancake and more of a gingerbread muffin that accidentally got promoted to breakfast.

The flavors were nice, the poached pears were beautiful, but the interior texture wasn’t for me. If you love gingerbread cake, you may love these. If you’re expecting a classic fluffy pancake experience, you may be surprised.

Would I come back to La Note? Absolutely.

Would I order the Lemon Gingerbread Pancakes again?

Not unless they come with a warning label that says:

“Attention: This pancake identifies as cake.”

Really adorable French cafe. Very busy Sunday morning for breakfast, but getting a table inside worked out well for us. Definitely faster than waiting for the patio.

The service was excellent: fun, friendly and attentive.

The food was solid but not incredible. The baguette with goat cheese and honey was delicious, but the breakfast sausages (apple and spicy - I forget the actual names) were underwhelming. The Bloody Mary was spicy and good.

Pricy but good. We’d go back.

Five stars all the way. The breakfast potatoes were crispy and perfectly seasoned, finished with fragrant herbs and mellow roasted garlic that added a rich depth. The scrambled eggs had a light, creamy texture that felt comforting and well prepared. The pear and gingerbread pancakes were not my favorite choice, so next time I would try a different flavor combination with a stronger fruit presence. The atmosphere felt warm and inviting, and the service was attentive and friendly. A lovely spot to relax and enjoy a satisfying brunch experience.
It’s my first time to try French food and I like the taste. The pancake is soft and not so sweet (they provided me with syrup). The oat meal is like a bowl of light sweet porridge, which is ok.

I had eggs benedict and honestly, the highlight for me was the herb and garlic potatoes on the side—so flavorful and perfectly cooked. It’s amazing how something so simple can taste that good. The menu being in French added a nice touch, and the cozy ambiance made it even better, especially with the rainy weather outside. A really warm and satisfying experience overall.

top_reviews.content: It’s an order at cash register and seat yourself atmosphere. The food was mid…. Yuca fries are over cooked and dry… and when i asked for a side of pico de gallo and a small side of cabbage i was charged almost 9$ on top of the 50$ we paid for food. The young black woman was super nice and asked the Latina expeditor about the side and she told her she must charge me for a full salad. Then brought me out a bowl of dry cabbage… couldn’t understand why it was necessary to waste so much cabbage for me to sprinkle a little more green on my already dry food. She also lied and said the cashier started i wanted a bowl of cabbage.  The pico de gallo was also very watery.

Honestly, I’m not sure it lives up to the hype as much as I’d hoped. While the vibe and decor are as bright and inviting as the welcoming staff, the quieted Cuban flavors left me wanting a bit more.

I had the fried pollo cholita plate, but the chicken thigh was overcooked and unfortunately tough and stringy. The beans and rice were excellent though, and I loved the plantains. It’s possible I just got a bad one-off with the chicken, but it still was a miss.

The cubano sandwich was much better, though after recently visiting Miami, I couldn’t help but think it could’ve stuck a better landing.

I know I’ve been here before and enjoyed the tacos, so maybe next time I’ll focus on the more Mexican-forward portions of the menu. Still, Cholita Linda brings a lot of bright energy on Telegraph which is always fun to walk by.

Always looking for great local food when I travel. This was outstanding! Ordered fish, pollo and carne asada. Wow! Juicy. Flavorful. Service was quick and easy. The space was so bright and the back seating area outdoor was perfect of enjoy the weather and food. Highly recommend

top_reviews.content: The thick crust pizza is one of the best if you like tomatoes.  It takes around 30 minutes to cook. Very flavorful and filling.

The menu has many delicious options.  Your can order just one slice or any size pizza you want with a variety of scrumptious toppings. My small mouthwatering pizza  was a hot, cheesy, saucy offering with sausage,  pepperoni,  mushrooms and spinach. There was plenty left over to take home for two more meals. The service staff are super friendly and knowledgeable. The ambiance is great. I loved the artfully pleasing wall decor. The place is super clean and that includes the bathrooms.
This was the first time I dined in because I  usually get take out. But there is spacious seating here that can accommodate any size group.

Forgot to make a review a year ago when I revisited. After a decade, I’m happy to say that the delicious taste of this deep dish pizza is still the same as before! There’s no place like Zachary’s, I highly recommend it. If there thin crust pizzas are anything like I remember, those were also really good. I also love that all locations have art pieces of Zachary’s in different media, it’s very fun and unique!

Supposedly this restaurant has been open since 1983, I’m not sure how they survived for that long if their pizzas were like what we had eaten. The place was still relatively crowded near closing, and was decorated with nostalgic memorabilia. Caesar salad was pretty good but standard and on the heavier side. The two pizzas we got were the thin style Rustic Italian and the Chicago style Zachary’s special. The Rustic Italian had pretty good flavor and I liked the whole garlic cloves, though it could be more roasted. The biggest problem was the crust; it was so granular it almost felt like it could break apart easily, and it did not have that pizza char that it could greatly benefit from. The Zachary’s special was very disappointing, it was filled with basically just canned tomato sauce with very sparse sausage (that was just steamed inside the pizza) and other toppings. The flavor was just sweet and lacked any depth. The crust was even worse on this one, and was just a chore to even finish. The prices for these were also more on the expensive side at around 25-35 dollars per 10 inch pizza. There are many other pizza places you can go to in Berkeley before even considering this one.
Even their smallest pizza good for 2-3 people. Great quality ingredients. They told us how long since some were deep dish. Six people. Everyone loved their choice.

Such great breakfast! the place is clean, spacious and has lots of free parking. Everything on the menu is excellent. Soccoro and Christine are the nicest employees and are great cooks! One of the last affordable and still delicious spots on the Bay Area! They also have great pies, coffee and burgers- but we come for the all day breakfast!!! We love Nations Berkeley!

I had a great experience at Nations in Berkeley. The food was fresh, hot, and exactly what you expect every time — solid breakfast and great pies.

What really stood out was the service. Socorro and Araceli were both incredibly friendly, attentive, and welcoming from the moment we walked in. They made sure everything was correct with our order and checked in to see if we needed anything else. It’s always nice to see staff who genuinely care about customer service.

I’ll definitely be coming back. Thank you for the great experience!
