top_reviews.content:
We stopped by this restaurant late at night, around 10 PM, for dinner. I wasn’t extremely hungry, so I ordered three tacos — though I could only finish two and ended up taking one home. My friend also ordered a few tacos along with a Baja fish taco and another item.

The place has a very casual, chic, student-friendly vibe and offers a wide variety of Mexican dishes on the menu. The food felt fresh and made from scratch, which I really appreciated.

Among everything I tried, the chorizo taco was definitely the standout. It was flavorful, juicy, and perfectly seasoned. I also tried carnitas and al pastor. Usually al pastor is my all-time favorite, but this version didn’t quite match the ones I’ve had in Mexico City. Still, it wasn’t bad by any means.

They had a salsa station where you could pick your own sauces, though I noticed they didn’t offer the usual grilled onions or spring onions that many more traditional Mexican spots serve. Overall, the restaurant felt more like a California-style Mexican place with its own twist rather than a fully authentic Mexican taqueria.

That said, the freshness and quality of the food really stood out. I’d definitely go back, especially for the chorizo tacos. Overall, a really nice late-night food spot.

This is a MEXICAN restaurant. The very  kindest and nicest service. The food is just way off the high end of the charts. The atmosphere... Fantastic. 6/5. Across the board. They have a chocolate horchata that is the best I have ever had.

This place is conveniently located right on University Avenue. The staff is extremely friendly and they offer many homemade items including homemade corn bread, etc. I ordered the steak nachos and they were perfect. Wait times were non existent and the service was very quick and professional. Will be back!

Quick service and sweet staff.
However I felt the legumbres vegetarian burrito could have had more flavor.
The chocolate cake was good but the icing was maybe a touch too sweet.
Husband liked his chicken burrito.
Lovely outdoor seating area.

Great burritos and other Mexican food. They’ve got beer and wine too.
Nice outdoor patio area. It’s screened off from University Ave with plants but you can hear some traffic.
Staff here are super nice and friendly.

reviews_snippets.content: "Amazing Mexican food work a great service and super friendly staff"

top_reviews.content:
I hadn't been to Picante since the remodel so I was looking forward to seeing what had changed. The remodel is fine, definitely more of a modern aesthetic. I remember the food being good but pricey and I'd say now they are closer to being average and pricey. I ordered two shrimp tacos which cost $6.95 each! I was expecting a hefty portion of shrimps for that price. Each taco came with two sad looking shrimps with the rest of the taco being filled with salsa and slaw. I also had an horchata which was fine but it's hard to mess up horchata. I gave it an extra star just for the helpful staff. Overall I was very disappointed with Picante and won't be coming back for future visits with so many amazing Mexican places in Richmond and Oakland.

Recommendation: If you want the most delicious shrimp tacos go to Tacos el Tucan in Richmond, top notch.

The food is great here. The server is fast/average, but the register was is SLOW. They could probably handle a slightly faster pace.

There is a hot sauce refrigerator where you can get three different levels of "hot". Be bold, try the habanero! It doesn't hurt going in or out!

They recently completed a remodel, but unfortunately the atmosphere changed. It seems a bit too "upscale", even if it looks REALLY nice inside and out.

i’ve been coming here for many years and i went again last night with family for a lovely meal.  at first i did not care for the new renovation, and strongly preferred the original picante with red vinyl booths, papeles hanging, viewable tortilla station, etc.  i am starting to better appreciate how nice it now is though in a different way.  we enjoyed our food a lot.  this is high quality food beautifully presented. staff are always friendly and efficient. food comes out so so quick. we have not had to wait in line at the front but even if u do, the food comes out very quickly once you order.  overall id say tho we do miss the old picante we will be returning soon! thanks to the staff for always serving us a beautiful meal. shout out to Alex for his warm hospitality!

It is consistently good. During covid they went thru some changes trying to make things work and come together... They're better now than they ever were! The food is really good! The atmosphere is clean, open, indoor and outdoor seating. The service is quick and efficient. The bathrooms are maintained well. (When that changes, there's a problem).

Picante is one of the best Mexican restaurants in Berkeley. Their food is good and tasty, but it’s a bit pricey, which is why I knocked their rating down a star. Street parking is difficult during most of the day, but there is a small parking lot across the street and to the south about half a block. That often fills up too though. They have a bar and a lot of alcohol to select from and I see people drinking margaritas, but I’ve never tried them. The chips are just so so, they’re thick and a little greasy. I suspect there are some people that like them as they are not the normal chips you’d get in a Mexican place, but they’re just too greasy. The salsas are in the fridge by the door and they are pretty good. Everything else I’ve had here has been good, my favorite are the mole enchiladas, which are probably some of the best mole that I’ve had. They make good guacamole, and good salads as well. If it’s not too cold out, there’s an outdoor seating place.

reviews_snippets.content: "Loud place, but a fun, family-friendly atmosphere and table service."
"Great space, lovely bartenders, delicious drinks and yummy food."
"Great burritos, homemade fresh fried chips, and the best salsa you’ve ever had."

top_reviews.content: Our first time here and it was amazing! Sunday  all you can eat Buffet was an amazing sampler of their delicious food! I really liked the juicey Carnitas and Birria! The Posole was filled with delicious ham hocks (watch out for the bones) and hominy and veggies.

Fun place with great environment.  The food is really good, I had the crispy taco (grilled beef) and it was amazing. The only knock would be, it is a litte too greasy. I also had the street corn, it was good.
Service is really good and fast.
Also I came in a Tuesday which is all you can eat from the taco bar, only $15 and kids under eat free.
You have to try. The Churo desert,  best I've ever had.

Came in on a sunday at 1pm, pretty crowded so i was on a waitlist and was able to get a seat by 2:30pm. No problems with the free parking garage nearby.

Food was solid, i liked the Mole de Mango in particular, probably from the slightly sweeter punch. Would have prefer a thicker consistency of the all the Mole options and  ideally a stronger taste for each. However for the price it's really good

Service was great, the selections were pretty much consistently filled and staff were friendly and helpful

Atmosphere was good, great place for groups of people

Absolutely loved this place. The variety of mole dishes alone makes it worth the visit, and the weekend buffet was incredible. Some of the best carnitas I’ve had. They also have a great selection of dishes like menudo, pozole, rice and beans, amazing Café de Olla, desserts, mezcal, and a variety of specialty drinks.

What really stood out was the hospitality. Our party of 13 was accommodated quickly and efficiently, and the staff was genuinely warm and friendly the entire time. It honestly felt like finding a spot that serves food much closer to what you’d get in Mexico rather than the typical watered-down version. You can tell they care about authenticity and quality.

Definitely a place we’ll keep coming back to, and it’s great that they have multiple Bay Area locations.

The food was just delicious,  had the mango habaneno mole with shrimp 🍤. And ceviche.  Had a brother licking his fingers and not to forget the handmade tortillas omg lost for words.

Don't miss out on delicious food . This place is a must!!

reviews_snippets.content: "Good food, drinks, music, service and atmosphere."

top_reviews.content: We had a great time here. The food was spot‑on: every dish was delicious, even with the classic carb‑heavy pub style menu. Honestly couldn’t find a single fault in what we ate. Service was on the slower side, but the staff were friendly and it didn’t take away from the experience. With screens everywhere, it’s an amazing place to watch the World Cup (or any other sports) and soak up the atmosphere. Would happily come back.

This is a typical touristy sports bar right on the pier. We sat down to watch some sports and it had a lively atmosphere with lots of television screens and plenty of tables and space.
The watermelon margaritas were delicious. Service was decent. Unfortunately the clam chowder was quite watery and not very nice.
It’s a convenient spot if you’re in the area and want to catch a game with a drink, but the food was a bit disappointing.

Showed up here with my fiancé for some quick grub, hoping it was going to be good. Let me tell you, stay away from this god forsaken restaurant. Was skipped about 4 times when waiting for a table, even when they clearly saw us waiting. After being seated, took about 20/25 minutes to even get a water or menus. We ordered the Hawaiian Pizza which came out undercooked, doughy, no meat on it, not to mention the sauce they used for it tastes like air. I hate to be rude but this place is actually horrible and will never step foot in it again.

Great place at the pier! I love the arcade! They have a quite small selection of prizes but the games are really fun! Definitely a must go for children. Prices are OK, i feel like some of the arcade games are a bit pricey but it’s fine. Staff is very friendly and overall a great experience. Food is good, they have a good menu and something for everyone. Defenitely recommend when around in the area. Also a good place to watch sports, they have large TVs.

Saw these fire pit tables while passing by on a chilly October evening and just had to come in. We looked at the menu right outside at the entrance. I saw clam chowder on the menu and was sold. The staff is super cool, service is quick , absolutely loved it - laidback, on point , superb on my scale. Loved sitting by that fire, clam chowder was delicious, but deceiving in size. Happy we stopped here, while in San Francisco. Thank u

top_reviews.content: I would give a much higher rating but I came here to see spacemoth and La Luz and the sound was terrible. The band was visibly pained by it. I had earplugs in and it was still so intense! The bass was so loud it was distorting. And this happened for both bands, so it wasn’t just the musicians’ setup. I have seen other reviews on here complaining about this. I’m not sure what needs to happen to fix this, but if the sound were better I would give five stars. spacemoth forever!!!

This was my first time at this music venue and gastropub. We were only there for the show. The interior was nice and new, though a bit bland. The menu seemed ordinary and I'm not into craft beer. I wasn't familiar with the facilities layout, but I later found that you enter the venue by going to the back of the restaurant and turning left. We only had drinks at the bar inside the venue. It was quickly served. The venue itself is a typical "black box" venue. Just the right size for standing GA shows of smaller bands and legacy acts. We didn't check out the balcony. The biggest negative was the concert started 1.5 hours (show at 8, but started at 9:30) after the scheduled time. The DJ who played during the wait time was okay, but still would have preferred to start on time.

My wife and I brought our son to see Wax, Jarv, and J Lately. We had never been to Cornerstone before so we came early and ate dinner and had a couple beers pre show. I got the Chicken Pot Pie and my wife got the BLT Salad. My son got the grilled cheese and fries. Beer was great, food was great, and Michele the hostess, waitress, runner, security person, was there to take care of us the entire night from beginning to end. She went above and beyond the call of duty for us. We felt genuinely cared for. We will be back for sure. Thank you!

It's a large venue with full bar and restaurant with many screens and projectors around. Great for sport watching, groups, casual hangouts and meetups.
There are big runs for private parties with screen in the back.
Not kids friendly on busy game days but could still be nice on regular days!
Service is great with many responsive attentive staff.
Foods are pretty good American style. I'd recommend burger, fries, sausage, tri-tips sandwich, pulled pork, etc pretty much everything is good after couple pitcher of good beer 🍻😀

First let me just say. This spot has it all. Great food. Awesome bar and socializing locations. Outdoor fire pits, indoor tables, counters, couches. And the music venue location is awesome 😎 And the staff here, is super cool. 🤘🏻😮‍💨💨

top_reviews.content: So today I went into the smokehouse for the first Time. My son goes to ABA therapy around the corner and we decided to try this place. Let’s start off by saying the customer service is amazing. The cashier made us feel welcome. Second of all best milkshake I’ve had in a while. I’m definitely going back to try a different flavor.

For a $7 hamburger, I should not be served with cold staled buns, shredded lettuce that was very sloppy put together.  Other than easy parking, I most likely will not eat here again!  There are plenty of other good eat places around.

The double cheeseburger was laughably small. The patties, not the buns. The patties were completely overcooked and dry. I wonder if I just got a bad batch.Because mine looked nothing like any of the pictures that other people have posted. Also, it didn't come with lettuce, tomato or anything.

Great service, food was not bad...next time will try the burgers..fish n chips were just okay but the fries were super tasty..chili was ok nothing great..shake was good, just not much mango flavor..I do like the vibe though..super easy..family friendly...

An extremely busy restaurant in a beautiful location with incredible panaramic views. The food was certainly good, but it was hard to get an alcoholic beverage because of a large party in the room containing the bar. The staff was stretched thin, but friendly and working hard. Not a place for dinner if you're on a budget. The noise level was incredibly high.

We’ve been here 4-5 times before, and it’s usually our go-to spot for family gatherings because of the wonderful scenery and consistent quality. However, our most recent experience was quite disappointing. The food service was incredibly slow—the tofu didn't even arrive until we were already full. To make matters worse, a young waiter we tried to flag down completely ignored us. We’ve always enjoyed this place, but we really hope the service improves next time

Delicious dim sum and a great view. Perfect for a special occasion. For great quality and flavor, the prices are higher but not as much as some of the fancier places in the bay area. I enjoyed all the standard dumplings shumai (very good), hargow, pan fried chive dumpling, and their crystal shrimp dumpling is delightful! The congee hit the spot too!

It’s definitely a nice spot for dimsum brunch and gorgeous water view. It feels clean and fresh. Food is alright nothing terrible or special about it. We ordered some dimsum and service is pretty standard tasting. Bland for my taste but just right for elders. They seem to let everyone sit by window which is nice. Came on a weekday so it was nice and not rowdy. Would try their dinner menu next time

Very nice Chinese restaurant next to the bay which can see the Golden Gate Bridge by the window. Food was good , drinks were amazing, better make reservation for window table for the view, and if the weather is good, can see the best sunset here

Had lunch with a friend. The mocha and coffee were delicious, the food was fine however quite expensive. The service was not really friendly. The customers who seemed to be regular there were much better attended 😉.
Too cool to eat outside, we opted for a table inside (to be noted the noise level was pretty high).

My dog and I were on a stroll and found ourselves sitting in a comfy, sunny seating area in the front.
The service was great! And the food was exceptional!
While waiting for my order one of the staff took their time to pour some fresh water in a dog bowl for my dog. (Scored major points to me on how awesome this gem in the city is.)
I hope they continue to have great success and maintain their well above average standards.

I came here for brunch and ordered the Ultimate Benedict. It was so good. Never had a Benedict with mushrooms before and it was amazing. Not to mention their house-made potatoes, SO GOOD! Got the organic chai which was ok, more like a holiday drink without much chai but overall flavor was good.

The service is great. Highly recommend this place.

Corned beef hash, coffee, the ranchero. Delicious with filling portion sizes, friendly and minimally intrusive service, great outdoor and indoor seating in quiet neighborhood.

Only qualm is maybe the street parking.

top_reviews.content: During my work trip, I ate here every morning and it quickly became part of my routine. Service was always fast, which made it perfect before starting the day, and the food was consistently great. The home fries especially stood out, they were absolutely delicious and exceeded my expectations. Great food, quick service, and a place I looked forward to coming back to every morning!

Food was pretty good. The syrup was the best. Drawn and kept warm so the drizzle on the toast and souffle was delightful. The place is super busy. I had to wait sometime for the syrup because I got my souffle (takes longer than other food to prepare they warned ahead of time) before the syrup came.

Oceanview Diner was a delightful dining experience from start to finish. I ordered the potato pancakes served with sour cream, house-made applesauce, and a sausage, and every bite was flavorful and satisfying. I also had the chance to sample my husband’s pancakes and my daughter’s potato salad, and everything across the table was consistently delicious.
The coffee was fresh, hot, and the perfect complement to the meal. Overall, a thoroughly enjoyable experience with comforting, well-prepared food. I would happily rate Oceanview Diner an 8 out of 10.

I found this pancake mix yesterday in a pantry of a condo in Florida. Was expecting it to be a couple years old and was shocked to see it's 30 yrs old so I had to look up the diner and read about it's history. The side had an order form for merch that you cut out and mail in with payment. And while I'm excited to eat her pancakes, I think I'll wait till I'm in the area for some fresh ones.

I mean . . . talk about amazing traditional diner. The question is always “would you go back to that restaurant again?!” 100% yes. Worth the wait for sure - latte was superb, omelette with avocado, salsa and sour cream - add bacon - crazy good. Fish tacos - gluten free- awesome! Thanks Oceanview Diner - Happy Memorial Day!

reviews_snippets.content: "Food the size of your face or bigger lol, amazing flavor and service."

name: Great China
address: 2190 Bancroft Way, Berkeley, CA 94704, United States

google.name: Great China
google.address: 2190 Bancroft Way, Berkeley, CA 94704, United States
google.description: Chinese restaurant with a chic, modern atmosphere & a menu that offers Peking duck & other classics.

top_reviews.content:
We’ve eaten at a few Bib Gourmands in the past and we mean it when we say it: this place deserves a star. We had a reservation and the place was so packed it had a line around the block at the opening for dinner service. The wait was about 15-20 minutes from when they opened as they were working quickly to get everyone seated and setup. We were seated at their family sized tables in the back and the service was fantastic. We ordered quite a bit of food since we had a large party so here’s a list of what we got:

Pork dumplings 8/10 - devoured in minutes within our party, everyone loved it.
Salt & pepper spare ribs 10/10 - some of, if not, the best we’ve ever had. Perfect seasoning and chew to them.
Fried rice 9/10 - just delicious, nothing special about it and yet still amazing.
Ginger scallion crab 6/10 - seafood is not really our thing to be fair, but we still did enjoy the meat, the sauce was a bit of a miss though.
Duck bone soup 9/10 - unbelievably good, the cilantro and onion pack it with flavor and the consistency is great.
Broccoli, beef, and string beans 8/10 - a classic just done right, seasoned well and broccoli with a good chew; beef perfect texture and velvety.
Chicken chow mein 10/10 - perfect chew, perfect flavor. Would’ve ordered another if we weren’t so full.
Peking duck with steamed buns and flat bread 11/10 - on this scale an 11 denotes it’s the best we’ve ever had, just in case you thought we failed 1st grade math. Crispy skin and delicious, tender meat.

Great China is undoubtedly some of the best Chinese food we’ve ever had. Add onto the fact that it’s at a better value than other places and it becomes clear that this is a special place. The food itself deserves a star but sprinkle in the service and it begs the question as to why it doesn’t have one. More on the service actually, they were incredibly patient as we ordered many dishes with different requests and were on top of everything from refilling water and tea to removing plates. When the only issue with a place is the parking situation then you know it’s good. (Side note: parking is pretty hard to find and we saw a lot of cars getting tickets for invalid parking so keep an eye out). That shouldn’t deter anyone though as this place might just be worth that fine, half kidding. Do yourself the favor and come here at all costs.

If you come to this restaurant, and I highly recommend you do, keep in mind it is very popular and there will be a wait. The only question is how long. We were expecting to wait a long time, but we got there before it opened on a Sunday, and only waited about 10 minutes. We felt very lucky! We came here in a big group, which is definitely the way to do it because you can get a variety of dishes. Everything was absolutely delicious! The Peking duck was our favorite. But we also liked many other dishes. The only dish that I would say was not fantastic was a fried rice, but that could be just my taste, because someone else actually liked it. This is a really terrific place to come with a group for delicious Chinese food. Highly, highly recommend.

Food is pretty good, though don’t expect authentic Chinese cuisine; this is more Chinese-American food.

The double skin is an interesting dish and definitely worth trying. The walnut prawns are also good, though I’ve had better versions elsewhere. The guo ta fish is a little underwhelming, as it’s just very simple steamed fish with soy sauce, but not very good quality fish.

Portions are fairly decent, but I still found the pricing a little high.

Peking duck is great with pancakes. Pricy but worthy the money. We also ordered eggplant with tofu, sadly was greasy and not impressed. Will skip this dish is possible. Overall, very authentic Peking duck.

This place has the best American Chinese food I’ve ever had anywhere.  The prices are a bit higher than other places.  But well worth it.   Everything always tastes fresh and well made and each visit provides consistency from the last.  The spring rolls are some of the best I’ve had anywhere.   And the steak dishes are always tender which is not always the case as most Chinese food establishments.  Service is quick and efficient.   I’ve never found better Chinese anywhere.  The quality is definitely worth the price.

reviews_snippets.content: "I love 2 skin appetizer, rice sizzling soup, crab meat with buns."

top_reviews.content: Pra ram, pad se ew, crispy pumpkin with peanut sauce, and chicken sate. The pra ram was rich, heavy and outstanding. The crispy pumpkin was awesome. And that was hands down the best chicken satay I've ever had. Big win.

Come for the food and good service! This was my first time here and I always see long lines, but the table turnover is high and so you'll get a table fairly quickly. Everything we had was delicious! Started off with the Tom Kha, Papaya Salad, and Crispy Pumpkin. All SO GOOD! Then we got the Kua Gai and that was so TASTY! Highly recommend!

Imm Thai serves yummy food at a student friendly price point.

The pad see ew was my favorite here. Red curry and Tom kha were also delicious and fragrant.

Ambience is a little cramped. Service is bustling and efficient, but friendly.

10/10 will revisit when in the east bay.

The dining experience at Imm Thai Street Food stands out for its impressive ability to deliver bold, authentic flavors reminiscent of traditional Southeast Asian street vendors. The boat-noodle-inspired dish is a true highlight, featuring a deeply complex, rich, and well-balanced broth that leaves a memorable impression.

The venue itself offers a relaxed, comfortable environment that encourages a laid-back meal. While a full exploration of the menu was limited during this visit due to prior appetite constraints, the quality of the primary dish establishes a strong foundation for future exploration. Given the high standard of execution and the inviting setting, this establishment merits a return visit to sample the broader spectrum of their culinary offerings.

This is the only thai restaurant that I would recommend in the berkeley area. Because of its food being so good its always crowded and needs a weird checking process. I had the fried buttermilk chicken filet with cole slaw on French roll (fancy way to say chicken sando 🤣). The bread was fluffy with every bite, and the flavor palette works really well between the classic well-seasoned chicken patty and cole slaw combo.

To be nit picky, the proportions are a little off:
1. There was too much bread for the amount of meat and coleslaw. The cole slaw could be kept better in the sandwich if it was more finely chopped. Going from rough to fine chops allows the slaw to be more flexible (like solid to liquid) and fill out the inside volume of the sandwich instead of constantly falling out of the sandwich.
2. While the chicken was perfectly salt-and-pepper seasoned, had a nice crispy crust, and looked appetizing, it's skinnier cuts relative to the wider roll left more savoriness to be desired. Butterfly-style cuts can help produce wider chicken slabs increasing surface area-to-volume ratio enabling the display of more of its flavor.

The real thing that'd discourage me is the price and not enough seating. My friend and I paid half a benji for 2 sandwiches and potato balls that we couldn't enjoy until we got home.

Again, the above are nit picks, and wouldn't discourage me from eating here again! In fact, I'm writing this review in hopes that my feedback is valued to make the chicken sando better than it already is. :) The potato puffs are 🔥!!! And the server peeps were super friendly!

After placing our initial order, we didn't see our server for 45 minutes (time stamped, yes). When we wanted to order more food, we had to ask the food runner to find someone. Even then, it took another 15 minutes before someone finally came to take our order.

No one refilled our water even once, and no one checked in to see if we needed anything. We saw servers refilling water at other tables, but they never came to ours. Servers were basically nowhere to be found, to the point where when I finally saw one closing out another table, I handed her my card before she could run away because I was worried she'd disappear again and we wouldn't be able to pay for another business day.

We added a bottle of sparkling water to our bill before closing it out but it wasn't brought out until we were waiting at the door ready to leave, that was also after when we had to ask again for it.

At no point were we acknowledged for being ignored. Nothing like "It's busy tonight" or "We're short staffed". We would've understood if there were special circumstances, but we received nothing aside from what felt like attitude and impatience from the waitresses. (God bless them, hope they had a better night than I did)

The experience left us speechless. For a place where per-person spending is $100+, the service was shockingly bad (although is it really "bad" if it were nonexistent?) The menu deserved better service. Just stick to DoorDashing or takeout.

Hopefully others won't have the same experience we did.

Edit: The owner kindly reached out to us in regard to our experience. We appreciated the effort from their end to better the situation and improve their quality of service.

top_reviews.content:
BLAND FLAVORLESS NOTHING
Can't recommend this place.

Let me make this clear before I continue. The staff is great, they were totally cool with me, friendly and helpful. This has nothing to do with the staff or how they prepare the sandwiches.
The ingredients IB's is using are substandard. I've worked in the restaurant business for 35 years and I know, when substandard ingredients are being used.
The sweet peppers have no flavor at all, the cheese has no sharpness, the buns are bland and the meat is either under seasoned or just doesn't have a lot of flavor. These are the hallmarks of restaurants that source all of the ingredients from one company and the company kind of just throws them together to make a profit.
I drove 50 mi, because I had heard it was a great cheesesteak, and I am a fanatic for great cheesesteaks, and got a large one to share with my buddies, and what I got was a bland, bland, bland. No flavor, no sharpness, no cut.
You know that when a cheesesteak is properly constructed and still has no flavor, it has nothing to do with the staff, it has to do with where the owner is sourcing the ingredients from, and the ingredients suck. Okay I feel bad for the staff there, having to work with those ingredients. It's probably going to cost them in the long run, because cutting corners like that, will lessen your business in an area where people want strong flavors.
Anyway the staff was totally cool, I didn't mind the price for the gigantic sandwich, but the experience was just boring, and bland, and no flavor.
Anyway, I wish I could send a better report, I hope they do better maybe I'll give it another chance at another time, but probably not if it's going to be like this.
I'm sure the management is going to respond to this with some cookie cutter response, not taking responsibility, because people that take responsibility for their food, don't work with food like this. It looks like they've gotten in trouble with dozens of people before, and apparently the sale from the old owner has resulted in not only poor quality ingredients, but also poor quality responses.
Stitch incoming 3.2.1

They make a damn good hoagie picked one up while I was in the area.

Great service and easy to order. You know the ingredients are fresh and ready to go.

Parking is a bit of a hassle but there's street if you could find it or a parking structure nearby.

Tips: Order online and skip the line! (All orders are quoted 15 minutes per the site as it doesn't provide you pick up time upon confirmation). Then, walk across the street and get yourself a refreshing tea from Feng Cha!

Got late night munchies or simply need some comfort food to satisfy your cravings?  This is the place for you!

We arrived on a Saturday night and the shop cannot be missed as there is a crowd of people hovering the shop.  As it was our first time here, it was hard to determine where is the ordering line since there are a lot of people crowding by the counter waiting for their food.  The staff who is taking orders is also packing snd calling out pickup. And that is when I check and realize you can place an online order.

There are varies cheese steak sandwiches with different toppings.  The best part is you can customize the sandwiches by selecting your protein choice (beef, chicken, or halal lamb).  Then you got "the work" which is grilled onions, cheese, mayo, mustard, lettuce, tomatoes and hot sauce).  Again, all customizable.

In addition to the traditional chessesteak sandwiches, they have burgers, fried chicken, and fries.  As a person who loves curly fries and tots, I was very happy that you can choose your fry types: Onion Ring, regular fries, waffle fries, curly fries, and Taylor tots. Mind blown! 🤯

The sandwich tasted amazing and in a huge portion. especially late night munchies.  😆 We opted for BBQ chessesteak and mushrooms cheesesteak.  The mushroom one is the winner for me!   The only thing I didn't like is the sandwich probably sat longer than expected and the steam soften the bread which becomes mushy to my personal preference. Otherwise, the flavors are great!

Couple things: When ordering online, you have to enter your street address which I find extra....
Parking is a challenge as the shop is located on the busy Durant Ave.  If you can, walk.  Otherwise, be aware when you double park...

Popped in and saw a combo (adding fries and a drink) to your $16 burger is an additional $7.. walked out and Went to Zydar Mediterranean next door. You’d think UC Berkley students were smarter than spending $26 (including tax)on burger and fries lol. Pure greed
It's a takeaway place. Prices might seem a bit high but the food quantity is also good. Prepare to be stuffed!

top_reviews.content:
I came here after going to Marufuku in walnut creek and having the absolute worst ramen of my life. I had to get that garbage taste out of my mouth.

Ramen shop accomplished that mission. The ramen egg was eggcellent. It was fully seasoned with a cured yolk. If you zoom in on the egg you can tell the texture of the white wasn't perfect but I think that is just part of making them in mass quantities for a restaurant.

The noodles were very good. Good texture and good snap. The broth was creamy and rich. I ate everything, including the soup.

I very much enjoyed that it looks like they took a torch to the chashu to give it a good charr which elevated it to another level. Really made it stand out from other chashu at other ramen shops.

Definitely recommend eating here. Some of my favorite ramen in the east bay.

Phenomenal chicken shoyu ramen and black sesame ice cream sandwich. Also not pictured but ordered tempura veggies and pickled cabbage to share, great apps!

Also would like to highlight the outstanding service from Alicia! She checked on our table several times after ordering and was very warm and polite.

All in all, one of my favorite ramen places in the east bay!

We sat at the counter. Watching the cooks prep dishes was very interesting. They had a good flow and good communication while working very quickly to get dishes out. We ordered crispy full belly bintje potatoes to start - it was served piping hot so be careful. The potatoes were perfectly crispy on the outside and creamy on the inside. The curry sauce was mild enough for me to handle. The pickled carrots had a crisp freshness to them.

I had a Under the Cherry Moon mocktail with Hokkaido miso ramen. I also tried a bite of the Liberty Farms duck shoyu ramen. Everything was highly flavorful. The noodles had a good bite to them. The ratio of noodles, toppings, and broth was just right. And no cheap bean sprout fillers.

We had an incredible experience here! Finding a place that pairs top-tier food with a genuinely welcoming environment for families can be a challenge, but this spot nailed it.

The Food: The vegetarian/vegan ramen was absolutely delicious. It was rich, deeply flavorful broth, perfect noodles, and beautifully prepared toppings. It's easily some of the best vegetarian/vegan ramen around.

The Vibe: Exceptionally kid-friendly without sacrificing the great atmosphere.

The Service: What really blew us away was the staff's incredible hospitality. They went above and beyond to make our kids feel special, even turning a simple drink order into a small theatrical performance to ensure it was poured exactly 50/50 between two cups.

Fantastic food, wonderful team, and an all-around great spot for parents and plant-based foodies alike. We will absolutely be back!

Returned after 11 years away and this place truly crushes it. Get the fried rice every time, as an extra item... You'll thank yourself. The ramen is superb, love watching the kitchen team work their magic.

Crepevine has a cozy, inviting vibe and a menu packed with variety—crepes, pastas, salads, and more. The food is solid and satisfying, with generous portions and fresh ingredients. I’ve tried both savory and sweet options, and everything has been consistently good.

That said, nothing really stands out as exceptional. It’s tasty, but not memorable. For the price point—often $18–25 per plate once you factor in tax and tip—it feels like you’re paying a bit more than the experience delivers. The ingredients are fresh, but the flavors are pretty straightforward, and the presentation doesn’t quite justify the upscale casual price.

Still, the service is friendly, and it’s a great spot if you’re in the mood for variety or need something crowd-pleasing. Just manage expectations—it’s more of a convenient comfort food spot than a culinary standout.

top_reviews.content: Great experience at Marugame Udon! The udon was fresh and chewy, the broth was flavorful, and the tempura topping was crispy and delicious. The drink was refreshing as well. Service was fast and friendly, and the restaurant had a clean, comfortable atmosphere. I would definitely come back again.

8/10 (this location) | 9/10 overall

How can you go wrong with Marugame Udon? Seriously. It’s one of those spots that just hits every time. This location gets an 8/10 from me—still solid, still satisfying—but overall, the brand is easily a 9/10 because it’s just sooooo good.

If you’re going for the first time (or even if you’re not), do yourself a favor and get the beef or nikutama. The broth is rich, savory, and comforting, and the noodles have that perfect chewy texture that makes every bite worth it. It’s simple food done really well.

And don’t skimp on the tempura. That’s where people mess up. Load up your tray—shrimp, sweet potato, whatever catches your eye. It’s crispy, fresh, and honestly half the experience.

Quick, casual, and consistently delicious. Hard to miss here.

Now that I’m done with UC Berkeley, I can confidently claim that this has always been a very tasty ramen restaurant. I would go here whenever I had in-person campus visits. The thick vegan noodles with carrots, broth, and cabbage are very delicious.

My son attends UC Berkeley, so I come to Berkeley at the beginning of each semester. This time, he took me to Marugame Udon, and it was such a great experience. The food was simple, fresh, and delicious, and I loved the whole concept. There’s nothing like this where I live — definitely one of the best!

It is a great spot for comforting and authentic Japanese food. The udon noodles were freshly made, thick, and perfectly chewy, and the broth was light yet very flavorful. I appreciated being able to customize the bowl with different toppings, which made the experience fun and satisfying. The service was fast and well organized, even when there was a line, and the prices were reasonable for the quality and portion size. A solid choice for a quick, delicious meal if you’re craving udon in Berkeley.

top_reviews.content:
Some restaurants simply serve food. Others create an experience. This place belongs firmly in the second category.

We arrived around 6:00 p.m. and were pleasantly surprised by the efficiency. Despite a growing crowd, the wait was only about 10 minutes before we were seated. From the moment we walked in, it was clear this restaurant runs like a well-rehearsed orchestra. Every member of the staff seemed to know exactly where they needed to be, creating a smooth, welcoming atmosphere that immediately sets the tone for the evening.

The restaurant itself is spotless, modern, and full of energy without ever feeling chaotic.

The menu is extensive—but in the best possible way. Instead of feeling overwhelming, it feels like an invitation to come back again and again because there’s simply so much worth exploring.

Every dish that arrived at our table was memorable. The pork belly was outstanding, cooked with that perfect balance of crispy edges and tender, juicy meat that almost springs back with every bite. The cheesy noodles arrived still bubbling with heat, rich, comforting, and packed with layers of flavor. What impressed me most wasn’t just how good each dish tasted, but how every ingredient held its own while contributing to the bigger picture. Nothing disappeared into the background. Every bite told its own story before coming together in perfect harmony.

A few Korean soju shots, a couple of cold beers, great company, and incredible food turned dinner into one of those evenings you don’t really want to end.

As the night went on, the restaurant filled to capacity, and after eating there, it wasn’t difficult to understand why. Great food, attentive service, fair prices, and an atmosphere that makes you want to linger a little longer.

Some restaurants leave you full. The best ones leave you planning your next visit before you’ve even paid the bill.

This is absolutely one of those places, and I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it.

We were seated immediately for a late Monday dinner. We ordered the spicy rose rice cakes and bulgogi. The banchan was served right away after we ordered which was great. Service was good all around from start to finish. Highly recommend when you’re in the area!

I really wanted to try Blood Sausage Soup after hearing my friend who just came back from Korea, say she had it three days in a row. Luckily, I found a place tjhat serves it!

I ordered the Spicy Blood Sausage Soup, which came with blood susage, broth, offal and meats. I would say the blood sausage had a really interesting texture, chewy but soft at the same time. I don't fully get the hype around it, but the flavor was really good!

We also tried the Spicy Stir-fried Octopus & Noodle, which tasted really delicious. it came with lots of small octopus and shrimps, and the flaor was enhanced by Bonito flakes and sesame oil, giving it a really unique taste. I would highly recommend this dish!
I ordered the beef soup. I was nervous at first but this soup was bursting with flavor. Primed with kim chee and topped off with ice water. Definitely coming back.

This was my first time here the and I was looking for soup and Bossam. The Seol Leong Tang was good and tasty and the Bossam with Garlic was a huge portion, but the garlic was a bit overkill for me. The garlic tasted very mild in flavor and slightly sweet. Nor what I was expecting, so I should have ordered the regular Bossam. It was a good experience overall.

name: Belotti ristorante e bottega
address: 5403 College Ave, Oakland, CA 94618, United States

google.name: Belotti ristorante e bottega

top_reviews.content:
Belotti Ristorante e Bottega in Oakland is a must-visit destination for anyone looking for authentic Northern Italian cuisine in the East Bay. The kitchen operates with a level of precision that is rare to find, and the consistency from start to finish is excellent.

The handmade pasta is the clear highlight of the menu. Their Casoncelli, prepared Bergamo-style with beef, prosciutto, pork shoulder, and Grana Padano, is a masterclass in balance. The dough is rolled perfectly—thin and delicate, but with enough bite to stand up to the savory butter and sage sauce. The addition of chewy smoked pancetta adds just the right amount of texture to the dish.

For starters, the Uovo Asparagi e Tartufo is a standout and a great example of layering textures. The egg has a perfectly crisp exterior that yields to a rich, molten yolk, and they aren't shy with the fresh truffle shavings. It’s an earthy, savory dish that works incredibly well with the fresh asparagus and creamy, savory fonduta underneath. The Vitello Tonnato—slow-roasted, grass-fed Piedmontese beef with a delicate yellowfin tuna sauce—is equally precise, with the caper essence and lemon zest providing a bright, clean finish.

Even while dining in the outdoor parklet, the experience was great. It’s well-designed and comfortable, making the most of the natural light while keeping the atmosphere quiet and enjoyable. I also appreciated that they serve imported Italian MoleCola rather than standard sodas; it has a crisp, refreshing bite that cleanses the palate effectively between heavier courses.

Dessert service was exceptional. The Affogato al Caffe is excellent on its own, but adding a splash of Grand Marnier gives it a sophisticated, citrusy complexity that pairs perfectly with the espresso and vanilla gelato. The Bunet Piemontese was also a highlight—a rich, velvety pudding of cocoa and crushed amaretti cookies, encased in a 60% dark chocolate shell and topped with soft, unsweetened whipped cream. It is intense but not too heavy, which is exactly how a dessert like this should be.

There isn't a weak link in the experience at Belotti. It is officially one of the best spots in the East Bay for anyone seeking high-quality, authentic Italian food.

Fell in love with this place. Everything was so delicious. I rarely eat Northern Italian food. The flavors were such a treat. The weather was perfect for the parklet outdoors. Everything combined for a perfect meal. Can't wait to come back!
Great food and good service. The bread in the beginning was hard and crusty. The tiramisu was very 3/5 at best. Pasta dishes were excellent and memorable, worth going back for.

Wonderful neighborhood restaurant with the perfect vibe. Their pasta dishes are divine and made with love... Michelin style dishes without being pretentious. I'm so impressed with the dishes that they pump out of that tiny kitchen for the amount of tables they support inside and outside. Big claps to the chef and staff!!

We had an incredible lunch at Belotti Ristorante in Rockridge, Oakland. We tried the Pappardelle Al Funghi, Spaghetti Pomodoro with Burrata, Bruschetta, and Panna Cotta for dessert. Everything was outstanding, but the Pappardelle Al Funghi was truly unforgettable – rich, earthy, and perfectly balanced. The panna cotta was divine!
Staff is welcoming and service is great.

The service was mediocre at best, with no complimentary refills offered on soft drinks, and the burrito itself was noticeably smaller than what I’d expect for that price.
For the same money, I can get a more generous portion at Chipotle just down the street, with free refills included. Given the combination of high prices, small portions, and lackluster service, I’ll be eating at corporate America owned Chipotle next time. top_reviews.content:
Ippudo is the closest you'll get to authentic Japanese ramen in the states.  The price is average to high, but its definitely worth it.
If youre eating ramen, save enough broth to do kaedama (its free)!

Parking in Berkeley is a bit tough, so I would recommend parking a little ways away and walking 5 mins or so.

We reserved a table for 7 a day before but when we got there in time, we still have to wait a whopping 20 minutes. On top of that, the portion size was not generous (little soup which is extremely salty because there was no liquid, basically no meat, and no toppings). I feel like I am basically spending 20 dollars for just a bunch of plain noodles. I would not recommend this place at all.

Ippudi's hakata ramen is the best I have found outside of Japan. Always consistently good and made with quality ingredients. Our table was not cleaned well and the condiments on the table looked old and the containers looked like they needed to be cleaned, hence the reason for my 3 and 4 stars on the service and the atmosphere.
Pictures says it all: Ramen egg was served with a gigantic hole. I understand that eggs have variations but even at home if I open an egg that looks like that, I would never serve it to my guests.

Food: OK, solid for US ramen. Nice to be able to get Hakata style. Broth was solid, presentation was lacking but not terrible. As lunch, this bowl of ramen did not leave me feeling disgusted at the amount of food and oil consumed, which I think is a failing in the world of ramen. It lacks the carefully put-together excess that should be present.

Price: too high. Without adding the $4 egg, my $17 bowl of ramen was fairly simplistic and the portion size didn't feel like a serious indulgence the way ramen really should. I think this is one of the better options for ramen I've had in the bay, but as with most US ramen, the value is just not there and this value is worse than some other very solid I've had in the area.

Atmosphere and Service: Nice, clean restaurant with attentive staff. The disposable chopsticks are cheap and do fray - not the end of the world. A few hand-trucks of ingredients came through the front at about 1pm - also not a big deal, but did have to interact with that on my way out. Overall very pleased with the atmosphere and service, no strong complains or issues. The Japanese menu wall art is a nice touch.

Overall: For me personally, I probably won't come back, but if you're into the local ramen scene you'll probably enjoy this spot.

top_reviews.content:
An ok 3.5 / 5 experience.  Rounding up to 4 🫥

I understand that carrots and zucchinis in your taco burrito can throw people off. On the other hand if you want more veggies in your Mexican food, this place would be a blessing. I think they should do bell pepper and onion fajitas, instead of carrots and zucchini.

Overall, under spiced and missed the mark flavored, but freshly made, which is always nice.

I did wish they grilled their burritos like many other Mexican places. Or just generally made it less soggy and wet.

Perhaps this place is more suited for people who don’t want as many spices in their food and don’t have a pepper tolerance

They do have a little kids plate for $6.50 which is nice. Seating space is very limited so take out is advised.

We’ll probably give this place another shot for their tacos, but not for their burritos

A classic, awesome burrito place, I’ve been going to Gordo’s for 20+ years. Simple, delicious ingredients, fast service and friendly staff. Love it!
A little tight space and light on the seating but still a cool vibe.

Just like another reviewer, I had started with Gordo’s on Clement St. when I moved to East Bay, the college Ave location was the tops.

It had been 20 years since I was in the Bay Area, and was so happy to nothing changed.  Just delicious burritos.

I think Gordo’s secret is steaming the tortilla with the cheese.  Get it all melt.

I hope it won’t be another 20 years; but if it is Gordo’s: please don’t change. 👍👍

In response to some of the other reviews:

The pollo asado is the best I’ve ever had—perfectly cooked. If someone is afraid of, or confused by, blackness on their chicken, may I recommend Chipotle.

The moisture in the burritos is part of the excellent cooking. The beans are perfect, every time, and this means that they are perfectly moist; as is the salsa, the meat, and the rice. All perfect, every time. So, yes: you won’t get a super-dry burrito, and yes, this means that if you insist on taking it home, it may degrade slightly in structure (it will be perfect if eaten in-taqueria). My friends and I have been eating these burritos for over twenty years and have enjoyed many a one at home, just a little wetter. It’s worth it to have perfectly cooked ingredients.

Atmosphere. Let’s talk about atmosphere. This is one of the last  not Starbucked, not third-wave-coffee-housed joints left in the Bay. If you’re uncomfortable with the small space or old-school tables and chairs, then, again, allow me to recommend Chipotle. Or Taco Bell. How about Taco Bell? They keep their revolving-door A.I. market image updated every few months. You shouldn’t be bothered by any authenticity or lasting tradition there.

Bottom line: Gordo Taqueria is a Bay original. So many old authentic Bay Area eateries have been bought out, disappeared, or made unrecognizable. Please let Bay Area natives enjoy this one in peace before we flip every last space into a Tesla showroom.

I am sorry to hear about poor customer service, if it’s true; and to hear that long-timers have experienced bad food service. I hope that everything is going Ok for the owners and staff during a weird, tough time in the Bay and the world. Customers do have a right to demand civil treatment and continued quality.

We went on a Friday morning (keep in mind they are closed Monday through Wednesday, so plan accordingly when you want to go buy these pies), and while the lines were a bit long, the line wasn't too bad, and they went rather quick.

Me and my friend got the banana cream pie, and the key lime pie. I love how tart the pies were -- the banana cream was so layered, made with actual banana and it was topped with another layer of cream and chocolate covering. All in all, $7 a slice for a piece of pie is not bad at all, especially if they were made by food artisans who knew their craft.

Ambiance is rather good, and not underwhelming at all. This place IS worth the hype forsure xD

I'm definitely recommending Bakesale Betty to any and all friends who want to try this :)) till we meet again!!

top_reviews.content: Arrived about 3:10pm, after lunch before dinner service, not a full menu available. I tried their pastrami sandwich which was really tasty and fries. Everything was good. Nothing blew my socks off though. Will be back to try dinner. Make your reservations ahead of time, the place is small, I thought it would be bigger. Some paid parking available along the street.

Food is 5 stars for flavors and presentation and the cocktails are quite tasty too. We had the potato fennel soup and Brussel sprouts to start. The soup had a surprising  kick and the sprouts had bite from the apple and acv that made them totally pop.

One of our entrees was the pork chop with seasonal veggies, a grilled peach and sausage bites. Each component on its own was a burst of flavor but when you put them all together it was a true flavor explosion. This sausage bits we amazing!

Our other entree was the half chicken with roasted potatoes, which also had great flavor and again when the components were eaten in one bite, the combination was fantastic. The sauces on both dishes did their job and brought the dishes together too.

For desert, we chose the profiteroles with seasonal fruit and ice cream and that was a great way to end the meal.

We may have caught them on an off night, but service was a bit slower than we prefer - was just over an hour from being seated to main course, but the food was worth the wait.

It was a clean restaurant too, but could use some sound baffling to make conversation a bit easier. We were seated in the center of the room and found it a bit noisy.

We will definitely be back again!

We got to the Oakland restaurant right before they opened for lunch and were greeted warmly by the staff. They gave us our choice of a table right by the window or a spot further inside the dining room. We picked the window, which turned out to be an awesome people-watching node while we looked over the lunch menu.

Our waiter was incredibly friendly and helpful. We ordered the pastrami sandwich and the hot pork sandwich, telling him we planned on splitting them. When we asked if they came with fries, he mentioned they usually come with coleslaw, but he kindly let us swap out one of the slaws so we could try the french fries too. A short time later, the kitchen went completely above and beyond—they brought our food out pre-split on four separate plates. Getting a perfect half-sandwich, fries, and slaw delivered right to each of us without us having to messily cut them at the table was a really kind, thoughtful touch of hospitality.

Starting with the sides, the fries came out piping hot, perfectly crisp, and well-seasoned. They tasted great with just standard ketchup.

As for the best pastrami sandwich in the East Bay contender? It completely delivered. The meat itself was deeply savory, perfectly cured, and piled high on a phenomenal, crusty baguette from La Farine bakery. The Dijon-horseradish dressing gave it a great, sharp kick that cut through the richness. It’s an absolute triumph and entirely worth the trip.

The hot pork sandwich, however, hit a weird bump (3/5 stars for this one). As I picked up my half, the first thing I noticed wasn't the sharp, bitter scent of broccoli rabe, but a strong smell of cooked spinach. When I took a bite, an overpowering spinach flavor totally took over the palate, completely masking the taste of the pork. My partner noticed the exact same thing. I opened up the baguette to check it out, and while there were a few actual pieces of broccoli rabe, the main culprit was a dark green, long, stringy mass. I ended up scraping most of it off. When I isolated the pulled pork by itself, it was actually delicious, tender, and beautifully seasoned, and the bread was excellent. But with that heavy cooked spinach smell and taste, I just can’t recommend the pork sandwich in its current state. It completely ruined the sandwich for me.

Overall, between the flawless service, and the great tavern atmosphere, Wood Tavern is easily one of the top places for a pastrami sandwich in Oakland.

Probably the best New American restaurant in the East Bay. Their steak never misses—perfectly cooked, delicious, and big portions. Rotating dinner menu (except steak and pork chops) and even the veggies included differ depending on what they have available. The scallops and risotto are always so good when it’s on the menu. Bonus: complimentary bread and butter.

It’s always packed and busy, even on weekdays. It’s been a local staple in the piedmont area. And it’s really the only new American restaurant that I find myself revisiting!

top_reviews.content:

This place has been on my want to go list for a while, and I finally got to try it! We didn't make a reservation and walked in instead. We waited for about 30 min and the restaurant texted us once the table was ready.

We ordered quite a few dishes and started with Omakase gushi, which came with chicken breast, thigh with leek, heart, cartilage, and minced chicken.  We also ordered the oden set, sasami, tori tataki, gyu-tan, enoki bacon, and buta bara.

Evertyhing tasted pretty good, but the most impressive dish was sasami with umeboshi, which was inner bresat with umehad was the inner breast with umeboshi. It was my first time trying raw chicken, and it tasted really good. The chicken breast was really tender, with a tuna-like texture, and without any slimy or odd flavors. Ever since then, I've been telling my friends to try it. The Tori Tataki was seared chicken breast sashimi with ponzu, which tasted a bit plain compared to the sasami. So  I would highly recommended to get theeir sasami!
Wow!!! i loved this place - great food, great atmosphere- about as japanese as you can get outside of japan - wish i lived closer so i could eat here all the time!! seriously worth going to.

Ippuku (一服), which means to take a short break for a cigarette or tea during a busy day (literally meaning “one dose”), had a very nice vibe walking in. The entrance was unassuming, but the interior transported me back to Japan. They had seating areas which simulated traditional seating on zabutons and tatami maps, and also more western style sitting areas. You can immediately tell they take pride in Japanese tradition without becoming pretentious or trying too hard to be "unique".

They gave a complimentary chunk of cabbage with kewpie mayo topped with togarashi. While pretty difficult to eat since it is just a large chunk of cabbage, it was a very nice palate cleanser throughout the whole meal. We ordered four skewers: Gyutan (beef tongue), Kurobutabara (pork belly), Negima (thigh with leek), and Kawa (skin). Additionally, we got the Ikasumi chahan (squid ink fried rice) and Kani korokke (dungeness crab creme croquettes).

The squid ink fried rice, while pretty good, was the biggest disappointment. It tasted like a standard rice that can be made at home, but colored with squid ink. The squid ink felt more like a gimmick that made my tongue and lips black after eating a few bites. The crab croquettes were very solid, a nice structural integrity and creaminess one bitten in. The crab slivers were noticeable and added a nice sweetness and crabby flavor overall. The sliced cabbage under them was a good palate cleanser too.

The skewers, specifically the yakitori, was their advertised specialty. Starting with the beef tongue, it was slightly thick, but cooked perfectly. It had a nice bite whilst not being too chewy, and the charred jalapeños provided a good spice that broke up the pieces of meat. It was also seasoned nicely, without need for a sauce. The chicken skin was my least favorite of the skewers. While the outside had a good crunch, which I love in chicken skin, the inside became very soggy and chewy. I would have preferred them to not be in skewer form, and to just be fried as whole skin pieces. The chicken thigh was very impressive. With a thin coating of sauce, the chicken was succulent and juicy, very flavorful, and the leeks provided a nice textural contrast as well as a freshness. This was a very impressive skewer that I would definitely get again. The pork belly was my favorite bite of the night. It was both juicy and had nicely rendered fat. It was a very meaty taste, accentuated by the simple seasoning of just salt and letting the charcoal flavor come through. The sauce they served with it was also really unique, a mix of miso paste and doubanjiang, giving a slightly fruity note and a perfect accompaniment to the pork belly.  The server also gave complimentary matcha ice cream, which was really good too. The matcha flavor was deep and was a creamy ice cream.

Overall, it was an obvious upgrade to the last izakaya, and no dish was bad. While only a few items truly wowed me, I enjoyed how they stuck to tradition to provide an unpretentious experience that reminded me of Japan. While pricey, this is a place I could recommend to others who want to try a very solid izakaya.

Appreciated the small dishes for variety, but quality differed between dishes and I also found many of them lacked flavor.

My favorite dishes were the negima (thigh with leek), the shisho making, and the goma yogoshi (spinach in sesame paste) for their more unique tastes. I wouldn't recommend the Nama-Yuba nor the mochi wrapped in bacon or nori.

Hidden gem with soul - this is where Japanese food feels right.
Every dish at Kiraku is crafted with care, precision, and that rare sense of warmth that’s hard to find outside Japan. But what truly sets this place apart isn’t just the taste - it’s the consistency. Year after year, the quality doesn’t fade. It actually improves.

The staff? Always kind. Always attentive. The atmosphere? Casual but cozy, like your favorite local spot back home.

If you’re new to the Bay Area or just hunting for a place that gets Japanese food right, start here. Kiraku isn’t just a restaurant. It’s the kind of place that makes you want to come back before you’ve even left.

This is honestly my favorite spot in the entire SF/Bay Area — no competition, no close second. I mean it. Nothing else compares.

I first came here around 2022 and was absolutely blown away. I live far, but this is still a place I’ll happily drive an hour for, wait 40+ minutes for, and revisit 10+ times without hesitation. Zero complaints. Always worth it.

The space isn’t big, but the sticker-covered walls and posters give it so much personality. It feels like a place that’s been loved and thoughtfully run for years — a true neighborhood gem with soul.

✨ My forever must-orders (these NEVER miss):

• Ankimo mousse + sweet potato chips — this combo is unreal
• Roasted beef tongue with truffle oil — insanely tender and bouncy; WAY better than the tongue skewers (not even the same level)
• Wagyu tataki — rich, buttery, milky wagyu flavor… I sometimes order two
• A5 ribeye nigiri — just WOW. If you love wagyu, you CANNOT skip this

These feel like permanent-menu-level safe choices. I’ve ordered them countless times and the quality is always consistent.

⸻

🌿 Other favorites from past visits

Corn tempura, miso black cod, and tuna 3 ways are also great picks.

⸻

🆕 New dishes we tried this time

• Hamachi carpaccio salad — light and refreshing, great palate reset
• Yuzu chicken udon — comforting, and the hint of yuzu is genius. So satisfying.

Grilled rice ball was just okay for me, but my boyfriend loved it.
Sweet potato brûlée for dessert was creamy and not overly sweet — so good.

⸻

💛 Service

Always lovely. Angelina especially is such a sweetheart. Every time we come, she always has the warmest smile and is so attentive, just adorable energy.

⚠️ Reality check

This place is VERY popular. Expect a 30–60 min wait, even on weekdays.

💡 Best tip: come right at 5:30pm opening or join the Yelp waitlist in advance.

Writing this review makes me sad thinking about the day I leave the Bay Area and can’t come back here anymore.

Kiraku is absolutely a must-try in the Bay Area. Come experience it yourself — you won’t regret it!

Absolute meet cute with a cozy vibe. Came here for a late night snack at 10pm.

They have a little table out front to check in, but as I was a walking they came to get me and seated promptly.

Whole place sits maybe thirty people tops thirty five

They have a tapas style menu of small plates which is nice if you want to mix and match.

I got the toasted green tea, clam miso soup, garlic edamame, and a skewer each of the eel and lamb.

The green tea wasn’t piping hot but warm. Tasted… toasty. Didn’t think I’d like it but three cups in it grew on me. Give it a chance.

Garlic edamame was excellent. Had a coating of anchovy bits that made it unique and had me snacking my lips. Will order this everytime.

They said that the miso soup usually comes at the end, after the other courses. When asked for a preference, I deferred to them. They thought it right away.

The soup had about five clams which imparted a salty brine depth that eclipsed the expected umami of the miso. I’m not mad. Tastes great. But I do like my miso on the lighter side. Worth trying to see if it’s for you.

Lamb skewer was well seasoned and light. It’s rare to find lamb in Japanese restaurants so I make it a point to order it. Had bits of scallions grilled with it, came with a dollop of mustard. Delicious.

The eel skewer was my absolute favorite. Soft and buttery, partitions on its own and melts in your mouth. Seasoning was strong but adequate. Cane with some wasabi. Avoid the wasabi for this one. You don’t need it, as it distracts from the unagi’s natural qualities.

They had a dessert menu, but I passed on it

The restaurant’s dark wood walls are sprinkled with vintage Japanese beer ads.

The staff are attentive and very sweet. When I came in, they asked if it was my first time here and walked me through the menu. Then they proceeded to give me a warm towel as I was coming in from the rain. An absolute vibe.

Remembered fondly by some, these places were known for good food at cheap prices.

Daimo in Richmond is a far departure from those "day mouws" in China but is nonetheless a solid choice for those looking for traditional Chinese fare.

Their go-to dishes include their beef chow fuhn, beef stew over rice, and other assorted rice plates. Prices are moderate, but for certain items, portions are quite large.
In fact, they're well known for their large portions. People seem to come from far away to take advantage of this.

Service is good, and the waitresses are friendly and  helpful. The restaurant has a lot of windows and they give the place a bright airy feel.

If you're in the area and looking for Chinese food, give Daimo a try. The food is good, traditional and you certainly won't leave hungry.

Its a little retro 90s inside, but its spacious, my table was clean, they offered a complimentary hot tea & hot oil on the table for the food.

I ordered a lunch special for $15.95, I asked for her reccomendation - she suggested the beef Xo. This came with a beverage (I chose a can of coke) & a small soup (sweet & sour). The beef xo also had a side of white rice on the plate as well - which turned out great, because although the Xo is yummy, it is quite rich and salty, the white rice cuts that richness very well. The portion was also ample for a lunch serving. I say it is for sure worth it! The beef was super tender and flavorful as well. I really didnt care for the Celery in this dish though. Next time I'd ask them to leave it out, its really nothing but a filler & not a good one at that. The snow peas were a nice addition though.

I also ordered Beef & Chive chow fun i believe it was $17.95. This is a HUGE portion, so while $17.95 sounds high to me, this can easily fill 3 people with just the chow fun alone! This price is super reasonable. As far as taste of the chow fun - the beef was great and tender, I just wish the noodles were thicker and fatter. These arent typically the kind of noodles I envision when I think chow fun... this is probably closer to a thai pad see ewe noodle, still good! But i was really wanting a fatter wider noodle. The sauce was perfect - maybe id have liked it to be a little wetter even, but the flavor was good.

For appetizers i ordered a
- BBQ pork rice roll $7 8pc (my favorite thing out of everything!)
- Shrimp & Chive Dumplings 3pc (my least favorite of everything)
- Turnip cake $6 3pc (this was interesting - texturally like a mix between fake mashed potatoes & gelatin.. I didnt hate it. The seared parts were super yummy)

The shrimp & Chive Dumplings was a bit dry. Bland & a little over burnt on the seared outside. It also didnt come with any sauce. Id never order it again

The BBQ rice roll was texturally pleasant to me - with the super soft rice roll & the addition of the BBQ pork added texture + it was laying in a sort of ponzu or soju sauce which was also yummy.

Overall I'd rate everything a 4 out of 5. The service was great. The ladies were super friendly and wiling to make suggestions. They even packed my to go leftovers them selves, & didnt charge me for my extra coke... which may or may not have been intentional - either way I added what that cost would have been to their tip so it works out.

Id definitely be back!

top_reviews.content: We ate as a party of 13 friends at the China Village located at Solano Ave, Albany near Berkely yesterday night on 5/21/26. The restaurant is located conveniently by itself across the sidewalk from parking. All you need to do to get there is cross a short sidewalk. The area felt clean and safe. When we arrived and walked in, we were greeted by many nice, beautiful and hospitable ladies who were to be our waiters and led to a private "Dragon" party room near the back. In the front were standard tables and a lot of pretty Chinese decor from Gold to Dragons. There were bathrooms separated by gender and area located near the front. There was also a fish tank full of sea-life such as Crabs and Fishes and Lobsters that were on the Chinese Cuisine's Menu. It was a very laid back vibe and very quiet and peaceful and relaxing. In the back, were we were seated, the tables had comfortable chairs and a round spinning table like something you would find at Chinese Dim Sum. The atmosphere felt very relaxed and easy-going and brought us back to feeling like we were in China or Shanghai's Nightlife. The waiter's service was great, they constantly came to check in on us and were very personable and formidable and made nice small talk with us and chatted and it felt like they were close friends which each waiter should strive to be. Our table was filled with neat napkins to wipe, put on your lap and to double as a handkerchief with, silverware, a glass of fresh water not tap as well as herbal fresh tea that was simmered just right with a hint of bitterness you would expect from fresh tea with leaves. We ordered and the food was promptly brought out almost immediately with little wait time. This restaurant is known for their fresh Chinese spark of Sichuan(Spicy) and Mala(Spicy) as well as Seafood(Seafood), once again it felt like we were transported back into the luxurious city of China. This was very authentic and fresh Chinese food, not like the fake food that is AmeriChinese like Panda Express. We ordered delicious food such as clams and oysters which were paired with a lot of extra garnish to truly bring out their wonderful shelly flavor, beautiful and delicious small crustacean prawns and shrimp that tasted fresh from the sea, Spicy Mala/Sichuan Beef as well as Fish which were pretty spicy yet savory, Yangzhou Fried Rice with the perfect amount of veggies and beef, Honeybee Lobster that was golden crisp, Orange Chicken that was not as sweet as many fake Chinese places make them so these were the authentic real deal, Pork and Shrimp Dumplings which were nicely coated and didnt fall apart, Shellfish which were deliciously chewy, Scallops which were very tasty and more. The food was very clean and fresh, they had a rich savory seafood taste and aroma and tasted like the deep blue ocean, and most of the food came with a side of unique sauce that was to be best paired individually with each unique dish. The service was great, the waiters were very attentive and attentful with their service, constantly refilling our glasses and helping us make way and navigate around our big party of guests and limited spaces to make way for new dishes to glaze our table. Everyone was full, we were not rushed and came out feeling very refreshed and sleepy as the food was so so delicious. Fair price! I attached some pictures below of what I had, if anyone is in the nearby area, I encourage you to come try the food at this delicious and authentic Chinese restaurant. Even if you are not in the immediate area, this place is worth a drive as we did coming from the Solano Area all the way here just to sample this delicious food from a mutual friend's wonderful recommendations. We are sure to come back in the near future to try their delicious other menus offerings and we are confident that we will be equally if not more impressed with their offerings the second time around as well. Thank you so much to China Village for hosting our large party and be very pleasant to be around for both service and coordination of the big dinner that took place yesterday.

top_reviews.content:
Stopped in after a salon appointment in Albany and found this to be a slightly more polished version of your typical Bay Area pho spot.

Food:
The fresh spring rolls (gỏi cuốn) were fresh and well-prepared. Peanut sauce was good, nothing standout, but definitely enjoyable.

I ordered the bún bò Huế, which included traditional congealed pork blood (huyết), always a plus for authenticity. The broth had good depth of flavor, but it lacked the expected spice. This dish should have a bit of heat, and that was missing.

The side veggies leaned heavily on bean sprouts (very typical here), but I would’ve preferred more shredded cabbage for balance.

Drinks:
Vietnamese iced coffee came out almost immediately, so it’s clearly pre-made. Efficient, but you do miss the traditional drip experience.

Service & Atmosphere:
Service is very fast, everything came out within minutes. After that, it’s pretty hands-off, so you’ll need to flag someone down if you need anything.

The space itself is nicer than most pho spots, and the uniformed staff gives it a slightly more put-together feel.

Overall:
Good food, very quick service, and a clean, comfortable space. Not exceptional, but a solid, reliable option if you’re in the area. Pricing is in line with current Bay Area averages, though it feels slightly high given the quick-service, pho-house style experience.

Pricing (my order):
•	Fresh spring rolls: $10.95
•	Bún bò Huế: $17.25
•	Vietnamese iced coffee: $6.95

3.75⭐️

Overall great spot for Vietnamese food. Fresh and delicious. I like how they have a small bowl of broth on the side for their rice plates. It's a perfect pairing. The spring rolls are on point as well.

Outstanding Vietnamese Pho Experience!
This is hands down one of the best bowls of pho I've had in a long time. The broth is the true star—rich, deep, and full of flavor, yet incredibly clean and not greasy at all. You can tell it has been simmered for hours with great care. Every sip is comforting and satisfying.
I also love that the pho is served in a double-wall stainless steel bowl, which keeps the soup piping hot from the first bite to the last. It's such a thoughtful touch that makes the dining experience even better.
The fresh herbs, bean sprouts, and onions were crisp and vibrant, and the beef was tender and delicious. But what really impressed me was their house-made chili sauce—it's packed with flavor, perfectly spicy, and takes the pho to another level.
If you're looking for authentic Vietnamese pho with exceptional broth, excellent presentation, and attention to detail, this place is a must-visit. I'll definitely be coming back again and again. Highly recommended! 🍜🔥⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
