top_reviews.content: I’m rating Gioia five stars on the pizza. I love it. Love it. And I love the style which is the New York style way. You order your slices which are pre made pies. Then they heat them in the oven which makes them hot and crispy. Several topping choices to choose. No indoor seating. Other than a bench there’s really no outdoor seating either. But the pizza is so good. And it’s nice, shady outside. Decent amount of street parking.

YUM. I’m so happy to have found this spot. This is some of the best pizza I’ve ever had, and I’m a former New Yorker.

The crust is perfectly chewy and the toppings are absolutely delicious. Our favorite is the Julian, which I’m pretty sure is perfect. The cheese and sausage are so yummy and they are generous with the garlic and lacinato kale. So delicious and dare I say healthy too?

The fact that you can get most of their specialty pizzas by the slice is the cherry on top and reminds me of my days in nyc, but pizza this good was even hard to come by there.

Tucked into the side of your average street in Berkeley is the best pizza we’ve had in the Bay Area. GIOIA is serving up some VERY good pizza out of what feels like a hole in the wall. Beware that parking may be hard to find as it’s right off the street although there is a lot just down the road. The inside is very bare bones, which in this case is a good sign. The smell of the oven and dough just hits you once you step in and it’s fantastic. Ordering was quick and easy and the slices are priced a bit high but for the quality of pizza we’d say it was worth it. We got some classic slices and also their fungi slice. From ordering to eating it took about 5-10 minutes despite a few people ahead of us so it was relatively quick.

And now time to try it… man was it good. It’s clearly a good representation of NY style. The crust is firm and crunchy but the pizza has a nice flop to it. The cheese is tasty with a good sauce under it too. The fungi also popped with flavor from the mushrooms, parsley, and olive oil; just a great series of slices. The best place to eat it is probably the bench seating they have outside but it may be full as a heads up. As far as we see it, GIOIA is a must stop in Berkeley. It came very highly recommended and was devoured in less than 5 minutes. We almost wish we didn’t have plans to eat later that day because we could’ve eaten 2 more slices each then and there. This is as close to true NYC style pizza as you can get outside of NYC.

There is the original location in Berkeley and then another location in Hayes Valley in San Francisco. We passed it all the time so we thought we would come in and try it. They are crust is incredible! Nine out of 10 in that category. They have a very interesting sauce, it’s almost on the edge of a pasta sauce, but not quite. I think honestly if they slightly changed up their sauce, the pizza would be better. If you like cheese on your pizza, this is the place to go because they’re pretty heavy handed on the cheese. Overall, we liked it and we would try different slices, but it is not our absolute favorite pizza in the bay area. We tried the margarita, so we haven’t tried all of the different slices and flavors that they offer. So we’ll have to go back and see how the others compare. Thus far, we would give it a solid 7/10.

The pizza had a perfectly cooked thin crust. The dough was so sparkly doughy and stretchy with the right amount of firmness on the bottom of the crust. The toppings (kale, sausage, mozerlla cheese, garlic..)Jwent well together too with a fair amount dispersed on the slice.

The salad was filling. I probably didn't need to get the pizza. It was well balanced with farro, avacado, golden raisins, and almond. The vinaigrette was also a nice balance (you don't need much).

Go check them out!

Seeing my food arrive with no curds, I sent it back because I was sure something was missing. Alas, no, the cotija cheese was the cheese for this dish. I would have rather they used queso fresco instead. It doesn't have a strong flavor and would have satisfied my cheese curd craving </3 That being said, it still slapped.

The star of the show was the Millionaire's Bacon. The cuts were thick, flavorful, creamy (?) and almost melted in my mouth. I won't lie, it's heavily influencing my review.

I wish the outside tables were a bit more spaced, as I felt cramped.

I came here during a weekday for brunch. That is probably the best time to come due to street parking filling up fast.
To drink, I had the raspberry lemonade. This is easily 5/5. Perfect blend of sweetness & tartness.
For an appetizer we got the popcorn chicken & Korean FC. My favorite was the popcorn chicken it was 5/5 and I loved that they added actual popcorn. The Korean FC was okay 3/5.
The Mac N Cheese sounded very interesting, however, it fell flat. It was dry and not cheesy. I would rate it 2/5. We got the Chicken & Story Burger. The Chicken Burger 4/5 was definitely better than the Story Burger 2/5. The Story Burger was lacking in flavor. The potatoes wedges were really good though. Not pictured was the millionaire bacon 5/5. It was so good and I would love to try the BLT with millionaire bacon.
Lastly, we got the Lemon Ricotta Pancake 1/5 it was bitter and the second pancake under the first was burnt. We also got the Mascarpone Stuffed Deep Fried French Toast which was 100/5. Every bite was amazing. Would definitely come back again for that dish alone. Other than that, a lot of the dishes fell flat for me but the presentation of the food was beautiful and service was good as well.

This has easily become one of my favorite brunch spots in Oakland. I usually come with my dog, and one thing I really appreciate is how consistently warm and welcoming the manager and servers are :)

The menu has a Korean-inspired take on brunch, and I almost always order the Blackstone Benedict and the Lemon Ricotta Pancakes.

The Blackstone Benedict is probably my favorite savory dish here. The combination of bacon, asparagus, bread, and hollandaise just works, the richness from the sauce, the saltiness of the bacon, and the freshness of the asparagus are really well balanced. I will say that on a few visits, the sauce had a slightly eggy aroma that I wasn’t crazy about. It’s pretty subtle and hasn’t stopped me from ordering it :-)

As for the pancakes, I’ve tried a few of the options, and the Lemon Ricotta is easily the standout for me. The pancakes are incredibly soft and fluffy, with just enough lemon to brighten everything up without tasting overly citrusy. The ricotta adds this subtle creaminess and richness that makes them feel a little more special than your standard brunch pancakes.

Great food, genuinely kind service, and very dog-friendly, which, for me, is always a plus :-)

Phenomenal brunch flavors are worth the wait (and sore bum)!

Kitchen Story is an epic brunch spot. If you're planning a weekend visit, I definitely recommend making a reservation, or be prepared for a bit of a wait.

I met a friend here for Sunday brunch, and we ordered an assortment of plates and beverages to share. Everything was delicious and repeatable, but here's my order of personal preference for the food:

Korean FC Wings: Crispy, flavorful, and absolutely standout.

Lemon Ricotta Pancakes: Perfectly fluffy, and bright flavors on perfectly prepared pancakes.

Goji Bowl: A solid, satisfying savory option.

For beverages, the Ube Latte and the Millionaire's Bloody Mary were the stars of the show. Their house coffee and unsweetened passion fruit iced tea were good, but fairly standard.

My only suggestion for management would be to invest in more comfortable seating, but honestly, it was worth the sore bum to enjoy all those delicious flavors! I will definitely be returning and recommending to friends.

Wanted to try something different for Sunday brunch. The noodles with the egg, bacon and pork had just enough savory flavor to knock your socks off. The service was ok. The waiter forgot to process my order so I had to ask about my food after watching other people around me get seated and served before myself. He was apologetic and did comp my meal so he did make it right. Just disappointed because the food was soooo good.

top_reviews.content: Hmm, it was alright. I don't think I would come back, but it's important to try new things once in a while. If I remember correctly pasta base is between 11-13 dollars, and picking a sauce/topping adds an extra 4-6 dollars, so at the very least you'll be paying 15 dollars for one bowl of pasta. Kinda pricey. The bowls aren't even that big, only enough to feed one person with a big appetite, 2 people at most. It was enough to fill me up but the flavor was just not there. But it wasn't the worst pasta in the world, just one of those things where you know you could've made something better at home for a fraction of the price. Service and atmosphere are also lacking. Overall, 3/5.

Absolutely loved this place! The pasta was fresh and delicious — especially the tagliatelle with Bolognese and a generous amount of cheese on top. The flatbread on the side was a great surprise and paired perfectly with the meal. Cozy and welcoming interior with a rustic touch, and everything was clean and well organized. You can tell they put care into both their food and the space. Definitely a hidden gem — I’ll be coming back!

It was $50 for on lasagna and one tortellini order (I got no drinks) . You had to get up and order like in a fast food place. At the end you had to put your plates in this tray full of dirty soaking dishes. The lasagna was good but the tortellini was way too chewy and had this tangy flavor that did not go with marinera. The plates look nothing like the website photos. I came because the reviews said it’s great, but that sadly was not the case.

Great, authentic food. Homemade pasta. LARGE portions--prepare to share or take some home. Only suggestion is change pop music out for Italian tracks: Perche' no? Good service. It's an order and take to table situation, self serve. Can order ahead, pick up, and eat in, if desired.

Just like the one in San Francisco, this delicious pasta shop offers a mix & match option to choose a sauce and then a type of pasta. They are fast and delicious.

They also offer salads that are quite hearty and accompany the meal quite well or treat yourself to one of their gelato flavors.

My favorite part is that they have a pasta guide, and I highly recommend their gnocchi!

top_reviews.content: Been to this place before with friends. Can be busy at times up to a 20-30 mins wait to get a table, indoor and outdoor seating, street parking as well. Food is pretty decent. I can personally say it’s a hit or miss. I’ve gone before where it’s a 10/10 knocked out of the ballpark and then others when it’s a 6/10 where the meat is overcooked and I’m still chewing on my steak for 5 mins. Place is pretty nice as well, it can be busy as I’ve mentioned before. If it’s busy, you can expect longer delays which tends to happen. Good for all ages.

It is always lovely to see friendly and welcoming Crystal.  She is there most times we visit and is knowledgeable and so enthusiastic telling us about new things to try, the things she loves and what's coming up next!  Many restaurants will offer vegan choices which just means it is minus something.  5 Tacos and Beers however gives us innovative and exciting new dishes full of flavor and actual vegan sour cream which adds a huge factor of deliciousness! This weekend I tried enchiladas with a tangy Verde sauce, cheese and lots of deep red beets and a side of black beans with vegan sour cream which were wonderful! The restaurant itself is a fun place with plenty of seating both indoors and out yet maintains charm.  I love that on good weather days they open up the doors to let in fresh air and a view of the passersby and outdoor diners.
If you love tacos and beers, this is a must-go. Absolutely delicious food and tasty beers. Just great. I come back every time I visit.

The ribeye taco is Hella good. I also tried the Octopus taco and that was pretty good too. Beans and rice could be a little better, but good. I tried the ceviche with Octopus,  scallops and Tuna and I thought it was good, but I wish there was more lime and flavor. But it was good. The service was good and we didn't wait long at all to be seated and to get all the items we ordered. I'm looking forward to visiting again, soon.

I came here right before happy hour, 3 pm to ?, and I liked it! The food was good, but the chips and guacamole are top notch! 👌🏻I ordered some drinks and had some tacos. Good tacos and good drinks! Happy hour pricing is 20% off regular prices. Would recommend and return!

reviews_snippets.content: "Great food and service, nice location, tasty drinks, fair price -recommended!"

top_reviews.content: We loved the seasonal peach pizza, very unique. We ordered foccacia to take home. We usually get the vegan mushroom & spinach but wanted to try something new today. We haven't been in for awhile, being parents of an energetic kid, we really appreciated the addition of games. They have rackets, corn hole, books, hula hoops and bubbles for kids. They have a dog leash station and water bowls for your pups. The cashier was warm and welcoming.
I’ve been here a few times - won’t be going back. If you’re charging $40 for a pizza - put some toppings on it. Barely anything on it, and the last inch and a half of the crust is completely bare.

I coworker turned me in to this place. Staff are very friendly and engaging. They keep the space clean and welcoming. The pizza is AMAZING! Seriously the best thin crust pizza I’ve ever had. While this location is out of my way for the most part, I’ll make it a point to stop by when I’m around. Thank you!

They have great thin crust sourdough pizza. It takes a lot of time and effort to master a great pizza dough not to mention a sourdough one. The staff were nice, very friendly, and welcoming. The soft chewy sourdough pizza crust will be memorable to us and we'll definitely return. The toppings and sauce were very good too.

Nick's pizza is the best pizza I've ever had. They also have really good baked goods and their homemade ranch is amazing. Their crust is so chewy and flavorful due to it being sourdough. Highly recommend!

top_reviews.content: Walked in for dinner for 2 on a Thursday afternoon. There is some street parking around the area, we parked kind of far and just walked over. They have both indoor and outdoor seating and a nice little bar, it’s a cozy restaurant and it got busy. Service was also really friendly. We got the arancini to start, I think it was still a little cold and we also go bread with oil which was really good. I got the lasagna which was really big and I devoured it because I was starting. My friend got the involtini and he finished it as well. The food took some time but overall it’s a nice vibe and a cozy restaurant. They said the lasagna and ravioli porcini trifolati were popular dishes to get.

Really disappointing experience. We ordered four dishes and not a single one was done well.

The tomato burrata came with completely flavorless tomatoes. The tuna carpaccio was overly salty, drowning in dressing, with wet, salty tuna and even mayo on top—which felt completely out of place. The pasta ragu had noticeable chunks of pure pork fat, which made it hard to enjoy. The campagnola pasta was swimming in sauce and, instead of pappardelle, had random pieces of spaghetti mixed in.

Across the board, the pasta was overcooked, with strands stuck together. When we pointed it out, we were told this is “expected over time,” even though it arrived like that, and that the mixed pasta shapes were just an accident due to batch cooking.

Service was practically nonexistent. No one checked in to ask how anything tasted. Our half-eaten burrata and tuna were taken away without a single question. We interacted with at least four different people bringing plates, and even the wine was served by a busser, which made the whole experience feel disjointed and inattentive.

Overall, poor execution, questionable explanations, and not worth the price.

Inviting ambiance, absolutely delicious authentic food, and charming fantastic staff! Five stars easily, they transported me back to Italy! Let them order family style for your group so that you can enjoy all of their best dishes and drinks. Shout out Angelo, he was the best!

My friends, new to Berkeley, were telling me that they loved Italian food, so I told them that we must try Agrodolce Trattoria on Shattuck. I know that Agrodolce has roots going back to Caffe Sport in North Beach which I would go to in the 70's, and more recently Trattoria Siciliana on College which was my buddy David's favorite restaurant.
We loved it! The atmosphere was great, including projecting the classic film La Dolce Vita on the wall. The food was fantastic, my Swordfish was cooked, as the menu said" perfectly! The cocktail bar was  right out of an old movie. And the bread and dipping sauce was a signature classic.
My friends and I were able to catch up on recent trips to India, Normandy France and Budapest. It could hardly have been a better choice.
Needless to say we'll be back!

The food was variable...some dishes were very good, others were pretty mediocre.  The service was some of the worst I have experienced at a restaurant of this level for quite a long time.  Things started out fine. We ordered a second bottle of wine that took 15 minutes to arrive, by which time some of us were nearly finished with our main course.  I could see our bottle was sitting on the server's table where our server stood, joking with the other staff, for a good 5-10 minutes before I stood up, walked over, and requested that she bring the bottle to our table.  At dessert, we were handed two dessert menus for a table of six.  When we asked for a menu per person, we got quite the strange/annoyed look from the busboy.  A good 15 minutes had passed after we finished the desserts and no server came by to deliver the bill.  Not wanting to hang around longer, I went to the bar to request the bill.  It took them another 10 minutes to furnish the bill (the restaurant was not busy by then), upon which they added a mandatory 20% tip on the POST-TAX total, which I disputed but they refused to change.  We will not be returning, and given the long list of better and more professional options out there, I would caution anyone else from going.

top_reviews.content:
Very yummy food! Im a huge fan of mexican food, and this fusion food brings it to another level. Truthfully ive only ever gotten their bowl with chicken, but getting it with golden rice and all of that is so worth it. Its got a kind of richness and creaminess to it that i love. While ive only tried that one thing, i will say that their ingredients seem very good quality, and ive never gotten a piece of gristle, or wilted lettuce, or anything like that. Their salsas are also very yummy, although i wish they were a bit spicier. But they're very suitable for people with average to low spoce tolerance!!
The outside seating is very cute, and the "inside" seating next to the main building is pretty nice too. My friend and i normally just get take out, but eating there would be nice, and the place is pretty cute with its decorations.
I highly recommend you give the Afghan way a try!

I tried the Afghan burrito today, and it was absolutely delicious! Everything was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned — every bite was full of amazing taste. I loved it so much that I’ll definitely come back to enjoy it again and again.

The customer service was also excellent — very friendly, welcoming, and attentive, which made the experience even better.

It’s a great option for family meals and events too. Highly recommended!

Came to this spot last night to break our fast since we were in the area and had heard great things about it. The birria tacos were so delicious, the meat was high quality and very well priced. I also tried the burrito bowl, which came half golden rice, half lettuce, with chicken and topped with guacamole. The bowl was a bit on the blander side, although when I tasted some of the sauce (maybe the golden/sweet sauce?), it was good. I think next time I’d try something different.

Otherwise, the service was great. My only small complaints are that the sauce containers are tiny and the side of chips is more of a sprinkle than an actual side, lol. That said, I really appreciated that they offer dates to break your fast and have tons of Palestinian art and messages throughout the restaurant, it was amazing and very supportive to see. They also use halal meat, and the quality is excellent.

The bathrooms were impeccably clean, customer service was solid, and I loved that they carry Palestinian soda instead of Coke or Pepsi. Overall, a great experience and I’d definitely come back.

What a unique taco experience! It would be a great place with a larger group and there is total privacy which is fun.  We went back and forth on which tacos to order and settled on these but for both of us it was totally about the Birria tacos.   We didn’t finish the 5th one so they are filling.

I got the vegan Golden burrito here, it was very tasty and a huge portion! I wasn't blown away by the taste, but it was interesting to try since it was like a normal burrito (beans, rice, fajitas etc) but with their Golden sauce inside. The burrito comes with a few chips and sweet chili sauce on the side. The burrito leaked quite a bit near the end, so it's better to eat it over a plate with a fork ready.

The menu has clearly labeled vegan options, which I really appreciate! The restaurant is part of a planned outdoor space (Cal Food Garden), so there is plenty of high-quality outdoor seating as well as bike parking.

top_reviews.content:
We recently visited Pyeongchang Tofu House and it really hit the spot. My daughter was craving spicy pork, and I was in the mood for tofu stew, and this place delivered on both. The flavors were on point and exactly what we were hoping for.

The service was also great. The staff was attentive, friendly, and made sure we had everything we needed throughout our meal.

One small note, they served us the crispy rice from the bottom of the clay pot. I remember having this growing up, but with sugar, and since I haven’t seen it in a long time, I wasn’t quite sure how it was meant to be enjoyed here. It would have been nice to have a little guidance, as I think we might have appreciated it more with some context.

Overall, a really solid experience. We’ll definitely be back when we’re craving comforting Korean food.

One of the best Korean places in the Bay Area. Started with great banchan. Eggplant was our favorite. A wide selection of bibimbap. We tried the wakame and seaweed one, and it didn’t disappoint. Tofu soup warmed us up on a chilly evening.

As someone who appreciates Korean food, I was disappointed with the quality and flavors of the dishes. Overall, the food did not live up to expectations. It felt underseasoned, lacked flavor, and was simply not very good. I wouldn’t recommend this place if you’re craving good Korean food.

Been coming here for 15 yrs straight, since undergrad! Amazing every time. Highly recommend the kimchi tofu soup, galbi tang, bi bim bop, bossam, gal bi, soba cold noodles. They have probably the best banchan. Thank you to all the staff and kitchen, this place is a true Oakland gem.

The seafood pancake here is a must try crispy, flavorful, and easily one of the best I’ve had so many others end up soggy in comparison. If it weren’t such a drive, I’d be back every week just for that. I also love that they serve crispy rice with the soft tofu soup, it adds the perfect crunch and soaks up the broth beautifully.

top_reviews.content: I rarely ever leave reviews, but I had to for Blondie’s because it’s the VERY BEST pizza place I’ve been to. As someone who is a pizza fanatic and tried pizza across CA and Italy, I can say that this pizza is perfection. I went for lunch, there was a short wait time, the owner was so nice and funny, and the place was clean with lots of seating space. As a Cal student, I feel like I got more flavor and quantity for just $8. You can taste the love in this pizza ❤️🍕❤️

The place is amazing. They were super accommodating to our big group. The pizza was fresh and hot. The hyphy was so delicious, having pepperoni,pineapple,jalapeños,and olives go so well. The crust was super crispy and the toppings were loaded to the max. I've had pizza all throughout the bay and this place takes the cake. I will be returning in the future.

Five stars for Ismael at Blondie's Pizza! 🍕I had an amazing experience here thanks to Ismael. He was incredibly welcoming, friendly, and efficient. The customer service was top-notch, and he made sure our order was perfect and piping hot.Great food tastes even better when it comes with fantastic service. Ismael is a huge asset to the team, and his positive energy really stands out. I will definitely be back!

Have been to blondies a few times. The pizza is really well done! There usually isn't a long line. Recently tried their vegetarian pizza 10" with vegan cheese which was really well done. The crust was nice and soft. It had a nice blend of veggies and cheese (especially since vegan cheese has a distinctive taste) it wasn't too overwhelming at all. Highly recommend for vegan's or people of are lactose intolerant
Great place pizza feels a bit home made the cheese all comes off in the first bite. Not my fav place for pizza

top_reviews.content: This is my third time dining here. Absolutely 💯 love this place and the meals are phenomenal! Great service. We had a party of 12 and everyone had an excellent meal. Staff helped us by keeping cold, then cutting, a celebration cake.

My husband and I went to Revival last night for dinner and it was an awesome experience from start to finish! Our server, Landis (sorry if I’m misspelling!), was so warm, friendly, and attentive. He made recommendations from the menu, checked on us often, and made our first time at Revival a real pleasant experience. We ordered some cocktails (Smooth Sailing and Trip to Trinidad), a half dozen oysters, and two specials (Denver wagyu steaks with chimichurri, broccoli, mashed potatoes, and pickled radish). Everything was delicious!!! We also ordered a pear and caramel sundae with candied nuts for dessert and it was to die for! Special shoutout to Manager Lucy for making it happen—turns out it was a seasonal dessert and they had actually switched to a strawberry rhubarb sundae, but she said they still had pears on hand and was able to make it for us anyway. Lucky us! My husband and I agreed it was the best meal we’ve had in a good long while! We really appreciated the amazing food and service and will definitely be back in the future!

Excellent pre-theatre restaurant. Quick and friendly service. Really tasty food, well prepared and presented. As appetizers, we had Kenebec potato chips,duck confit legs, and focaccia with three dips, all perfect to start. Then margarita pizza - sauce tasted out of a jar but really good base; little gem Caesar - good dressing but so-so croutons, and crispy pork belly -the star dish. All in all, great food and pretty good value. Great atmosphere.

The service was kind, the atmosphere delectable.

I ordered this mushroom risotto off the specials at the recommendayion of the waiter.

When I tell you it was awesome, I do it with the full weight of my thesis advisors censure on the usage of the word for anything that was less than a sign from God. For in this case it was close to a religious experience. The greens were fresh, well blanched, and tender. They perfectly offset the richness of the risotto and mediated texture via the pumpkin. Around the edges dollops of parsley-garlic muddles provided bursts of flavor that provided the dish a well-modulated method of enhancing the senses. The mushrooms, well, they are freshly foraged and treated with care by the chef.

Taken together I will say I was blown away. It reminded me of a Slovenian risotto made by a grandmother who has cooked it for decades, but with a presentation and sophistication suitable for a diplomats table.

If you are so lucky as to have this offered on the menu, do not miss the chance.

If it is not already clear, compliments to the chef. I eagerly look forward to whatever they whip up next.

I was so hungry and exhausted.  I didn't want to dine in a samll.whole.in the wall with quick food. I knew ai wanted something good. I came to the corner of the block and found Revival. I am very impressed with the presentation of the food, the warm ambiance inside. Plush seats and open space. Open bar very classy and upscale. Out server was polite, nice and informative.  He was patient and  offered good suggestions.  I will make this my new spot.

top_reviews.content: This was a really fun place on a great commercial corridor. There are inside an outdoor table and the ambience is terrific. Service was attentive and food came out promptly. The food was delicious and the menu was quite varied and unique. I also really enjoyed the nonalcoholic Mojito. So delicious. The sushi was quite fresh. We also had salmon that was quite delicious and the appetizers were really nice too. Overall, a very positive experience. It was not deep but once in a while, it’s worth it.

Isahare was the highlight of our trip. We are now referring to this meal as THE Meal. It was a beautiful day and our table allowed us to enjoy it. Unfortunately, I didn’t take a picture of our eggplant, tempura, and tofu dish, but It was superb. I had the black cod and my friend had the salmon.  We relished every bite. The service was excellent.

Another unusually warm day in East Bay, and my 14 yo son and I were on a fragrance crawl down 4th Street when we both decided to eat. Having lived in the area for a while and tried various restaurants on 4th and been repeatedly disappointed by them, but the reviews did look positive and the place inviting so we thought we'd give it a go! We were seated right away outside because under the tree and shade it was nice, we ordered multiple items, but some like the tuna tartar was really good until we noticed the rather strong flavor of Parmesan cheese in it which was an odd addition. Secondly, the seaweed salad was mixed with some other greens as well as baby tomatoes and tofu, overall a pretty presentation but took away from the taste of the seaweed, which we really enjoy. The fish was fresh, not the best, but still enjoyable while the rolls were really tasty but small for the price. The service was outstanding and our server Maddie was great! I believe that made the experience, so I think this place has promise and just need to be open to try some different things on their menu. Definitely think it deserves a second look.
The Superb-intendent 🍀

Oh my god! This is one of the best Japanese restaurants I’ve ever tried. Everything was absolutely delicious and when they told us about their best seller shrimp tempura they were not lying. I had dinner here for the first time and it was great! I ordered a few items, but I cannot add some pictures to the app for some reason. top_reviews.content: We had an absolutely amazing experience and cannot wait to return. It was SO special and the food and wine were absolutely incredible and so fresh. Will absolutely return, thank you so much for the best night to celebrate our graduation.

Over all I was surprised at the poor quality of food for $200 for 3 of us with drinks.
The place has such a nice atmosphere but expensive low quality food.
To bad!

I would want to come back again to try other things on the menu.

The sticky rice pork ribs are tender and flavorful, while the green beans and eggplant are perfectly seasoned and rich in taste. The spicy lamb skewers are also a standout, bursting with bold flavor. top_reviews.content:
The Noodle is a fantastic Thai restaurant that brings authentic Thai food to Berkeley. It's small and casual, making it a really great place to bring your friends. It's also delicious and affordable, making the food addictive. My family and I have eaten here many times for all those reasons.

The menu at the Noodle is extensive, so much so that it is hard to pick a favorite. I've been here enough to summarize the following menu highlights. The fried spring rolls, fried calamari, and larb are the best appetizers I've had in this town. The Pad Thai and Pad Se Ew here are fresh-tasting, delicious noodles you've got to try. If you can handle a little spice, then try the Pad Kee Mao as well. If you like fried chicken, the fried rice with fried chicken and the crispy mango chicken are incredible! And I would also recommend a tase of the Massaman Gai curry before you top everything off with the fried ice cream or the sticky sweet rice with mango.

Some lesser known but still enticing menu items include the Khao Soi (which is great with their gluten free fried chicken) and the Lord of Noodles. Both of these are solid main courses you may or may not have tried elsewhere, made with the Noodle's signature Thai style. As for lesser known appetizers, try the Tom Kha soup, the Thai fish cakes, the chicken satay (which are totally addictive), and the papaya salad. These are not so famous but are very interesting choices.

This summer, they are adding Ka Na Moo Korb (pork belly with Chinese broccoli and egg) and cheesecake with Mitchell ice cream. I'm a real fan of these new options!

If you haven't tried the Noodle yet, I would definitely try it. Everything on the menu is so good. I know I'll be back for more!
A very clean place to grab lunch or dinner with 3-5 friends. Plan ahead for larger groups. Food was average but high quality dinnerware they serve in. Cleanliness top notch. Large portion size.

A wonderful find, light fresh food like Thai should be.
I looked in on the other Thai restaurants in the area but mostly looked hyped. This was the real deal which you could tell from the clientele and the footfall picking up for take out.

Last lunch seating is 2:00 which is strictly enforced.
Excellent value for the quality. The sashimi is very fresh and the sushi rice was perfectly seasoned. The space could be nicer, but the food makes it worth visiting. 10/10.

My partner and I had just finished playing Dave the Diver one night and got a massive sushi craving, so we looked up nearby spots and found this place. We enjoyed it so much that we came back the very next day，this time for takeout. The packaging was really nice, the prices are a great deal, and the flavors are legit. Pretty sure this is going to be our go-to sushi takeout spot from now on.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
The fish here is beyond delicious.  It’s the kind of meal you have and then wake up craving again.  Spectacularly simple but impressively memorable.

name: LIMEWOOD BAR & RESTAURANT

top_reviews.content:
We arrived at 7:45 AM. Parking is accessible immediately adjacent to the entrance, eliminating long pedestrian transit from the vehicle. Note on the parking procedure: upon parking, you must scan the barcode on the sign in the parking lot and fill out your information; later, when you receive your dining receipt at the end of the meal, scanning the barcode provided on that receipt zeros out the parking fee before you exit the property. However, as we walked from the parking lot toward the hotel entrance, the outdoor fire pit and lounge areas were left in a messy state from the previous night or shift, featuring unbusied glassware, empty bottles, stray beverage containers, and rumpled throws left completely unmanaged well before opening. Inside, the Claremont maintains a classic, historic aesthetic. The restaurant entrance is located just inside the hotel on the left, and service doors opened promptly at 8:00 AM.

We were seated at a window table with a clear, elevated view of San Francisco in the distance. Water was provided immediately, and order intake followed shortly after. The latte was functional but lacked depth; an additional shot would have improved flavor balance, though it remained enjoyable.

I ordered the Signature Breakfast with scrambled eggs, country potatoes, and chicken apple sausage, alongside a side of grilled sourdough. Execution across the plates was solid: the scrambled eggs were properly cooked, the potatoes were well-prepared, and the chicken apple sausage was flavorful with a balanced, mild sweetness. The side of grilled sourdough outperformed expectations, as the char added strong structural flavor. My dining companion's order, consisting of fried eggs, potatoes, and thick, chewy bacon, was reported as excellent across all metrics.

Service ran smoothly during the initial phase, with the waitress performing a midpoint check-in, and secondary staff efficiently clearing plates. However, post-clearance follow-through lapsed toward the end of the meal, as no staff returned to the table, requiring an approximate 12-minute wait before attention could be actively flagged to request the check.

Overall, food quality sits above average, and the combination of historic room architecture and unobstructed valley views adequately justifies the pricing structure.

I visited for the first time to attend my friend’s birthday dinner, and this stunning restaurant truly impressed me! Located inside the beautiful Clairmont hotel, it offers a spectacular sunset view over the bay. The staff is friendly and attentive, and the food quality is good. The atmosphere is elegant and upscale, but there is no dress code, so guests can dress casually or more formally. We came on a Saturday evening and there were still a few parking spaces available. There's a charge for parking based on hours parked.
Fancy little restaurant in the hotel with exceptional view to the tennis courts and SF bay. Service was excellent, the food was just ok.

Took my best friend here for a belated birthday celebration and definitely treated ourselves! Drinks were yummy, and portions were pretty fair. Food was decadent, though you definitely are paying a bit more for the ambiance. Go during golden hour and sunset for great photo ops and lighting, just don’t forget your sunnies 🌞

Beautiful views, very attentive service. The drinks were great, we shared a couple of small plates: corn and octopus. Spilt the pork entree so that we had room for the chocolate cake and strawberry torte for dessert

Chef Yosuke and his culinary team made our night very special.

Simple and delicious food, beautiful restaurant, great selection of Italian wines, and delicious cocktails.

Dolce Whisper or Dolce Whisperer? I can't rememberbthe name 😁, but that cocktail was so good.

100% recommended!

I ate here yesterday with my husband for the first time and it was very tasty.

We marked close by in the neighborhood. It was easy for us to find. I’m not sure what people are referring to when talking about windows getting smashed in a parking lot? But I did see broken glass in the library’s parking lot next door? FYI.

The food though was excellent. We got the fried olives, beet salad, pork chop, pasta dish (with crab and shrimp), tiramisu, and vanilla gelato.

My favorite was the beet salad (so refreshing!),
any of their house made pasta looks amazing, and the tiramisu was excellent.

Definitely would come again. Maybe next time I will consider doing their Oakland Restaurant deal which looked amazing but I couldn’t resist trying their pasta with the seafood :)

Fried olives were so good I almost choked to death, pizzas are good, just go ahead and order everything. Salmon was my fave! Finished with strong coffee and tiramisu. Drinks are all tasty as well. Staffs all super cool and the art they have up is dope!

A16 is Southern Italian food meets California. In a good way! The pizzas are excellent, with the true Neapolitan oven, especially recommended is the Montanara pizza which is briefly fried before being put in the pizza oven. Excellent also the appetizers, especially the squid with fried beans. And outstanding choice of Sicilian wines.

Almost every time we're in Berkeley, we come here as a family to eat. We had two college undergraduates, and typically end up celebrating most occasions here. Lots of options including vegetarian, vegan, friendly dishes. The salmon is perfectly crispy, moist, flavorful on a bed of vegetables. The pizzas, and specifically the pizza dough, are perfectly light, chewy, and flavorful. This place is such a vibe, and highly recommended if you're ever near the area.

top_reviews.content:
+ Extremely authentic and low profile. Feels like a family style restaurant and we saw lots of native Korean families there.
+ The soup is one of the best in the Bay Area. Rich and organic flavor. We ordered beef soup with tendon and tendons are so tender and soft that it almost melt in the mouth.
+ Large portions.
+ Owners are super friendly

The soups in this eatery are the bomb - we had seolleongtang (oxtail soup) and kalbitang (rib soup with mung bean noodles), both of which were nourishingly delicious. I had them with rice and it was just the perfect meal for a chilly day.

I liked it so much that I returned the next week - we had extra yukkejang, which was spicy and tasty and also the crispy and flavourful seafood pajeon.

This place has super fresh kim chee. Food comes out quickly. Their Kim Chee and chives pancake is perfect. I don't eat meat but my husband does and he was never disappointed with his order. He really likes their soup. The only thing to flag is that their soft tofu soup comes with pork even though it isn't listed on the menu. They were very nice to switch it out once I got it. Just wanted to flag for anyone who wanted the soft tofu soup but don't eat pork. The soft tofu soup with Kim Chee (no pork) is also totally yummy
Galbijim (braised beef soup) and sundaegug (rice blood sausage soup) were great. Expensive though — I’ve had same food at highly rated restaurants in other expensive cities for ~80% the price…

My family had an amazing Father’s Day meal at Seoul GomTang! We had many of their appetizers, soups, and noodle dishes. The food was amazing as usual - we were really happy with all of it. The portions were plentiful and the service was impeccable as well.

If you’re not sure what to order, I would look on the walls or ask the very nice server for advice. The owners know their food very well and try their best to help you out!

Overall, I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone curious about Korean food. Must try!

I'm definitely going to try to go to brunch here one weekend.

Great breakfast spot! Had lots of classic options and asian fusion dishes as well. The homestyle sausages was delicious, order extra when you're there.

My first time eating here. We came here on Sunday after spotting the place a month ago when we stopped by the Donut Farm.

name: Super Super Pho

top_reviews.content:
Super super pho is my go-to Vietnamese spot in Berkeley/Emeryville. And so reasonably priced.

I always get the original banh no with the pate. Soo good with the freshnwss of the herbs and acidity and sweetness of the pickled carrots and diakon.

The beef pho with 3 kinds of beef is warm and hearty. Their broth is clear and so flavorful.

Will be back again and again.

This was my husband’s and my first time trying this restaurant. When you arrive, you place your order and pay at the counter first, then take a seat in the dining area to enjoy your meal.

The prices are quite reasonable, and the food was pretty good overall. For me, the broth wasn’t as rich or flavorful as I had hoped, though they do give you a generous amount of it. The staff provided decent service — not outstanding, but not bad either.

There are several pho restaurants along this street, and this was the first one we decided to try. Overall, it wasn’t bad at all and definitely worth a visit, but it’s not quite my top favorite just yet.

Self-service, order food at the front and pay after ordering. Get your own drinks. Server will bring your food out. I got the combo pho, it was very delicious. So far the best soup/pho I had. The portion is great. Totally worth the price. Hot tea is strong and tasted great too!

Ideally, I'd give this place 2.5/5.

Usually, the Yelp reviews for a restaurant are always on point, and they've never let me down in the past, but this time, it was a different story.

Super Super Pho has a great setup for a casual dining experience. The covered patio with string lights and heaters looked inviting, and the counter service with "find your own seat" was convenient. We arrived right after opening, so there was no wait and service was very fast. Perhaps a little too fast...

Our food came out within minutes of ordering, which was concerning. Especially considering we had fried chicken wings, a dish that typically takes longer to prepare. Unfortunately, the wings were the biggest letdown. They were bland and undercooked, not crispy and flavorful like you'd expect.

The pho (super pho combination) itself was a mixed bag. The portion was generous, with plenty of meat (rare steak, well-done brisket, and beef balls). However, the broth was a major disappointment. It lacked depth of flavor and really needed a lot of doctoring with the provided condiments like lemon and Sriracha. The meat itself was also unevenly cooked - some parts were dry, others undercooked.

The Thai tea was decent. It was milky (not watered down, thankfully), but it had some chalky aftertaste.

On the plus side, the staff was friendly when we did manage to flag them down. However, with only one other table occupied during our entire visit, the inattentiveness was surprising. We had to track someone down for water and takeout boxes.

Given today's rainy weather, I was really looking forward to some comforting pho, but unfortunately, this place did not deliver.

This was my first visit, and since it was a rainy day, I decided to try their pho. There’s something comforting about a warm bowl of soup on a cold, wet day. The soup had a rich, deep flavor that was enjoyable, but not remarkable. For comparison, my favorite pho spot is still Pho Vi Hoa in Palo Alto, which I feel has more balanced and complex flavors.

Ordering here was straightforward. You place your order at the counter, and the staff delivers your food to the table. The service was efficient and friendly, which added to the overall experience.

For starters, I ordered A2: Fresh Shrimp Spring Rolls. They were fresh, light, and paired well with the accompanying peanut dipping sauce. As for the main dish, I went with the Rare Steak Pho, adding extra noodles for $2. While the broth and rare steak were satisfying, I realized the portion of noodles was already quite generous without the extra. If you’re someone with a hearty appetite, you’ll likely find the regular portion sufficient.

Next time, I’ll skip the extra noodles and focus on the base dish. It’s a solid spot for a comforting bowl of pho, but I’d still rank it below my go-to pho spot in Palo Alto.

We had the most delightful time interacting with the wonderful owners brother and sister Dynamic Duo
The Sushi is delicious!
Sushi is super fresh and a great portion in every bite.
They will definitely go back

Kiku Sushi delivers on quality in every way that matters. The fish is noticeably fresh, and the overall quality of the sushi is excellent. What really stood out is the variety, and we eat a lot of sushi. Kiku had rolls and preparations we genuinely hadn’t come across before, which is rare and a welcome surprise for anyone who thinks they’ve seen it all.

Beyond the food, the service was attentive without being intrusive, the kind of attentiveness that makes a meal feel taken care of from start to finish. Whether you’re a sushi regular or just getting into it, Kiku is worth a visit. We’ll definitely be back.

We absolutely love Kiku Sushi—it’s become such an important part of our neighborhood and our routine. Over the years, we’ve shared so many memorable meals here, and it has never let us down. The food is consistently excellent, and the warm, inviting atmosphere makes every visit special. It’s more than just a place to eat—it’s a meaningful tradition for us and a true local gem.

We absolutely love Kiku Sushi! It’s been our go-to spot for over 10 years, and it has truly become a cornerstone of the neighborhood for us. This cafe has been in the neighborhood for a long, long time and is a local favorite for breakfasts, brunches and lunches. The atmosphere is casual and diner-like and the foods as expected in a cafe style restaurant. There’s also some counter seating that looks into a busy open kitchen. It’s actually a nice place to hang out or meet up with someone.

Five Star classic Americana breakfast with a sleeper cafe latte that exceeded all expectations. As a test, I usually order the eggs Benedict and a while it wasn't overly innovative, was absolutely solid. (on second thought, I ordered a Blackstone) Hollandaise sauce was good, eggs cooked perfectly, and a home fries well,  yummy home fries. But the Cafe Latte was a surprise, so well made that I didn't need to sweeten it. This place is a slice of how this neighborhood used to be, and still here going strong after 50 years I believe. The food tasted like it was made with pure contempt — two bites in and I threw the entire thing away because it was that disgusting. I wouldn’t feed that garbage to a raccoon.

The staff somehow managed to be even worse than the food: rude, nasty attitudes, zero professionalism, and acting annoyed that customers even exist. If this place disappeared tomorrow, the local food scene would improve instantly. Absolute dumpster fire of a restaurant.

There’s at least one clearly labeled vegan option (the beyond burrito).

Unfortunately, the burrito was pretty lacking in flavor despite having ordered the spicy salsa roja. There was no acidity at all, and this resulted in a very bland filling. Some guacamole or salt or both might have helped round it out.

I pulled in here never hearing of it and found one of the great breakfast burritos of all time!
Get the Korean beef in the breakfast burrito, you’ll be glad you did!
And I always get it with refried beans and a side of sriracha cream

Cool place, friendly staff, big portions, decent flavor. A bit overpriced in my opinion. Many options in regards to protein and filling options (in response to another review, yes the steak was grey, but it tasted just fine). Verde salsa is good, rojo is INSANELY hot to me haha they also have taco Tuesday specials.

Burritos are always on point and they offer lots of vegan and vegetarian items. The refried beans have no lard and are so flavorful! Fantastic address for breakfast in Berkeley. Everything it should be.  Super friendly, delicious food and very correct prices. Too bad we don't have it like this in Belgium. From pancakes over delicious French toast to traditional and Mexican egg dishes. Oh yes, and very delicious scones. Highly recommended.

We spotted chilaquiles on a board behind the  counter as I was choosing my order. We got a Denver omelet,  chilaquiles,  and a breakfast burrito with chorizo added (to go.) I am not vegan; and this food was fresh, tasty, and felt homemade. We were all full, and loved our meal. I loved everything, especially the lentil and rice!!

The food was amazing, and somehow the service was even better. The woman who helped us treated us like family, and was the perfect balance of attentive and non-intrusive.

Highly reco. this spot to all. And wish them continued success! Their food is delicious, nutritious, clean, and healthy.

I love this place. Reliably tasty healthy food with just enough variety day to day to keep you coming back. I love that I don't have to order, just tell them how much I want. The moderate meal is a generous portion so I've never actually ordered the large.

So much gratitude for this place. Love the food and we're so grateful to have a quiet and peaceful place where humble, delicious, organic food is served by kind people. A true gem. Please keep doing what you do. I will be back soon.

Awesome, wholesome, healthy food. Soup is great and so tasty. Free hot tea and water help round out a perfect meal.

Order a medium-sized meal; plenty of it.

Really lovely vegan spot. Came here for lunch, perfect breeze, beautiful weather, got to enjoy the sun but also stayed in the shade. Lots of birds sounds. You pick either the moderate for $13 or full lunch for $15 and can add on kombucha or pies. We got the moderate, which were plenty of food. The flavors are rich and full bodied. Also would be a nice patio to take dogs to and enjoy a nice conversation with someone.

The environment is great for socializing, and the service is wonderful. The people who work there are extremely friendly and do what they can to make your time there enjoyable. It's a great place to hang out with friends and family.

The food, which is inspired by street food, is very solid. I wouldn't say it's the best or even that impressive, but it's also not bad in any way. The burgers there are everything you would expect from a typical street food burger. I'd say they were just tasty, satisfying and easy to eat that I had no real complaints. That said, the food, including the burgers, didn't really excite me either.

In other words, the food is just good enough not to ruin your dining experience with friends and family. I don't love the food, but it's not half bad and the restaurant still appeals to me as a place to socialize.

Really excellent spot, and close to the freeway if you’re just driving through the east bay and need a break.

I only got the burger and bacon jam fries, I think the burger was called the traffic jam. Really good w the cheese and fried egg, and for as messy as it was, the bun held up to the end. Fries were good, the bacon jam on the sweet dude, but also really excellent. The beer came from a brewery next door, also really good.

Service was great, staff all friendly. While I’m not often in this area, this is on a short list to revisit and try something else.

Who would have thought the combination of Dim Sum and burger could go so well together? It’s the best of both worlds, and it’s good that different people can have different food when they visit. Everything we tried was tasty (from burger to dim sum to fried rice). Would definitely return for more!

I’m so happy that we stopped in for brunch today! Another spot was busy with rude people from the moment we parked. Everything was scrumptious. Got my kid homemade chicken tenders and fries. There’s a batch of soufflé pancakes being prepped in the back (call ahead if you want them)!

Can’t recommend this cozy spot enough. There’s no sign but the atmosphere is unmatched in the warm, friendly service and I’ve never tried anything that isn’t downright delicious.

good food, on the expensive side so def save up before coming here! staff is very friendly and attentive. i had the pesto burger it was so good 😭 truffle fries to share, amazing and crispy!!!

This place is a cute local joint (now with several Bay locations) on the charming College Ave in Rockridge. They advertise as gourmet burgers, and they definitely are — but with all the possible toppings, be prepared to pay quite a bit for each add-on you’re interested in.

I ordered the Moroccan Burger (with sprouts) and the skinny fries, to-go. They prepped my food quickly and it gave me a few minutes to walk around the area and check out the cute cafes. It’s a short walk from the BART station, but there’s also plenty of parking on College Ave (I had no problem parking).

I’d definitely recommend the pretzel bun, as the soft and salty flavor added a unique twist to the burgers. The meat was tasty and you can specify if you want medium rare, medium, or well-done. I also liked how the toppings were overflowing — you might have to pay $3.50 to add something like crispy onions to your burger, but for that price they’ll make sure you get more than enough to fill your burger (and plate!).

Overall, it’s a nice choice for a casual burger in Rockridge.

I wasn’t there for too long, but it felt like I was being rushed. It’s too bad because I’ve had some great experiences here in the past. Let’s hope that this is a one time deal and not the new normal.

I had a fantastic dinner at this place. The food was prepared in a way that made me feel like I had my own personal chef. Everyone greeted me with a smile, making it feel as if we were old friends catching up after a long time apart. My date and I were thoroughly impressed by the ambiance and the lively neighborhood outside. I’ll definitely return to enjoy more of this delicious food!

name: Mount Everest Restaurant
address: 2598 Telegraph Ave, Berkeley, CA 94704, United States

top_reviews.content:
This is genuinely the BEST restaurant in all of Berkeley, and I do not say that lightly. I’ve eaten at a lot of places around here, and nothing compares to this spot. Every single time I walk in, I’m greeted by the sweetest and kindest workers I’ve ever met in Berkeley. They are always so welcoming, warm, and genuinely happy to see you, which already makes the experience feel special before you even start eating.

Now the food is absolutely incredible. The chicken tikka masala is honestly one of the best dishes I’ve had anywhere. The sauce is rich, creamy, and packed with flavor, and the chicken is always perfectly cooked and tender. It’s the kind of dish where you keep saying “just one more bite” and suddenly the whole bowl is gone. The garlic naan is also amazing, soft, warm, buttery, and perfectly garlicky. It’s literally the perfect thing to scoop up the tikka masala with. I could honestly eat the naan alone and still be happy.

And you cannot leave without getting the mango lassi. It’s so refreshing and smooth, and it balances the spices from the food perfectly. It’s sweet, creamy, and honestly one of the best mango lassis I’ve ever had.

Another thing that makes this place stand out is the price and generosity. Berkeley can be pretty expensive when it comes to food, but this restaurant somehow manages to serve amazing quality food at a really good price. On top of that, they are incredibly generous, they almost always give us extra food or something for free, which is honestly so kind and makes the experience feel even more special. It feels like they truly care about their customers and want everyone to leave happy.

What I love most is that this place feels genuine and welcoming, not just another restaurant trying to rush people in and out. The workers are so friendly and kind, and the atmosphere is always warm. You can tell they take pride in their food and care about the people who come in.

If you’re anywhere near Berkeley and want amazing Nepalese food, this is the place you have to go. The chicken tikka masala, garlic naan, and mango lassi combination is absolutely unbeatable. Great food, incredible people, generous portions, and such a great experience every time. You can NOT beat the price or quality anywhere.

I honestly recommend this place to everyone I know. 10/10 — the best restaurant in Berkeley.
Excellent!!! The BEST Indian Food in Berkeley! Must try! Chicken Tikka Masala my favvvv! Lunch specials great deal too! Mango Lassi, lemonades, chai OMG SOOO GOOD!

The food is always 10/10!! This is the best Indian food in Berkeley & I guarantee you will LOVE whatever you get. Everything is so fresh & tastes amazing. The staff here is AMAZING. They are all so kind & make the experience amazing. My favorite is the butter chicken I highly recommend!!! You need to try this place for lunch they have an amazing $11 lunch special. One of my favorite spots in berkeley!
The service was amazing! It felt so homey and the food came out so fast. The kadai chicken and momos are to die for!!!

A gem hidden in plain sight !! This place has been around since I was in high
school (over a decade) and although it seems it may be receiving less foot traffic during the summer months, this is not a restaurant to miss!
I got the lunch set with lamb curry. The meat is tender, the spice perfect, the curry flavorful and delicious. It also came with a generous portion of naan and rice, plus chana on the side and a nice salad.
The rose lassi is also a refreshing choice, not too sweet :)

Service was so wonderful, warm and helpful staff. 100/10!
For under $20 it’s a great deal for lunch and a great place to visit.
Come check it out!

Everyone who works here is super kind and we have not had a bad experience at all

Take a look at some of the pictures I posted for the latest menu and what we got. The highlight for me was the duck confit and banana flan. Oh I can’t forget the steak and fruits perfectly cooked. The gnocchi with mushrooms was also very memorable. Let’s be real. I pretty much liked everything I ate.

Drinks I tried something that was supposed to remind you of nacho cheese. It was interesting for sure. Probably not the drink I would go for, but you do actually get reminders of sitting at a ballpark eating nacho cheese. Try it if you’re feeling adventurous.

Def will be back

Easily the best meal I've had at a restaurant in a while.

The Tuna Tartare was my favorite item of the night. It had so much flavor within the first bite.

The Maude Burger was really good.

The Short Rib and Rib plate was ridiculously good. Both meats were cooked perfectly. The sauce on the ribs is pretty spicy, but if you're not into that, I'd have them put it on the side.

I would definitely recommend this place, especially for group outings.

An amazing throwback to the era of sophisticated delicious food, an extensive menu, affordable nice wines, friendly attentive service, and comfortable quiet tables all at fair (not crazy) prices, in a neighborhood restaurant that is easy to book!  The seafood and vegetable-based appetizers and main dishes, breads, and desserts we ordered were wonderful.  (Did not try any meats.) We lingered over a Sunday night dinner for a couple of hours.

I really wanted to like this more. First time going, maybe one more try?
Went on a Thursday at about 6:30, plenty of tables available, no reservation, seated immediately. Got a brand new server - truly, it was his second day. Very sweet, polite guy, but didn't know anything yet. Took a long time for him to come take our drink orders (fatal mistake in the profit margin game of restaurants) and then didn't know what we ordered, but fair to him he probably wasn't or just barely 21 himself, so...

Menu selection is classically Italian, with a good mix of northern and southern cuisines. We ordered the risotto; good, not something we'd order again, but fair enough, and the squid ink pasta. Again, good, but depth of flavor was tragically missing. It needed a deep tomato/umami base that just wasn't there. With that, I think it would've been great - an inventive dish. I ordered it because you don't see it in a lot of places and I would not likely make it at home. So close, but no cigar. Everything else on theenu of course contained pork and milk, neither of which is edible to us, so that left us with few choices.

I will give the atmosphere and the senior wait staff (who took over for the kid, he might have been in the back trying to pronounce Fortaleza) a 4 star rating - both lovely, but not quite enough to make up for the early missteps and lackluster meals. This Korean-style Chinese restaurant located in Oakland, California, offers a variety of delightful dishes such as Tangsu-yuk (sweet and sour pork), fried dumplings, Jjajang-myon (black bean paste noodles), and Jjampong (spicy seafood noodles). The fried dumplings were exceptional, boasting a crispy exterior and a succulent, well-seasoned filling of pork and vegetables. The sweet and sour pork was equally impressive, with a delightful blend of sweetness in the sauce complementing the perfectly fried pork strips. While the noodle dishes were enjoyable, the texture of the noodles did not quite meet expectations, lacking the desired hand-stretched quality. The green chili sweet potato noodles provided a tasty kick with hot chili. The service was excellent, though there is room for improvement in the restaurant's overall ambiance to elevate the dining experience.

The service was pretty standard. I wasn't really expecting this style of jajang mian maybe because this one is more Korean and not as Chinese like I'm used to, or this is the more traditional kind? The noodles were pretty chewy which was fun but the sauce was too much and I'm not sure what the flavor was but it was maybe too overwhelming with not enough substance or toppings in it.

It’s truly a gem of the bay. This is probably the best Chinese/korean food in the bay. The jjajangmyeon, jjajang and tangsuyuk is all we come for. Sadly, the last time we visited, the current owners of the restaurant are retiring and handing off the business to a new owner. I can’t say it’ll ever be the same. They’re training the current staff right now, but I don’t if it’ll ever feel the same…

top_reviews.content: If you’re just looking for a reliably good pizza place, this spot definitely delivers. They’ve got a really nice dough, tasty cheese, and a sauce that pulls everything together into a pretty satisfying personal pizza. They also have some nice drink options and a good range of wines if that’s your thing. Overall, it’s just a really nice place to grab a good pizza.

*For context, this review is largely for vegans (3.5/5 stars).

Had a reservation on a Friday evening on the back patio. Beautiful weather for the back patio. I had emailed the restaurant in advance to check on vegan menu items, and they assured me that most of the menu items can be made vegan. There seems to be some confusion between the staff and management though since when I came to the restaurant it wasn't as vegan friendly as advertised (e.g., it turns out the gigante beans could not be made vegan). That being said, they were still able to make vegan the two pizzas I was interested in the She Wolf and the Old Faithful. They use Daiya cheese which looks great, but doesn't have the strongest taste profile and texture isn't amazing when it cools down. We asked for salt to increase the taste on the pizza, but think they could do a lot more to increase the flavor profile on both pizzas, since we've had similar pizza toppings elsewhere that were more flavorful. (Honestly, the toppings combination for both pizzas were excellent, but a little undersalted with the current vegan cheese choice.) Both pizzas were still solid though. I am bummed I missed my opportunity to try the pizza back when they used Butcher's Son cheese. There's tons of better tasting vegan supermarket cheeses out there over Daiya too (Parmela, Good Planet, Miyokos, etc.), but perhaps they use Daiya because it melts nicely/better or they haven't tried the others. Food was good but could still do better, especially knowing the strong competition for pizza, vegan and non-vegan.

Highlight:
Delicious vegan-friendly pizza in a spotless space with a patio you’ll want to linger on.

Restaurant:
This cozy Berkeley pizza spot takes pride in crafting high-quality pies with fresh ingredients and thoughtful flavor combinations. The atmosphere is relaxed yet well-kept, and the charming patio is the kind of space that makes you want to extend your meal just to soak it all in.

Service:
Service here is warm, welcoming, and attentive without feeling rushed. Staff members know their menu well and seem genuinely happy to guide you toward great choices. The care they put into the dining experience is evident from start to finish.

Food:
We enjoyed a vegan pizza topped with sausage and peppers, and it was packed with flavor—savory, well-balanced, and cooked to perfection. The vegan Caesar salad was another standout, with a creamy, flavorful dressing that didn’t feel like a compromise. Every bite spoke to the attention paid to quality and freshness.

Recommendations:
Whether you’re vegan, vegetarian, or just a pizza lover, this is a must-visit. Grab a spot on the patio if the weather’s nice, and don’t skip the vegan Caesar—it’s a pleasant surprise. The spotless dining area and even cleaner bathroom say a lot about how much the team cares. Highly recommend for anyone seeking top-notch pizza in Berkeley.

They have Mediterranean / Palestinian standards but with a twist; the flavor combos are so clever and they always taste amazing. They have slightly different menu items for dinner vs brunch so I’d really recommend trying both for the full experience. My favorites are too many to name but honestly you can’t go wrong—but the pancake is definitely top notch. Other favorites include the toum fries, the lentil soup, rotti wrap…actually you know what everything is good. I really don’t think you can go wrong. They also have vegetarian and vegan options, as well as other dietary restrictions options. Parking can be found on the street, though might be crowded during peak hours. I wish they were open more days of the week, it’s only Thursday - Sunday for now, but maybe in the future that will change…?

Was really sad to see my favorite unique + quality brunch spot in the bay change format to being fast casual. It was such an easy brunch pick to take out of towners or friends to.

Now instead, they've become easily one of the best fast-casual food in the bay. So I really can't complain.  I guess their format changed worked because I've eaten here more often than when they were full service. The value for the money you get here is pretty nuts. Still just as good ingredients & just as good preparation, all at a more approachable price point & form factor. When you compare to some of the other casual lunch/dinner places in the area that have a similar format, it's really no competition. top_reviews.content: Hard to find but worth the search Thai food in downtown Berkeley.  Found this delicious food paradise close to UCB campus.  Tried the pineapple fried rice, but there was so much volume to it, I had to split it.  It had an undertone of curry flavor in it, a good amount of pineapple but not quite enough cashews for my taste.  The rice had just the right amount of oil to make everything more flavorful but not overly greasy.  The Thai iced tea was smooth and easy to drink without being over sweet.  The dining room was simple and easy to navigate, and the staff was helpful.  There’s an option for touch panel ordering for cashless orders or cash only options if you want to talk to an actual person while placing your order.  The menu is long, but not so much so that it’s overwhelming.
The food was pretty mediocre for its price, but my vegetarian coworker said his dish of rice was pretty good.

The veggie fried rice was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned with a great balance of textures. The portion size was very good and the spice level was well balanced. The veggie pad see ew was equally satisfying, with soft noodles, crisp vegetables, and a rich savory sauce. Overall, both dishes were comforting and delicious and definitely worth trying again.

Rats!

Eating there and I saw a rat run from under the fridge back into the kitchen, then later walking up in the ceiling decor.

Food is great for the price and area, downside is there are rats all over the neighborhood, I just wished they kept them out of the restaurant. It's too bad, I've been going here for years, hope they clean it up.

Thai Basil in Berkeley offers a convenient option for a quick Thai food fix. I tried their Basil Chili Chicken with fried egg, which was a decent portion size. The chicken itself was cooked well, but the overall flavor lacked the punch I was hoping for.

The ambiance of the restaurant is pretty basic, with simple décor and generic Asian-style furniture. It's clean and comfortable enough for a casual meal, but the inside space may feel very crowded when you have a few occupied tables. There is open seating outside the restaurant, which is shared by all the other restaurants in that section, so it's available on a first come, first served basis.

The service was fast but the staff could have been friendlier. When my friends and I asked for to-go boxes and utensils/napkins, we got an angry look from the staff. Please also note that the restaurant doesn't have a bathroom for its customers, so you'll have to find some place else if you really need to go.

Overall, Thai Basil is an average option. The food is decent, but a little pricey for what you get. If you're in the area and looking for a quick bite, it's not a bad choice, but there are probably better Thai restaurants in Berkeley worth exploring.

Brought my wife to this spot because we saw it on IG. I wanted to surprise her with a date night. They were showcasing their Christmas themed atmosphere. I made a reservation because it was suggested if going on the weekend. They get very packed. I made the reservation through their website. It was easy.

We got there and immediately noticed how beautifully festive it was. That was really beautiful and intentional. My wife was real happy with her surprise. We were seated immediately, so that was a plus.

Our waitress provided helpful food and drinks suggestions. We ordered chicken wings as appetizers, I ordered Pad See Eew and my wife ordered the dry glass noodles with various meats and tofu (I forgot the name). The wings should have came out 1st.. but that was not the case. My food came out 1st without my wife's. The chicken wings came out about 5 to 7 miss later and then my wife's food came out.. about 2 mins after the wings.

While we both enjoyed our entrees, the wings were undercooked. Like they seemed done, but you could tell and taste that they needed to have fried a bit longer. One of them had a little redness on the bone. Nonetheless, we ate them. Our drinks were so delicious. She had the green Christmas one and I had the blue Christmas one. We put Soju (Korean alcohol) in them both. So far, the night was actually Purdue decent minus those lil hiccups. However, when the waitress came over to check on us and asked us if we needed boxes for the leftovers, we said we did.. but I still had half a drink left. Sure then brought the boxes and check. I did not understand why because I was actually going to order more drinks. However, at that point, I felt like we were being rushed to get up from our table. I told her that I was not ready for the check and she was adamant about me placing it on my section of the seating. I had to tell her again.. that we did not ask for the check and that we were not ready to leave yet. She walked away and then less than 5 mins from when she came.. someone else brought the bill. I had to day the same thing to him to.. that we were not ready for the bill.

I did not like that at all. No one else around us was provided the bill while so having food/drinks on front of them. I watched the movements, so why did this happen to us? No one should be rushed to get up while still enjoying their meal and/or drinks.

Although this did not happen to us, I am still putting it into my review due to witnessing it. The party next to us found a small crystal that looked exactly like glass in their noodle dish. One of them actually had it in his mouth due to taking a bite of his food. He stated that it was hard and definitely not food. He reported it to the same waitress who simply said " Oh sorry, do you want me to get you a new plate of food". She did not ask him if he was alright nor did she bring any manager over too talk matters over with them. They agreed to a new plate, but after we all discussed what just happened, they decided to get the plate of food taken off the bill. Even when they attempted to do that, they were met with the food is already cooking.. so they had to push a little bit to be heard. She took it off of the bill. I disliked how that situation was met. Lack of full apology, no managerial apology nor followup, no automatically insisting to clear it from the bill without being asked by the customer and the fact that they do expected the customer to pay any bill after going through possibly eating glass. My wife and I were appalled.
