top_reviews.content: This place has become one of my go-to lunch spots since I work right across the street🥰I order from here all the time during work, and the food is always consistent. The Hainan chicken is super tender and flavorful, never dry, and the rice is really fragrant too. I also love the sauces that come with it. Portions are good, the staff is always friendly, and the food comes out pretty fast, which is perfect when I’m busy at work. I’ve already ordered so many times and will definitely keep coming back. Highly recommend if you’re nearby and want something delicious and healthy！

I payed $20 for a cut up chicken tender over rice. Really confused because I’ve eaten here before and got a normal portion size. I ordered the mixed chicken, what I received was literally tiny scraps of hainanese chicken and the tiniest bit of crispy chicken. This photo is BEFORE I took any bites, I thought the chicken was under the rice or something so I was digging up the rice with my fork I was so confused. What the hell is this portion, I genuinely can’t believe they packed this up and allowed this to be sent to a customer. Never coming back. DO NOT COME HERE
The khao man gai here is very yummy. Less than $20 with big food portions. I feel like I'm in Thailand again when I have each bite. Very good

The portion size was bigger than I thought ans overall wait time wasn't that long!

Ordered the Mixed Chicken Rice and both portion of the chicken was handful and taste pretty good! Also comes with a soup though didn't try that much.

Near hotel we were staying at. I’ve eaten a lot of Hainan chicken growing up and I’ve missed it so much had to go in a get it. It did not disappoint! My daughter got the fried chicken and loved it. And the Hainan chicken was perfect! You have to understand Hainan chicken are serve room temp or slightly cold and bland you add the sauce to it. Took it to go because they were closing. The behind the counter workers were also super nice and helpful.

reviews_snippets.content: "Nice staff, nice service and nice atmosphere."

Been going here since freshman year, its good and relatively affordable. Decent sized portions, the bibimbap always makes me full! Food tastes like how i ate at home! I reccomend the spicy soondubu on a cold day, bibimbap, and japchae!
Great Korean restaurant in Berkeley. amazing food, service and atmosphere

That we're here once a week, and notice other regulars, says something. This is authentic Korean comfort food made with care. Feels like we're eating at owners Heera and Jacob's dining table. Thanks to them and their hardworking crew.
i love this place i’ve been going here for 2 years and it never disappoints. AMAZING FOOD AND STAFF!🙌

name: Dolly's

top_reviews.content:
My husband and I were recently recommended to try Dolly’s restaurant and we’re so glad we did. From the moment we walked in, the whole experience felt relaxed and welcoming. The hosts and owners were incredibly warm and friendly.

The food was delicious. We loved the cheese wheel pasta, the bread and tomato salad, and they also had a really good wine selection. As a small business owner myself, I always appreciate supporting local family-owned spots that truly care about good food and good service. Dolly’s is definitely one of those places. We’ll absolutely be back.

We came here because of the 4.8 star rating and I’m still trying to figure out how that happened. We spent nearly $100 for fast-food quality (or worse) pasta and slow service. I ordered the Alfredo in the Parmesan wheel with smoked salmon. The sauce was incredibly watery and seemed like it was just jarred sauce boiling in a vat. It didn’t even seem like the place had a stove. The pasta was precooked and warmed up before being mixed with the watery sauce and tossed in the cheese wheel. Then they put a whole package of smoked salmon on top, not cut up or mixed in or anything. The only upside was that the servers were very nice! They kept offering us free wine. I’m not sure if they knew it was an off night or if that is the norm there. Based on the kitchen they seem to have I’m not sure how it could be much better.

What do you get when you take a young Sri Lankan chef, (Dolly) who studied under a master of Italian cuisine, (Ruggero Milano, of Milano ristorante in Tiburon), an obsession with fresh pastas, imported desserts and gelatos and add one of the best wine lists in the East Bay and a giant authentic Permesano Regiano cheese wheel?

You get my new favorite Italian place in the Bay Area.
In an out of the way location, one block from the Rialto theaters in El cerrito, this area is mostly known for its Asian cuisine which I have covered extensively, but lo and behold! An authentic Italian ristorante, with a real trained Italian chef, and a casual laid-back setting and unassuming vibe.

Following my patented strategy of emulating success, I asked the guy next to me, (Who turned out to be a baseball scout, and looked super happy with what he was eating) what to order, and he recommended the Smoked salmon Fettuccine Alfredo.
I ordered it and I watched the careful preparation of perfect pasta ending with a generous toss in a Parmesan cheese wheel, and a glass of Daou Cabernet.
Dolly really knows what she's doing, and has set a new standard for my fettuccine enjoyment, and while the dish was so rich I felt guilty eating it alone, she still gave me a spoonful of REAL Italian spumoni, flown in recently.
This place is a kind of restaurant we need more of in the East Bay. Unassuming, friendly, homey, first class Italian food for the people. I cannot recommend this place highly enough if you want to have an actual Italian food experience but need to stick close to the east bay.
And by real Italian I don't mean some shishi spot that's going to charge you $100 to bring out three olives and a single slice of veal, I'm talking about real, hearty, delicious Italian food for the people.
Thanks Dolly.
Strategy: go see a movie at the Rialto, one block away, and arrange to have some Italian food afterwards. You'll be glad you did

I went there with my partner, and the wheel cheese is amazing! They have a balanced style, very soft, chewy, and milky at the same time. The owner is so nice! We had a wonderful time! Definitely will go back!

A lovely, cozy place in El Cerrito. Family owned. Friendly service and friendly customers!  And a Fettuccine Alfredo to die for! Great salads as well and imported Italian desserts. My friend and I split the Mozzerella Fresca and the Fettucine Alfredo and it was plenty. We didn’t have room for a dessert, but we will be back!

I ordered the Spicy Beef Noodle Soup, which was similar to Bun Bo Hue in spirit but much more simplified. The sate had a nice lemongrass aroma, a good amount of heat and  elevated the pho broth. Broth was on the sweeter side, but worked with the strong flavors of the sate.

I stumbled into this local gem by accident and found one of the best and most filling bowl of pho in Piedmont! Small menu but I love the spicy beef pho and their pork chop rice. You order at the counter and they bring the food to your table. Pretty much self service but we like minimalist interactions. I hope more people discover this family run restaurant!

We were in the area so we stopped by for lunch. We found parking a couple blocks away. Service was fast. Iced Vietnamese coffee was good. I appreciate the portion sizes. Garlic noodles were great. Shrimp was grilled well.

A Must-Visit East Bay Gem for Spectacular Vietnamese Comfort Food!
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
If you are looking for perfectly executed, deeply flavorful Vietnamese classics, Monsoon in Piedmont is an absolute must-visit. The ambiance is welcoming, but it’s the kitchen’s mastery over crunch, seasoning, and texture that will make you a regular.
On my latest visit, a few standout dishes completely stole the show:
The Standouts
• The Egg Rolls: Hands down some of the best around. They arrive piping hot, shattering into a crisp, flaky crunch with every bite. The filling is perfectly seasoned, savory, and dense without being greasy. Wrap them in fresh lettuce with a dip of nước chấm, and it’s pure perfection.
• The Fried Chicken Wings: Absolute perfection. They hit that elusive sweet spot—shatteringly crisp on the outside while remaining incredibly juicy and tender on the inside. The garlic and savory glaze coats them beautifully without making them soggy. They are addictive.
• The Pork Chop: This is the ultimate test of a great Vietnamese spot, and Monsoon nails it. The pork chop is beautifully marinated with distinct notes of lemongrass and garlic, boasting a gorgeous char from the grill. It’s incredibly tender, packed with smoky flavor, and avoids the dryness you find at lesser spots. Pair it with broken rice, and you have a flawless meal.

Monsoon delivers massive flavor, excellent execution, and fantastic consistency. Whether you're dropping in for a casual weeknight dinner or grabbing takeout, the quality is always top-tier.
Do not skip the wings as an appetizer, and make sure someone at your table orders the pork chop. I’ll definitely be back to work my way through the rest of the menu!

I recently visited Chandni Chowk and had an amazing dining experience. From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere felt vibrant and welcoming, capturing the lively spirit of Indian street food culture while still being comfortable for a relaxed meal.

I started with the Tikki Chaat, and it was outstanding. The tikki was perfectly crisp on the outside and soft inside, topped with flavorful chutneys, yogurt, and spices that created a great balance of sweet, tangy, and savory flavors. Every bite was packed with authenticity and reminded me of the chaat stalls back in India.

For the main course, I ordered the Goat Nihari along with Garlic Naan. The nihari was rich, aromatic, and slow-cooked to perfection. The goat was tender and full of flavor, while the gravy had the perfect blend of spices without being overpowering. It tasted homemade and authentic, which is hard to find.

The Garlic Naan was fresh, soft, and beautifully baked with just the right amount of garlic and butter. It paired perfectly with the nihari, making every bite even more enjoyable. The portion sizes were generous, and the quality of the food exceeded my expectations.

The customer service was also amazing they were keep checking on us and the food took no time to reach our tables hot and nice.

Overall, Chandni Chowk delivered an authentic and memorable dining experience. The food was flavorful, fresh, and clearly prepared with care. If you’re looking for delicious Indian cuisine with authentic flavors, I highly recommend trying the Tikki Chaat, Goat Nihari, and Garlic Naan. I’ll definitely be returning to explore more of the menu.

My boyfriend and I have been loyal customers here since our freshman year (we are about to graduate now)! The food and service is great. We really recommend. Thank you for a great 4 years❤️
The samurai, Philadelphia, lion king, and highway rolls are all very amazing. Highly recommend!

Genuinely my favorite place to grab food amongst all the places on Durant. Been coming here since my first year at Cal and I’ve never been disappointed. I'm not sure who prepared my food, but I am truly in disbelief at how they got this so wrong; Ordered a salmon ($9 upcharge, ouch) bowl with chimichurri mushrooms, received bland chicken and inedible sweet potatoes instead (somehow they were way overcooked on the outside and not cooked at all on the inside). Not sure how they can call this steamed broccoli "charred broccoli" either, but at least it's broccoli. Kind of a major bummer to pay almost $30 for an entirely incorrect order.

I got their Spring Noodle Bowl 🥣 with Double Plant Protein Patty and a chocolate chip cookie. The noodle bowl was okay - lots of fiber, but I do recommend getting extra protein with it to feel full. Besides the food, the staff were super friendly, and the atmosphere was wonderful.

Hooray! Somebody is making great quality food that I can eat.  😁

A local stand-by: so Bay Area. The ingredients are top-notch, and the food is nourishing and a very welcome departure from the “standard-American diet”, or “SAD”!

The staff seem well-treated by management.

I love coming here with my kiddo or guests. Casual and relaxed vibes with interesting, chill clientele. I recommend the fries, the green smoothie, the burrito bowl, and the power bowl. Enjoy!

Cost with tax: $20
What/When: Poke bowl. I was a walk in order and got it to go today. When you’re as active as I am, when it’s time to fuel it’s time to fuel. We’re scouting the region and this was my first order. We will likely move to the area.

My biggest expectation is that food is prepared to expectation and taste. This tuna poke bowl was poorly seasoned and overwhelmed by onion fillers.

There was no poke preparation. There was no soy/ponzu marinade on anything, and definitely not on the tuna. It was naked tuna.

There were two types of onions in this “poke” bowl which made it super overwhelming and taste bad - green onions (white bulb ends and green ends) and what was obviously a too-quick-pickle on onions. They completely just tasted like raw onion without a pickling and didn’t work at all.

The chipotle mayo also didn’t work.

I suggest someone with a good pallet go back to the drawing board with the tuna poke bowl and please, for the love of customers, don’t leave out the actual poke marinade.

top_reviews.content:
Stunned by the quality of this unassuming banh mi place on Northside. The quality of the bread was excellent -- both crunchy and chewy.

The portions were huge. For happy hour, you can get a huge sandwich for only around $8, pre-tax. I also got both the shrimp spring rolls and grilled pork spring rolls. Usually I like shrimp more, but this place's grilled pork spring roll had a solid char that I really liked/made it more unique.

The peanut sauce is ammitedly, not the best l, but the rest of the food more than made up for it.

Will definitely be back for the excellent and filling food.

First time trying Banh Mi and I LOVE it!! (⁎⁍̴̛ᴗ⁍̴̛⁎)❤️
Their crispy baguette sandwich taste AMAZING and their smoothie is also super awesome!!

I’ve also tried their Shrimp Egg Rice Plate, and it’s was really good as well! Their food tasted healthy and fresh, no heavy cream nor sauce that most restaurants have.
But you could also add their sauce packages yourself if you prefer strong flavor or spicy.

If you’re a vegetarian, pescatarian, or just live eat healthy, this is a definitely a great place for you (a log of veggies dishes, including their spring rolls and banh mi) ! And their meat dishes are amazing as well!
The shrimp rice plate is one of my favorite. The eggs are tender and the seasoning is just right, fresh and tasty.
The spring rolls are also really good, especially their sauce ☺️
You could tell them not to add cream or sugar if you don’t want it. My favorite smoothie flavor here is avocado, but they also have other flavors.
You could have coffee here, but it’s Vietnam coffee, which is similar to iced coffee that is sweet and dense.

They don’t have a large inside space, but they do have some outdoor seats. And since most people take out their orders, you could still find a seat if you’d like to dine in. They don’t have restroom available for customers, but the new Mind Coffee beside the place does. It’s a good “combo” schedule for me to have lunch and then go to the cafe afterwards!

Definitely one of my favorite restaurants on Euclid Ave 🥰

# Mini Turkey Sandwich 🥖
# Avocado Smoothie 🥑
# Shrimp Scrambled Egg Rice Plate 🍳

We had both their (Crispy Roast Pork Belly Banh Mi) and (Shrimp Spring Rolls) which were both great! The bread was crunchy and fresh paired with all the crispy veggies as well! The spring rolls paired with their peanut sauce was great as well. We were also able to order ahead using Snackpass!

It's been a while since I've been back to this place. I got 5 sandwiches with the discount and brought them back home. The whole family got food poisoning that afternoon. The bread and fillings didn't even taste that spectacular given the price.

Came here Saturday morning for a delicious fried egg sandwich & Vietnamese iced coffee -

Very lovely new seating area to eat with the rebrand and easy to order using Snackpass app or the terminals. Owner and staff are gracious and super friendly.

top_reviews.content: Absolutely delicious I’ve been on a quest for the tastiest butter chicken for the last few years and have tried many places and this spot takes first place!!! I will be back. The restaurant itself is so cute and beautifully decorated
I'm so happy to have this little indian place near my work.  Their food is absolutely great.  The samosa comes with 2 sauces.  One is sweet and another green one is very spicy (love it!).   I ordered

We went to this place because of the reviews. I would say I wasn't as impressed as the other reviewers.

First the good things:

- The place inside and the decor was good.
- The service was attentive too.
- Pani puri was presented nice
- Their homemade spicy sauce was excellent.

What I didn't like:

- The paneer tikka masala was bland. Paneer felt very fresh in the sauce and it didn't have to time to soak flavors
- The tikka masala sauce had no salt but we could remedy that easily
- Pani puri had no tangy sauce in it. I had to ask for it separately

I wanted to give this place a 3.5* but I rounded it to 4.

Still it was good place to try. I hope they can improve with this feedback.

We were just wandering by, thinking about going to Smokehouse for burgers when this overwhelmingly delicious aroma of Indian food wafted across our path. Do not pass this spot by. The flavors are amazing - we ordered pani puri, lamb vindaloo, okra bindi, mango pickles and garlic nann. I only have a picture of the pani puri because we were too busy eating the rest when it arrived at our table. Service was sweet and attentive. So glad we stopped by!

Solid Indian cuisine that’s open til 10pm. Carry out orders are ready in 15min. I got the chicken tikka masala and malai kofta with one garlic naan. It was well made albeit a touch salty. Naan could’ve been slightly fluffier. Just an observation not really a complaint. Will come back here for their lunch buffet and to try more things.

Edit July 2026 - finally went in to try their lunch buffet

Selection is limited, and I felt some of the dishes were just fillers

The saag paneer could definitely use some more paneer. The chicken tikka masala was good but was a little watery. Could be thicker.

Garlic naan was one of the best I’ve had in some time. Memorable.

Dishes are still a touch salty.

No desert, and tea is not included in the buffet. No sugar free sweeteners with the tea.

Tandoor chicken was cooked well but tad underpriced

No bowls with the plates. Which is not the best experience when you have multiple curries at the same time.

For $20 a person it’ll do in an otherwise expensive and competitive area.

I think I’ll stick with take out or dine in à la carte.

No. Just don't.
We ordered the tofu stew, cheese corn, kimchi pancake, chicken bibimbop, and bulgolgi. Cheese corn was soaked and the cheese was barley melted. No stone bowl for the bibimbop. The chicken in the bibimbop was stale and hard. The bulgolgi was insane pricy for dry beef that was somehow still wet and maybe 6 pieces In the whole plate of onions.  When the server stopped by and asked if everything was good I politely told him the kimchi pancake was overcooked and was soaking in it's own oil. He just said oh ok and walked away. No effort to fix it, offer to take it off the bill.

Even checking in later the host asked how the food was, despite us eating almost nothing other then the stew and a few topings off of the bibimbop(it was mostly stale rice) . We ate what we could of the bulgolgi because at the end 109 dollar bill is crazy for how not good it was. He still didn't care when he offered us to go boxes and we flatly said no. I understand not being a problem customer and complaining about everything but even the served rice was stale.
Save yourself and go somewhere else. Theres like 3 others spots nearby. We just wanted to try some where new....

Delicious Korean food, with amazing wings and delicious sides. Went for dinner and enjoyed everything. The wings are huge, perfectly cooked crispy and delectable sauces abound! Bigobi or however you spell it lol, was delicious and plentiful. Corn appetizer also amazing. One of the best Korean places I've been to good job guys! Keep it up

I have been thinking about To the Moon ever since I left Cali 😭 I’ll start with how kind the staff are—super attentive, friendly, tackled a huge wave of customers like absolute champs. Atmosphere wise, it’s pretty standard, not like a romantic spot or anything decor wise. We went at like 7pm expecting a wait…there was none. However, the restaurant was packed by 9pm or so, which has been SO different from all the other restaurants in SF, where things close by 9. So amazed this place is open til 2pm with how many tables they are able to turn.

Okay onto the food. Incredible, delicious, had leftovers bc the portions are huge. We ordered the menbosha which was crispy and not too salty. It was however, scorching hot haha. I got the pork bibimbob and my husband ordered the soondobu with pork. Both were super tasty. I couldn’t decide which I liked more so I would eat a spoonful of mine then a spoonful of his. The only let down here was the creamy steamed egg pot, which was a bit overcooked and lacked flavor. It was good dipped into the soup though, so no big deal. The BEST part though was the banchan….one of them was like a marinated eggplant banchan and oh my goodness that was so tasty!! Overall would def come back again. Only wish I had more stomach space to try more stuff

God, I love this place so much. It’s the best Korean food I’ve tried so far in Oakland. From the condiments to the food, it has never disappointed me. I’ve gotten seafood pancake before, soft tofu soup, and spicy beef soup. I’ve come here about 5 times already and I love taking people who are visiting me here. I did try the bibimbap before and it wasn’t my fav but the rest of the stuff I’ve gotten here has seriously been so yummy, tasteful and comforting. Amazing food, generous portions, cute music and a simple restaurant ambience. I love it and will keep coming back!! ☺️

We stopped in for dinner and enjoyed the food. We got the chicken katsu and the beef short rib soup. Both were really tasty. The chicken was really tender and the short ribs fell right off the bone. Good flavors.

The Best Place in the Known Universe.

This is a truly special place. The owner Palden is a beautiful soul passionate about making good, healthy food. We were blown away by the food. We ate so much but somehow left feeling energized because the food was just that healthy and good for you. I cannot recommend this place enough. I would truly eat here everyday if given the opportunity. The no bake, vegan key lime pie is literally worth selling your first born child over. It’s that good.

This is the food I will eat in heaven.

The restaurant owner and staff are polite and friendly. The way you order food here is picking the food portion and the ingredients that you'd like to have from the white board near the cashier.
The food is clean and full of good vitamins. They also make their own desserts. The chocolate cookie, chocolate pie, key lime pie are highly recommended. Additionally, the ambiance is peaceful.

I went to dinner here for an event and the food was fantastic! Portions were very good, and it was nice to have some good vegan desserts as well. I also appreciated that the food was seasoned well and not over-salted. I also had a really nice glass of vegan wine, and the whole meal went together very well. Additionally, the team members at the restaurant were great hosts for the event. Though I don’t live that in the neighborhood, I would definitely journey over from San Francisco for another meal.

What a treat of a restaurant! It serves incredibly healthy and delicious dishes that always leave me feeling great. The staff are some of the kindest people you’ll meet, and the peaceful background music makes the whole experience even more relaxing. I love coming here solo with a favorite book or meeting friends who appreciate a unique and special culinary offering. It’s truly a gem for anyone who enjoys thoughtful, flavorful vegan food.

Just went to Peace for the first time, right as they were closing for the evening. No worry, the owner was super nice and happy to prepare a takeout order. The food is ordered in a prie fixe menu style where you choose a size (small, medium, large) and then pick among a few options of things you’d like. I got the large to share two ways, which included a lentil soup, salad, cooked squash and other root vegetables, leafy greens, rice, and adzuki beans…honestly a great amount of food for $21. I also got a side of momo ($9 for 6), which were delicious. It was all very good! Having the feel of a healthy, home-cooked meal, not too heavy, and offering a nice complement to restaurants that go heavy on flavor but probably aren’t the best for you if eaten too often. All the food is vegan and organic, with a Tibetan emphasis. I’m not vegan, but there was really nothing unusual among the menu items that I wouldn’t normally be very happy to eat. The ambiance inside is beautiful, so I’d definitely like to come back sometime and have dinner in person.

google.description: Take-out spot whipping up gourmet, locally sourced Indian dishes with many vegetarian options.

top_reviews.content: Great food, lovely owners. The veggie platter was a great value for the price and everything was super flavorful and delicious. We walked in and ordered, the food came out in about 10 minutes. This is the only Indian takeout spot I need to go to now :)

Munch India operates with quiet rigor from a compact storefront just off Shattuck. There is no dining room, only a kitchen. The entire floor plan is devoted to the hotline and prep station. There is no freezer, only refrigeration. Ingredients are purchased daily, mostly from Berkeley Bowl a few blocks away. Orders are placed online each morning before noon; cooking begins after.

The daily walk-in menu is limited, changes daily, and is prepared to order. The results are consistently superb. Spicing is precise, textures are balanced, and the dishes—drawn from across India—reflect deep training and care. The chefs, Diana Afroza and Nick Ahmed, have cooked professionally since the early 1990s, with backgrounds in Boston, Europe, and India.

Prices are extremely reasonable given the quality and labor involved. They are searching for a larger, dine-in location. If they find one, their costs—and likely their prices—will rise. For now, this is high-level regional Indian cooking, offered at below-market prices. It smells wonderful inside and the people you’ll meet are awesome. Order while you can.

THE BEST! delicious, sophisticated Indian food with burst of flavors in every bite. This is my one and only go to spot in the east bay. The owners are kind and genuine people who knows how to cook with high quality foods! They are super conscious of the ingredients used making it a truly authentic experience everything i order. My taste buds thank you munch india!

finally went here for a picnic with some friends last weekend and it was such a good time. the grilled cheese was perfect, super crispy and melty, exactly what i wanted. we grabbed a spot on the lawn nearby and just hung out for like two hours cause the food held up well. i honestly dont even remember what my friend ordered but she kept saying how good her sandwich was too. the vibe was just really chill and easy, not pretentious at all. im already planning to go back next time im in the area.

Thoroughly mediocre chicken shop/specialty grocer.

Stopped in for 1/2 rotisserie chicken box. Found they had a decent selection of sodas, non-alc bevs, wines, prepared sausages, specialty goods. May stop back in for these other things.

The half chicken, at almost $20, came packed in the box atop chicken schmaltz roasted potatoes. It was paired with hot olives and roasted garlic. An assortment of sauces (aioli some kind of green sauce and some kind of red sauce) were provided.

The chicken was aggressively seasoned and moist. Unfortunately none of the flavor had penetrated the skin which meant that if the piece was without skin, you’re left with the bland flesh. The sauces were all meh. Potatoes, perfect. Olives, nicely varied. My guess is that the bird could have been cooked a little longer and seasoned a little further in advance. (And also checked for feathers.)

I also had a slice of the key lime pie. The beauty of key lime pie is the sharp acidity of these limes (which are in season right now) and the intense floral profile of the oils in the rind. This pie was all oil and not sharp at all. Which is a shame because otherwise, it was great. Not cloyingly sweet, not too much cream on the palate. Oh well.

Hands down the best rotisserie chicken I ever had! The potatoes are cooked with chicken schmaltz and very addicting. They have so many other amazing selections from handmade sausages to their daily sandwiches. I always highly recommend this place to all of my family and friends and now I’m telling you to go and try it out, you won’t be disappointed!

top_reviews.content: I was up on the North side boppin around with a group of Jamaican Astro Physicists showing them what a typical Berkeley hipster dofus looks like, and I'll tell you they were not impressed!  This group of intellects even snubbed their noses at the freelanders at the people's park, and our walk up Telegraph Ave didn't even raise an eyebrow..they told me the people in Berkeley don't know how to be layed back, and cool like an island breeze.  We settled in at Bongo Burgers up in Northside because they liked the name, it seams the group also has a band back on the island that is made up mostly bongo drums and steel drums!  Everybody in the group had an amazing lunch and as soon as they were finished, the leader, Bogart passed out Ganja..(weed) to everyone, and the had a group high out on the sidewalk!  I had the chicken sando and rings...it was amazing! 5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s

Bongo Burger in Berkeley is hands down one of my favorite spots! The food is always amazing and consistently delicious every single time. The Persian Burger is by far the BEST burger on the menu — packed with flavor and absolutely unforgettable.

The owner is also incredibly kind and welcoming, which makes the experience even better. Anyone visiting or living in Berkeley needs to stop by and try this place. Highly recommend!

Really enjoyed Bongo Burger! The Persian burger was delicious—great flavor and cooked really well. The fries were crispy and tasty, and the kabob wraps were also really good. Solid spot if you’re craving burgers or Persian-style comfort food. Will definitely be back!

Bongo Burger is still the best burger in the Bay.

What makes it so good is the style. It’s not a massive, overloaded burger… it’s light (but filling), balanced, and somehow they manage to make a thin patty that’s still cooked medium-rare, juicy, and perfectly pink in the center. That’s surprisingly hard to find.

The grilled onions have are so good on the burger, really make it a signature. Add fresh chopped lettuce, ripe tomato, and the classic Bongo Burger bun, and it’s just a perfect combo. Also the use of two different color cheeses really makes it visually appetizing.

The fries are equally impressive. They’re crispy on the outside but somehow stay soft, fluffy, and full of actual potato on the inside instead of drying out.

The cooks are talented clearly.

On top of all that, the prices are incredibly reasonable, the staff is always friendly, and the vibe feels like old Berkeley in the best possible way.

The Euclid location is my favorite. I grew up eating there in the ‘90s, and I’m amazed that the quality is still just as good today. Places like this are rare. I hope Bongo Burger is around forever.

I decided to try this place after seeing a recommendation. While I always enjoy exploring new burger spots, I have to say that my favorite burger is still In-N-Out, especially when factoring in cost.

I arrived early and was the first customer of the day, which gave me the opportunity to observe how the restaurant prepared their food. One thing that stood out to me—but not in a good way—was how they handled the grilled onions and bacon. Rather than cooking fresh ingredients in the morning, they simply reheated leftover onions and bacon from the previous day and used them for my burger. That was disappointing because I expected everything to be freshly prepared, especially for the first order of the day.

That said, there were some positives. The onion rings were excellent—crispy, and cooked perfectly. I really enjoyed them. The burger itself was just okay. One detail I found odd was the cheese. Instead of a traditional slice of cheese, they sprinkled cheese particles on the patty, which didn’t quite give the same melt-in-your-mouth experience.

As for the drink, the Coke (Pepsi) was fine—nothing to complain about, but nothing remarkable either.

Overall, it wasn’t a bad experience, but I wouldn’t go out of my way to return.

top_reviews.content:
This is a local South Indian restaurant chain with locations across the Bay Area, and this Berkeley location is a smaller one. We stopped by on the weekend for a quick filter coffee and a plate of masala/dal vada.

The vada was a little on the dry side, perhaps because it had been sitting for a while, although thankfully it wasn’t greasy. The filter coffee was pretty standard for the chain, and I especially like to have it with a spoonful of jaggery.

Overall, a quick and decent stop for South Indian coffee and snacks.

Very good place! Good deal on the combo in terms of price, only $11 for a dosa, medhu, and idly, and everything was delicious. The chai was very well balanced and they had jaggery to put in which was good and felt special.

In the south Indian desert that is Oakland it is very refreshing to see a stalwart take root in Berkeley. Everything Idly Express touches is savory gold. If you haven't spent time in Madras this will give you a good simulation - the music, the heavy smell of filter coffee in the air, the coffee itself....it all adds towards the small hustling and bustling vegetarian "hotels" one finds in Madras.

The food is unapologetically spicy and that's good. It keeps the flavors and the textures close the source. The soaked idlis were decadent as were the crunchy vadas. The korma had that sharpness to it and the benne dosa's life force ran all over my palm as I devoured it like a mild-mannered Bakasura at the local village.

The place is small and very functional. It's not date night material unless your date is an adventurous eater whose idea of Indian food is all the stereotypical north indian fare. Then, this place is the beginning of an adventure.

Beware, travel with a bottle of lassi, for the road is spicy ahead.

We've eaten at the restaurant 4-5 times since it's opening. Service is always speedy and the food arrives within 5-10 mins consistently. The staff are friendly  & attentive. Nice to have tasty South Indian food in Berkeley. Our favorites are the ghee podi idly, medhu vadai and masala dosa. The thali is great to share with someone if you aren't too hungry. The curd rice in the thali is creamy and delicious. The chai and filter coffee are must haves!

Bonus tip: The dosa batter in the takeout fridges make crispy golden brown dosas. Highly recommend!

top_reviews.content:
Super fresh banh mi with organic tofu! (4/5 Green Stars)
I wish I had tried this place earlier! I had the banh mi with organic tofu for lunch and the total cost, including tax and a 20% tip was $10.50! I was ravenous and had some concerns that it may not be enough – or come fast enough! However, the lady who took my order prepped the sandwich in as much time as it took me to take a few photos. Also, there was really a lot of tofu in the sandwich – two thick layers of it – so in the end it was pretty darn filling.

There were several memorable things about the sandwich, which I ate without any distraction even though I would normally read while eating. The bread was at a perfect state of crispiness – like a proper French roll – very light and also lightly toasted. The crunchy veggies – the daikon in particular, added a freshness to it that counterbalanced the umami of soy and tofu. I’ve only had a couple of banh mi sandwiches in my time but this one was not only the best so far but has also set a pretty high bar to measure others against.

I’m giving the Sidewalk Street Food 4/5 Green Stars for social and environmental impact. It’s a woman-owned and run business that offers affordable food in a fairly unaffordable neighborhood. Every dish option – banh mi, salad bowl, pho, and spring rolls all had a tofu option. Some of the other options – chicken and pork – are among the more sustainable choices for meat eaters. However, beef and shrimp are among the worst options Sidewalk loses a star for that. My sandwich was pretty much zero-waste in that it was wrapped in a sheet of paper and delivered in a reusable basket.

They’re wonderfully light and have that perfect egg-to-mayo ratio that I’ve missed since returning from Tokyo. Apparently Khánh brought together the influence of having lived in Japan to this setup and it’s such a refreshing take on grab-and-go eateries. My Meatless Mike had TWO meatballs in the entire sandwich (one in each half). Another sandwich had 3 pieces of salami total. It is absurd to pay $15 for what is mostly bread and sauce. I’m beyond disappointed and won’t be back sadly.

I love sandwiches and Ikes always hits the spot! Service was spot on and server provided great guidance as to which sandwich would fit me best. I gotta say the price is a little high for a sandwich/meal, mine came out to 22+(tip).

This now "corporate" chain is a far cry from it's humble beginnings. The portions have been significantly reduced, and I expect more for a $15 sando. I can hit other places for less $ and a better offering.

There are two things/"policies" that don't sit well with me: 1) they have no paper menus to take away. I'm sure the are being environmentally conscientious (they COULD use recycled paper) or they mistakenly assume that EC's older population is tech savvy enough to deal. I see this as a missed opportunity for them, unless they don't feel that is a demographic worth catering to.
2) I paid cash, and did not have any $1 bills to use for the tipping bucket. I asked to change a $5,and was flatly told "we don't give change". Shocked, I begrudgingly dropped a $5 in the bucket.

These may seem like trivial things, but to me seem like a lack of customer focus.

That being said, the staff were polite.

They probably deserve more than a 3, but I'm OK giving this score. I am in no rush to go back.

top_reviews.content:
What a gem! In the courtyard of the Anthropology Museum, you’ll find this charming oasis. Everything from the furniture, landscape, menu, and soundtrack are all thoughtfully procured. Afternoon tea consisted of 3 refreshing flavors of tea and 3 sweet dishes. The chia seed porridge was a generous portion with a delicious flavor profile as well as texture. The toasted hazelnuts added a tasty crunch. Blackberries and gooseberries were a nice palate cleanser, and the chia seed flour brownie bites were addictive! The black walnuts and coarse East Bay salt were a perfect combination! I’m thankful they don’t sell these individually otherwise I would be eating them daily. In bulk.
Not only was the meal unique and delicious, we also learned some Ohlone history and words as well as heard some lovely songs and spoken word that were pre-recorded. It’s such a nice experience and so much more than just food and drinks!

Truly magical find.

In addition to rare local foods, they treated us to games, stories, and song.

It's difficult to find behind the bookstore, but well worth the unique and private experience.

The decor of acorns, nuts, abalone, and cattails was really lovely.

Also, they provide lovely serapes for the chill.

BE HERE

Tucked behind University Press Books is a transformative place that allows you to turn back time. The lovingly gathered and carefully prepared foods are nothing like any foods typically eaten today. Instead, these foods are the mainstay foods that allowed the Ohlone people to live in peace and in harmony with their environment for thousands of years. The two indigenous men who have created this incredible space and menu come from an unbroken line of people who have lived in the East Bay for thousands of years. The foods they are offering take a tremendous amount of time and labor, but they are not offering them in a simple format. The foods are rich and complex and take freshness to an entirely new level. Be prepared to sit outside, dress warmly. Be prepared to learn. There will be abundant information given about each course. Be prepared to ask questions. They want to start conversations that feed your soul as well as your body. Be prepared for adventure. This is an incredible opportunity to explore foods you may not otherwise taste. This is fine dining at its very best.

This place is a MUST. Deliciously fanciful, natural, clean & exquisitely flavorful dishes from our Bay Areas very own indigenous Ohlone tribe. The experience has been well thought out, and you can truly see the intentions that are full of LOVE here. This is as LOCAL and NATIVE as it gets!! Not enough stars for how happy this place makes me & how fulfilling the tastes!!

The great thing about this place is it is done for awareness of ohlone that are still indigenous to the east bay. They have not moved from here ever. Hopefully this place can raise awareness that they are much alive and well as a culture. I was concerned I might not liie some of the food for the snacks and tea on tuesday night but it was delicious and very natural to the nearby land. The experience is great as it is communal at picnic tables, preceeded by prayer, and the food is explained. Very spiritual and tasty. It was an overall great experience. Highly recommended!

top_reviews.content:
Really delicious, flavorful food. We were sad that Standard Fare closed down, but if you liked Standard Fare, a lot of the great things can be found here as well—cute neighborhood spot, seasonal dishes, and of course great biscuits with butter and seasonal jam.

I ordered the shishito grilled peppers quesadillas w/ a very fresh salad, oh it was rich and fresh. Served with a green salsa on the side. You can tell it was homemade, no store bought products there.
My party all ordered the chilaquiles verdes with beans and and salad.  They spécialisé in high quality corn (masa) to make their homemade tortillas.  You can taste the freshness !!! If there is a line, don’t worry it worry, it moves quickly
Oh, their Salsa Macha is not to be missed
You have to purchase a jar of that.. the best !

The vibe here is summer lovin. High tables, low seats, cement steps. Bring a book and spend some time. The menu is tight and they may run out of items but the two dishes we shared - frittata and carrot masa - were fantastic. The agua fresca was taaasty. I saw a few baked goods on site but there are also two other bakeries to hit after.

Beautiful space with fast counter service and indoor and outdoor seating. We got the strawberry and preserved lemon aqua fresca and a coffee which were both wonderful. We wanted to try a lot so got 4 dishes (carrot tamal, frittata, tostada, quesadilla) and each came with beautiful greens and were so delicious. Incredible masa and such fresh produce. Wish we lived closer and could come all the time - it's well worth a trip from anywhere in the bay, come hungry. 🙌🏻

I was disappointed to find that the only vegan options were simply vegetarian dishes with the cheese removed. A quesadilla without cheese? No thanks. It's frustrating to lose a key component of a meal while still paying full price.

Things became more disappointing when I asked for a side of hot sauce or salsa and was told I'd have to purchase an entire bottle instead. Considering the relatively high prices and modest portion sizes, it seemed unreasonable that a small side of salsa or hot sauce wasn't available. The food itself was fresh and well prepared, but it lacked flavor and felt dry without any sauce or cheese.

The final straw came as we were leaving. After finishing our meal, we were scolded for not bussing our own table. It wasn't obvious that customers were expected to do this, and the interaction felt awkward and unnecessary. It also felt strange that no one checked on us during the meal or refilled our water, yet someone was quick to point out that we hadn't cleared our table.

The table next to us also appeared to have a frustrating experience. The cashier missed part of their order, and when they brought it to the staff's attention, the missing item wasn't prioritized. They ended up waiting long after everyone else at their table had finished eating. When they asked if the order could be expedited, they were essentially told no.

I would have gladly paid the higher prices for better service, more thoughtful vegan options, and a dining experience that didn't feel like I was being nickel-and-dimed at every turn. I really wanted to love this place, but unfortunately I won't be back.

We have been there couple times since it opened.
I really like Teishoku (Japanese set meal) in general but I always had hard time to find an authentic Teishoku place around East Bay.

Demiya not only has very authentic Teishoku (I order Karaage) but Japanese curry.
I have also tried Omurice which is also very delicious and great portion.

The other reason I really like Demiya is that their dishes have a lot of details that you probably will not pay attention to but that’s the things make their dishes really close to authentic Japanese Yoshoku. (The salad, pickle, meat, and rice also how those were sorted…) It’s hard to run small business this day especially after pandemic. top_reviews.content:
The most disorganized “The Melt” experience I’ve ever had.

First, I ordered a burger with a double gluten-free bun, but when the burger arrived at the table, it wasn’t gluten-free. I didn’t realize until after I took a bite. Fortunately, I always carry medication with me for my allergies and intolerances.

I ordered a second burger to give them another chance, and the one that arrived was a single, even though I was paying for a double.

I honestly don’t understand what’s going on here. They want to operate like a restaurant, but they can’t even match the level of organization you’d expect from a fast-food chain. The way this team operates is a complete DISASTER.

⭐️ 1 star (and that’s being generous)

I came to The Melt in Berkeley to eat. I ordered the garlic fries with parmesan, and honestly, it’s one of the most disgusting things I’ve ever tasted 🤢.
The fries were cold, maybe because they didn’t bring them on time or because they just dumped them in oil with chopped garlic and chili trying to fake a “chimichurri” or something. The cardboard tray had a literal oil puddle at the bottom. Total mess.

Then I ordered the tomato soup, which turned out to be the most orange and sugary “tomato soup” I’ve ever seen. Honestly, I doubt it was even made from tomatoes. The croutons were just as disgusting.
⚠️ Don’t order this unless your taste buds are dead.

Next came the Bacon Barbecue Double Burger. To be fair, the burger was tasty 🍔.
But it took forever. When it finally came, an older lady brought it—very kind, unlike the younger girl working there, who has zero empathy, no motivation, and probably some racial bias issues.
I asked if the burger was hot, she looked confused, said it was left aside and they’d make a new one. Three minutes later it was back on my table. Yeah right—they didn’t make a new one, they just reheated it. Inside was hot, bun was cold.

I had also asked for a side of pickles, and they just threw half a cold pickle on the tray paper. No care at all.
The place looks fine, but it’s empty—and now I know why 😑.
Checked Google Maps while eating and saw it has 2.8 stars, which honestly feels too generous.

About the beer 🍺:
•	The Pilsner is terrible.
•	The Mexican lager Agua Santa is decent, not amazing, but way better than the Pilsner.

💬 Bottom line: I do not recommend this place at all.
Bad food, bad service, and overpriced for what you get.
Save your money and go somewhere else.

PS: Kerry is the only valuable asset there.

top_reviews.content: Best skewers I've had at a KTV restaurant in the US. Try the chicken skin and gizzards. The staff is super nice. Grand and vibey 2-story venue.

Solid place for dinner, good value for money and the vibe with the music felt relaxed but lively. The grilled fish was the favorite: skin a bit crispy, meat soft with no weird smell, and the veggies under it soaked up all the sauce, worked so well over rice. Also tried the frog, really tender and kind of slips off the bone, nicely seasoned. Tables looked tidy, floor clean, and the staff were friendly without hovering. Easy parking in the mall, and the dishes actually look pretty instagrammable on the table, tbh.

Nice place for a casual dinner. Inside Pacific East Mall so parking was easy, no stress at all. Staff were friendly in a low‑key way, checked on us without hovering. The cold dish was the star for me: really refreshing, a bit sour and spicy, great sauce, and the leftovers mixed into noodles at home worked surprisingly well haha. Tables and utensils looked clean and hygienic, and the music vibe plus the lights made it pretty instagrammable tbh. Prices felt fair for what we got.

Grabbed a late dinner at MT Music Restaurant after wandering around the mall, and the first thing I noticed was how tidy everything felt, like tables actually wiped properly and no sticky menus. Open kitchen area looked organized, no weird smells, which matters to me with catering places. Staff kept coming around quietly picking up plates and trash, not in your face, just doing it. Music was a bit louder than I usually go for, but it matched the whole vibe with people chatting. My phone kept losing signal inside, which was mildly annoying, but food and space felt clean and hygienic overall.

They need to only sing when they have customers or a full restaurant and not sing just when they want to get attention or more people

top_reviews.content: The freshness, the flavor! All their noodles are hand made in house and they have the best texture: perfectly chewy and bouncy. You can taste a kaleidoscope of herbs in their broth. Im impressed by how well they execute a variety of dishes. And they have options for gluten free and vegetarian folks! I can’t wait to come back, though I suspect this place won’t stay under the radar for long.

Damn what good food! We got three noodle dishes, the mok paa and some Lao sausage, all were very impressive. The noodles in the chicken soup were the chewiest rice noodles I've ever had, the clear broth was simple but just right.

The boat noodles were a great contrast, rich warm broth with chunks of pork and meatballs, very hearty.

Everyone loved their dishes, and it seemed like there was no weak link in the meal, which is a rare thing for a restaurant this new. We are definitely coming back. And it's a good price!

Vibrantly-colored, high-ceilinged Thai/Lao counter serve eatery located in Downtown Oakland — urban, young, and casually hip.

Taste well-reflects the upper Mekong Basin palette, down to black-dressing in Green Papaya Salad. Khao Soy Lao Noodle Soup is deep in flavor, but the broth not quite as unctuous as one would hope.

$10 Rice Plates (with choice of basil sauced protein) makes for a rare-find affordable lunch.

Happy to see more Laotian Thai food pop up around the neighborhood. No frills, good food. You order at the counter and bus yourself after your meal. Souk savanh’s food has that home cooking flavor at affordable prices, with lunch deals at $10. I decided to give their boat noodles a try which was absolutely delicious and reminded me of a more fragrant pho, served with a side of pork rinds. Will definitely be back!

I've been looking for a good Thai place in downtown Oakland since Gai Noi unfortunately closed because of the fire in their building a few months ago. I think we have a winner.

It's mind blowing that their rice plates are $10 in this economy. Easily the best deal in the town. Basil chicken was excellent with good heat (I asked for medium spice, which is just above mild). Pad see ew was great as well, with a good mix of noodles, egg, and chicken. I see they have garlic chicken and ribs on their menu, so I will definitely come back for those.

I know it's just the soft opening, but I was able to sample their Lu rou fan (滷肉飯), their Kimchi Fried Rice, and their Chicken Croffle.

My favorite is the Lu Rou Fan, which is a Taiwanese comfort food consisting of braised, chopped pork belly served over rice.  It's savory/sweet pork matches perfectly with the rice and is hearty and filling and reminds me of home.

The Kimchi Fried Rice is also excellent and provides a bold spicy flavor that I think many will enjoy.  Both of these options are great rice dishes that have strong personalities.

The Chicken Croffle is also a great addition with the southern inspired contemporary signature dish that blends sweet and savory.  You can enjoy the chicken and the croffle seperately or stacked together, you can't go wrong.

I haven't tried the drinks yet, but I will definately be back to try them.

The most upsetting part of our visit was what happened to my son. He ate two small pieces of lengua from his tacos, and it was so spicy that it burned his tongue. He began to choke and started crying, which was a frightening experience for my family.

When we explained what happened and shared our concerns, the staff refused to offer a refund or make any effort to resolve the situation. Instead of listening or trying to make things right, they dismissed our concerns, which was extremely disappointing.

The burritos were also a huge letdown. They were overpriced and contained very little meat, with most of the filling consisting of rice and beans, making them unsatisfying and not worth the price.

Overall, between the high prices, disappointing food, poor customer service, and the frightening experience my son had, this was one of the worst taco truck experiences I've ever had. I won't be coming back, and I can't recommend this place to anyone.

top_reviews.content: I must say I had high hopes for this new restaurant. I've been in this neighborhood for 50 years and loved Uzen. Well, I love Japanese food in general and was excited to try a new place. However, I was quite disappointed in Gamsa's nigiri. THEY DRENCH EACH NIGIRI WITH SOY SAUCE!!!!!!! You don't taste the fish. You just taste SALT!!! Ikura is usually a rich orange color. Because they use soy sauce after making each nigiri, their ikura is BROWN!! I kid you not! ALL their sushi was way too salty, even the barracuda when I asked them to make it without soy sauce. They claim the fish is salty. I consider myself a sushi connoisseur  and I have NEVER tasted salty fish in sushi. To be fair, the chiwanmushi was good (although salty also!) The rainbow roll  was NOT drenched in soy sauce, but the crab inside tasted salty. They only serve full bottles of sake, not glasses. (maybe later?) The service was great, as well as the atmosphere. Very cozy and comfortable. I will give it a second chance and order the sashimi salad, chicken karaagi, and udon and see if they are salty. If so, I'm never going back!

This omakase experience was hands down the best I’ve ever had! The fresh fish from Japan, paired with a chef’s expert touch, created a perfect taste. Every dish was amazing, from the very first bite to the last. We also enjoyed the mentaiko pasta, chawanmushi, and hamachi carpaccio, and they were all delicious. Chef Dahan, thank you for the amazing food and experience. We’re definitely coming back again and again!
We went tonight and lived the rolls, nigiri, poke, tempura, yuzu cheesecake, and green tea ice cream! Highly recommend. Calm atmosphere and delicious food.

Amazing new sushi spot! They offer an incredible selection of rare sashimi and nigiri that you won't find at your average sushi restaurant. Their omakase is priced reasonably and delivered great dining experience. Highly recommend!

We’ve been lucky enough to have Chef Da Han come to our home for omakase several times, and he never disappoints!

We just dined at his new restaurant for their soft opening, and the food was absolutely amazing. My daughter especially loved the mentaiko pasta, while we enjoyed the omakase.

Hands down, one of the best omakase deals in town! Under $100 per person is an absolute steal for the quality and freshness of the fish served. You can really tell how much care and passion Chef Da Han puts into every dish.

We’re so happy he finally has his own restaurant. He truly deserves it, and we can’t wait to come back!

top_reviews.content: Just stopped in when looking for a fast meal. Reasonable prices, amazing food, and great service.
First time coming by here great experience, good food, large portions, and very reasonable price prices my girlfriend’s favorite was the garlic noodles and shrimp. Definitely recommend.

This is officially my new favorite restaurant! The service was fast and friendly, and the food was amazing.

I’m used to Mongolian beef being either too soft or way too chewy, but this was cooked perfectly. The shrimp garlic noodles were also so good, you could really taste the garlic, I love garlic!

We ordered the green beans, which came out first, and they were so good that we completely forgot to take a photo before eating them! The crab rangoons were delicious too, and I loved the presentation of everything we ordered.

We also had the chance to talk to one of the owners, Jenny. She was incredibly kind, and we made sure to let her know how much we enjoyed the food.

I’m definitely coming back. This place is a new favorite!
Great quality and portion, delicious food, kind staff.

Really liked this place. The food is reasonably priced and you can tell they put a lot of care into it.

I got the grass fed beef steak and really liked it. The beef tasted fresh and was cooked just right, and the sauce went really well with it. The orange chicken was crispy and juicy and probably my favorite. The garlic noodles were also really good. They had a rich cheesy and garlicky flavor, and I really liked the crispy garlic.

I also liked the space a lot. The interior is nicely designed and everything feels clean, comfortable, and well thought out.

Overall, really good food for the price and a nice place to eat. Would come back.

top_reviews.content: Finally Khao soy Lao soup in Albany over in the old matchpoint brewing space. large portions and good prices, $10 rice plates all day is unheard of these days, they're really doing the neighborhood a service by offering fresh affordable food.

I am SO happy souk savanh is back! My sisters and I used to go to their original location back in Oakland on E. 14 many years ago.

We are so happy they have opened up again in Albany. We still live in Oakland but it’s definitely worth the drive to Albany for their delicious Lao and Thai food.

We stopped by yesterday on a Saturday right at opening. I got the kasoy noodle soup and my sister got the boat noodle soup and we also shared a Lao papaya salad.

Everything was great, really good flavors. Their menu also has a variety of rice plates, stir fries, noodle soups, stir fried noodles, combo plates, etc.

Can’t wait to come back soon to try more things. There is plenty of free street parking and a good amount of tables inside the restaurant. I would recommend to anyone looking for some tasty Lao and Thai cuisine.
